It took 1st Runner-up Grand Prize in the High School section and won Best Village Project, and the reason is visible on every page: the wiki's standing rule is that every number carries its conditions and a source, and the team separates demonstrated results from deployment claims more rigorously than most university teams.

**frameworks.** The headline model is a calibration-and-inverse-prediction framework rather than a mechanistic simulation, and it is unusually well executed. Image signals were defined explicitly before any fitting: colour response C = 1 - (G_pellet / G_white) from green-channel intensity measured in ImageJ on pellets photographed against a white tile, and fluorescence response F = R_pellet / R_background from red-channel intensity inside a light box, with the matched untreated control from the same run and timepoint subtracted (delta-C, delta-F) and no OD normalisation. They then fitted a log-linear model delta-S = A + b log10(c / 0.005 uM) with 0.005 uM chosen as the reference so A is directly interpretable, giving delta-C = 0.04363 + 0.07591 log10(c/0.005) and delta-F = 0.42290 + 1.08721 log10(c/0.005). Crucially, calibration and validation data were separated up front - 20 calibration measurements from four runs (2, 6, 8 and 13 October) and 10 held-out validation measurements from two further runs (14 and 15 October) for each readout, all at the four-hour timepoint across 0.005, 0.01, 0.03, 0.05 and 0.1 uM. The model was inverted to estimate unknown concentration, c-hat = 0.005 uM x 10^((delta-S - A)/b), and scored by RMSE on the held-out runs: approximately 0.0483 uM for colour and 0.0319 uM for fluorescence, with all numerical predictions included so that failures were not hidden (a 0.1 uM sample on 15 October was estimated at 0.246 uM by colour). On the hardware side they ran CAD-based dry-lab studies for a UV advanced-oxidation-process reactor, modelling fluid flow dynamics, UV photo-oxidation kinetics and lamp exposure times for both a batch quartz-tube reactor and a thin-layer millifluidic cassette, computing a residence time of 192.6 s and a modelled minimum-to-maximum light ratio of 92.2% across the 1 mm layer; the filter assembly was developed parametrically in OpenSCAD. Promoter selection also used in silico promoter-strength analysis, which predicted J23106 to be comparable to P429 and so added it as a comparison design.

**datascience.** The analysis is notable for publishing its own limitations as a work plan. They state that the pooled model does not separately estimate run-to-run variation, that the reported concentrations are point estimates with no uncertainty intervals, that no detection or quantification limit has been established, and that rounded signal values were used as fitting inputs. They then specify the fixes concretely: a random-intercept mixed model delta-S_ri = A + b log10(c_ri/0.005) + u_r + e_ri with run-specific slopes only if the data support them and with convergence and singularity checks; inverse-calibration intervals that distinguish prediction for a new run from prediction for a run containing a measured reference standard; a per-run intercept correction A_r = delta-S_standard,r - b log10(c_standard/0.005) estimated from a known standard run alongside every experiment; leave-one-run-out cross-validation over six folds with the warning that selecting and evaluating on the same cross-validation results produces optimistic estimates; and comparison of the local log-linear fit against a four-parameter logistic model if data across 0.001-5 uM becomes available. They also ran and reported an exploratory sensitivity check swapping calibration runs, and honestly noted that because the validation runs were examined during that comparison they no longer constitute a completely untouched final assessment. Results-page statistics use two-sided paired t-tests across five independent paired runs with explicit notice that p-values are unadjusted for the three readouts. Hardware performance was quantified the same way: automated water delivery gave a coefficient of variation of 1.95% against 7.41% across 10 manual syringe runs, drainage retained volumes of 0.28, 0.31 and 0.30 mL (mean ~0.30 mL, about 95% liquid recovery), and reducing tubing bore from 7 mm to 1 mm over a 10 cm segment was computed to cut geometric dead volume accordingly.

**dataviz.** Presentation is built around separating what was measured from what is assumed. Charts show individual run points alongside coloured means and error bars rather than only pooled summaries, the model page plots known versus estimated concentration against a dashed perfect-prediction line with out-of-calibration-range estimates marked separately, and tables consistently split 'experimental finding' from 'design goal' and 'prototype performance' from 'deployment claim'. Every figure caption states its conditions. The hardware readout itself is a data-visualisation artefact: Detection Unit V3.0 pairs a Hamamatsu C12880 miniature spectrometer (288-pixel detector, 340-850 nm, 12 nm typical FWHM) with two ESP32-S3-N16R8 microcontrollers driving a local TFT display and a Wi-Fi-connected web interface that shows the recorded spectrum and the raw signal at a user-selected target wavelength, with online data logging, registered devices, selected-wavelength trends and recorded runs reviewable on a phone or computer. A red/amber/green status display was added later, and the team deliberately separated device status, fluorescence reading, concentration estimate and safety judgement on screen so that a green operational light cannot be misread as 'this sample is safe'.

**software.** Open hardware and firmware rather than a bioinformatics tool. The Detection Unit CAD is published in Onshape (https://cad.onshape.com/documents/2228cb45d05bdbc67479791d) and the firmware and software at https://github.com/hkjssplkchc2026/mercurysense, containing ESP32 firmware, the C12880 spectrometer driver, acquisition instructions and Python/web monitoring software, with a live monitoring web app for reviewing spectra and runs. The Extraction Unit code is at https://github.com/davidlueng986-alt/MerMAID-Extraction-Unit. An itemised bill of materials is published with a ~USD 357 core-component subtotal (LED 2x 560 nm at USD 2.60, etc.), and the team states plainly that this overshot the USD 40 affordability target stakeholders had asked for. The detection unit went through four versions (AS7343 14-channel spectral sensor in a laser-cut acrylic box, to an opaque 3D-printed enclosure with recessed lid and adjustable optical mounts, to the C12880 spectrometer with interchangeable filters, fluid handling and web interface) and the extraction platform through three, with state-machine control sequences published for the water, soil and UV-AOP modules together with error-handling tests covering pump timeouts, watchdog recovery, soil-mass checks, stirring feedback, reagent availability and weighing faults. An educational browser game, 'Small Signal: a MerMAID field school', is published as a 3-5 minute pixel-art laboratory game in which players build a biological signal path, compare an unknown sample with its controls, and decide what the evidence supports - and is labelled a beta prototype whose educational effectiveness has not yet been evaluated. Repository: https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/hongkong-jss.

**ihp.** Human Practices ran on a stated operating principle - respond promptly to stakeholder feedback, and let it drive the next hardware revision - structured across four stages and a five-question cycle (Inspiration, Intercommunication, Investigation, Implementation, Impact) with the rule that each engagement must end in either a documented change or a documented reason for no change. There is also a five-tier Target User Prioritisation Pyramid which they explicitly label a working framework rather than a validated exposure ranking, and which puts underserved communities near suspected contamination sources such as informal e-waste processing sites above farmers, researchers, regulators and the general public. The traceable changes: the Drainage Services Department's guidance moved them off the chromoproteins used in earlier projects onto mRFP1e as a dual readout - visible colour for non-specialists plus a more sensitive fluorescence channel for quantification - and DSD, the Water Supplies Department and university researchers together pushed them to test lower concentrations, benchmark against international reference values, and assess cross-response to interfering heavy metals (hence the Cd2+/Pb2+/Zn2+ selectivity panel). Koo's Farm and local wet market vendors demanded numerical readings instead of qualitative colour indicators, which is the direct reason the AS7343 14-channel sensor was replaced by the wavelength-resolved Hamamatsu C12880 and why a numerical display and web readout exist. University professors said soil particulates must be removed before optical measurement and recommended a modular design, which produced the separate water, soil and planned organic-mercury extraction modules. Users reported excessive syringe force on the V1 filter stack (2 um pre-filter plus 0.45 um membrane), so manual syringe delivery was replaced by pump-driven dosing - measured as an improvement from 7.41% to 1.95% coefficient of variation. On-site trials at Blue Girl Organic Farm and Yeung Marine Products Limited with agricultural soil extracts, irrigation water and fish pond water (run without GM bacteria, since they could not legally be taken out of the lab) produced requests for clearer indicators and better protection against water and mud, answered with a red/amber/green status display, a reinforced housing, and maintenance access and modularity designed into the proposed V4.0. A second public survey combining street interviews with hands-on demonstrations for 195 people found 87.7% more confident that ordinary people could participate in checking soil and water safety and 84.1% finding the digital readout easy to understand - and the team immediately noted that perceived confidence and readability do not establish analytical accuracy, and separated device status from safety judgement in the interface as a direct result. More Happy Farm said plainly that not every farmer wants to own a device, which pushed them towards a service model. Throughout, they keep stating what their evidence does not cover: a response in a controlled biological assay does not establish accurate measurement in soil extracts, reliable operation of the complete device, or suitability for regulatory decisions.

**publicEngagement.** Nine targeted outreach events reaching over 2,400 participants, organised as an explicit four-tier framework. Tier 1 (primary students and parents, over 1,600 people) ran interactive Open Day and Information Day booths at Y.W.C.A. Hioe Tjo Yoeng College and Po Leung Kuk Celine Ho Yam Tong College with strawberry DNA extraction and live gel electrophoresis demonstrations. Tier 2 (over 730 secondary peers) covered Microbiology 101 for Grade 10 students on microbe handling, laboratory safety, cleanliness and contamination prevention, and a morning assembly for 700 Grade 7-12 students that framed synthetic biology through agricultural mercury contamination and explained how cellular components can be repurposed as logic gates and biosensors. Tier 3 is the most durable: a two-day Teacher Biotech Training Workshop for 30 local school teachers covering PCR and agarose gel electrophoresis, combined with a standing loan programme letting those teachers borrow DNA samples and laboratory equipment from the team - a deliberate attempt to leave teaching capacity behind after the competition ends. Tier 4 took the work into public and civic space: an exhibitor stand at InnoEX 2026, the international innovation and technology exhibition in Hong Kong, and a presentation alongside the Drainage Services Department at its Annual Media Briefing, which put the project on an official government webpage and into local news. They also ran a street interview with 30 members of the public specifically about a 'mercury-free' produce certification label, finding unanimous support for the idea, 14 people rating it very important for public health, 12 supporting it even at higher vegetable prices, 22 willing to buy certified produce at normal prices and 4 willing to pay extra - while also recording that 19 respondents remained somewhat or very worried about engineered bacteria leaking from the sealed device against only 8 who were not, a finding they published rather than buried. The browser game 'Small Signal' extends this by teaching the reasoning - compare the unknown against its controls, then decide what the evidence can support.

**realWorld.** The commercial concept is Certification-as-a-Service rather than instrument sales: farmers pay an annual subscription, the team visits to test soil on site with MerMAID, passing farms receive a 'Heavy Metal-Free' certificate and logo for supermarket packaging that lets them command a premium, and random surprise re-tests throughout the year (affordable precisely because the test is cheap and fast) guard the certificate's integrity. The plan is backed by a SWOT matrix, a competitor comparison against off-site laboratory testing (HKD 500+ per test, weeks of turnaround) and quick chemical test strips, and a five-step business plan naming AFCD, the Hong Kong Organic Resource Centre and premium supermarkets as the partners whose endorsement would make the certificate a standard. What lifts it above a typical student business plan is the case-study section: they analyse three real commercial analogues - Hygiena's reader-plus-consumables-plus-records model, SGS's accredited food-safety testing service, and Hong Kong's AFCD/VMO Accredited Farm Scheme - and draw out the uncomfortable implications, including that MerR-responsive bioavailable Hg(II) and a reference method's total-mercury result may be different measurands that cannot be assumed to agree just because both are labelled mercury, that a logo on packaging cannot replace a sample-to-report record tied to farm, location, date, sample ID and method scope, and that the full cost per valid result must include consumables, controls, staff time, storage, failed runs and waste handling. They state outright that the USD 350 build cost missed the USD 40 target, that the certification journey is a proposed direction, that the current prototype does not establish that any farm or product is heavy-metal-free, and that they claim no certification authority. Real-world constraints are acknowledged rather than wished away: engineered microbes cannot legally be placed in bins or taken into the field in Hong Kong, the on-site demonstrations therefore ran without GM bacteria, and the sub-five-minute loading and readout sequence is distinguished from the five hours of reporter expression the actual assay needs.

**For GEMS:** Adopt their calibration discipline wholesale: split runs into calibration and validation before fitting anything, subtract a control from the same run and timepoint, invert the fit to predict unknowns, report RMSE on the held-out runs with the failures left in, flag out-of-range estimates, and then publish the statistical work you have not done yet (run-aware mixed model, inverse-calibration uncertainty intervals, leave-one-run-out cross-validation, a per-run reference standard) as a named plan. The second lesson is their teacher-capacity play - training 30 local teachers in PCR and gel electrophoresis and lending them the reagents and kit - which multiplies a school team's reach far more cheaply than any one-off workshop.

### UCAS-China — PARCEL
Undergrad · China · https://2026.igem.wiki/ucas-china/
PARCEL is an inhaled mRNA delivery platform built from elastin-like polypeptides (ELPs) rather than lipid nanoparticles. The fusion protein ELP-Pum2-EEP13 uses Pum2 to grab mRNA carrying a PRS tag in its 3' UTR, ELP phase separation to encapsulate and protect it, an endosomal escape peptide to get out of the endosome, and a Sortase A-conjugated anti-UPK1B scFv to target airway club cells; the cargo is mRNA for SLPI (inhibiting neutrophil elastase and the mucus hypersecretion it triggers) plus a lower dose of IFN-lambda-1 (antiviral defence and Th2 suppression). It won 1st Runner-up and Best Integrated Human Practices because the stakeholder work genuinely steered the science: clinicians moved the project from rescue therapy to maintenance therapy, and an asthma mechanism researcher killed one of the two original cargoes outright. The dry lab is unusually complete, modelling the whole chain from E. coli production through nebulizer aerosol deposition to a PK-PD readout in FEV1 and FeNO, with every module feeding the next.

**frameworks.** Six connected modules sharing parameters and declared input-output relationships. (1) Production: a SimBiology ODE model of a quorum-sensing kill switch (LuxI/LuxRm A1 variant, pLuxRm-driven lysis) combining growth-dependent dilution with AHL kinetics, swept across Anderson promoters to find the one that lyses the culture just before ELP phase transition - this chose the promoter the wet lab used. (2) Assembly: AlphaFold 3 predicted the three fusion-protein monomers (1052-1322 residues), coarse-grained into Martini 3 and run in GROMACS for 2-3 microseconds at 298 K, 1 bar, 150 mM NaCl, 50 mg/mL protein, with pLDDT used to justify stabilising the Pum2 fold while leaving ELP flexible; alongside this they built CAPE (Coverage and Assembly Prediction for Protein Ensembles), a reduced free-energy model calibrated against wet-lab data, and used Bayesian optimization over CAPE as the objective to redistribute ELP repeats around Pum2 instead of brute-forcing every combination. (3) Pulmonary delivery: MPPD v3.04 on the adult Yeh-Schum five-lobe geometry screened log-normal aerosol size distributions, flow rates and inhaled volumes against deposition in the last three conducting generations per lobe, then ANSYS Fluent CFD simulated 3D airway transport, feeding a distal airway and airway-surface-liquid transport model and a reference cell-composition mapping that converts deposition into surface contacts per club cell. (4) Intracellular release: a hybrid ODE-stochastic model of one particle per endosome (median 560 nm, ~2,400 fusion chains and therefore 2,400 EEP copies per particle), tracking acidification, ELP disassembly, EEP-mediated membrane opening and RNA degradation to output intact cytosolic RNA over time, with intact RNA tracked separately from fluorescent label. (5) PK-PD: a four-compartment model (bone marrow, blood, airway wall, epithelial lining fluid) with 25 species, 53 assignment rules and 51 reactions, adapted from Gadkar et al.'s severe asthma immune network, giving four clinical readouts - FeNO, FEV1, relative goblet-cell count and 15-minute mucin release - used to compare SLPI:IFN-lambda-1 payload ratios and dosing frequency. (6) Response prediction: an affine mapping baseline plus residual CellFlow (flow matching) trained on public cytokine-perturbation scRNA-seq.

**datascience.** Two concrete pieces. The target screen: using the Human Lung Cell Atlas they compared healthy adult club cells against other lung epithelial cells on fold change, adjusted p-value and detection fraction, and from 68 genes passing the criteria selected UPK1B - 2.28-fold enriched, adjusted p = 0.00559, RNA detected in 45.92% of club cells versus 3.43% of other epithelial cells. They then checked antibody accessibility (Human Surfaceome; UniProt O75841, 260 aa, four transmembrane regions, extracellular stretches at 37-60 and 108-229) and cross-tissue selectivity (archived GTEx: 0.11 TPM lung vs 21.90 TPM bladder; Human Protein Atlas showing membranous expression in urothelium), and stated plainly that UPK1B is not club-cell exclusive so the analysis prioritises an experimental candidate rather than demonstrating selective targeting. The response-prediction benchmark is equally honest: affine mapping cut mean-expression error 7.1% against predicting no change and beat the mean-response baseline, while the nonlinear residual CellFlow model improved some mean-expression predictions but worsened distributional agreement and the selected RNA panels - so they kept affine as the reference model and named cross-donor validation and RNA reconstruction as the open problems. Tasks were set up as donor-held-out rotations on GSE249307 and GSE246368 with unpaired source and target cells.

**dataviz.** The model landing page opens with a scripted animation that walks the whole mechanism in sequence - the E. coli shell fills with protein, lyses, chains assemble into PARCEL, the particle travels into the bronchi, binds a club-cell receptor, is endocytosed, disassembles, releases mRNA, and mucus drops one step per round - with replay and skip controls and a text fallback when JavaScript is off. AlphaFold monomer structures are embedded as interactive viewers with pLDDT and protein-region colouring and cartoon/C-alpha toggles, so a reader can see directly why Pum2 was treated as rigid and ELP as flexible. The wiki also carries font-size controls (A-/Default/A+) for accessibility. On the software side, the AeroEase Android app turns raw device timestamps into an expandable-card Overview with a seven-day activity chart and a date-filtered History, and the FeroEase app plots live temperature, pH and OD600 with a falling-trend detector that flags the harvest window.

**software.** Four software deliverables. AeroEase, an Android companion app for the nebulizer, syncs ESP32-C3 button timestamps over BLE through a validated handshake with checksum, session and duplicate checks, clock calibration from the phone, and acknowledgement only after durable storage, then presents them as a locally stored medication-use diary with daily and seven-day counts, date-filtered history, CSV export, and a rule-based offline assistant that answers questions without any cloud call; the team repeatedly states the records document device actions, not delivered dose or confirmed inhalation. FeroEase, written in Flutter, monitors the two-stage fermentation over Wi-Fi with temperature, pH, stirring control and a falling-OD600 trend detector that identifies the lysis harvest window a bench fermenter does not report. The bioinformatics pipeline for club-cell target selection is the third. A browser-based quiz game supports the education activities. Hardware: AeroEase is a portable vibrating-mesh nebulizer on an ESP32-C3 with rechargeable power, session logging, BLE, a gravity-fed reservoir and physically separated liquid and electronics compartments in a modular 3D-printed housing; FeroEase is an ESP32-S3 two-stage culture platform with pH and temperature sensing, controlled heating, motor stirring and transmitted-light OD600 tracking. Build resources and a user manual with source code access are published on the wiki.

**ihp.** The team formalised its own cycle, RCSF (Reflect-Connect-Share-Feedback), as a deliberate parallel to the DBTL engineering cycle, and ran the project through nine documented iterations with 20 individuals, teams and institutions across six defined communities (academia, medical professionals, industry, supervisors, patients and families, the public), 44 asthma patient representatives and 419 public representatives from under-10s to over-60s. Each community is introduced with who they are, what they know, and why their position matters. The changes are specific and traceable. Doctor Fei Wang's input moved the project from rapid-acting therapy to asthma maintenance treatment, which reset the whole target population. Professor Huaiyong Chen, who studies respiratory disease mechanisms, explained that in asthma many club cells differentiate into mucus-producing goblet cells - supporting the shift away from immune cells to airway epithelium - and told them that NKX2-1, one of their two original cargoes, matters in development but has little effect in adulthood, so it was dropped and SLPI took its place. Professor Pingsheng Liu's survey of liposome, LNP and polymeric carrier limitations fed directly into the ELP carrier rationale and the protein sequence design. Professor Yufei Xia flagged subtle flaws in the experimental design and walked them through the standard in vivo/in vitro validation workflow. Yaozhong Cao, a former iGEMer, argued with them about target specificity, which is upstream of the UPK1B antibody screen. Professor Xiaoru Huang, an ethics of science and technology researcher, reviewed the biosafety and bioethics discipline. They contacted the Huairou District Bureau of Landscaping and Forestry about local pollen and catkin management, grounding the project in Beijing's own regulation (the Measures implementing the Forest Law, effective 1 January 2026) and in observed thunderstorm asthma cases. Patient work was handled with explicit informed consent and privacy statements, and the questionnaire reports its own demographics (21 recovered, 21 currently medicated, 419 unaffected). The team states its guiding principle as 'local people solving local problems', and the HP group's standing job was to track every subteam's bottlenecks and feed external input back into each one.

**publicEngagement.** Education was designed from two findings in their own clinician interviews and 461-person questionnaire: patients stop medication once they feel better, and parents refuse to start it for children out of fear of side effects, so compliance - not just awareness - became the target. Activities are segmented by audience. For children: a booth with biology-themed games at the Huairou District National Science Popularization Month fair (September 2026), doubling as a questionnaire collection point, plus a Life Science Classroom proposal for fifth and sixth graders in Huairou primary schools teaching respiratory tract structure through illustrations and interactive demos, published as a downloadable PDF so other teams can run it. For university students: an iGEM Winter Camp training new members with offline wet-lab tutorials (plasmid extraction, PCR, homologous recombination, protein purification) and online dry-lab and modelling tracks, and an annual Microbial Painting competition open to all majors as a recruitment funnel - which failed to produce the expected colony patterns, and the team published the three reasons why (cell sedimentation from static suspension, insufficient streaking density, IPTG induction of EGFP suppressing growth) and used it to teach participants that negative results are normal and troubleshooting is the skill. For the general public: a Public Science Day stall and a browser quiz game on synthetic biology and iGEM.

**realWorld.** The entrepreneurship work is a self-critical commercial assessment rather than a pitch. The team states outright that PARCEL's case must rest on defined unmet needs rather than technological novelty, and tabulates the strengths as well as the limitations of inhaled corticosteroids, bronchodilators and biologics before positioning PARCEL as a non-hormonal, lower-frequency, modular maintenance option. The SWOT names real weaknesses: delivery efficiency and duration of expression were only shown in HEK293T in vitro, so mucus, mucociliary clearance, local enzymes and immune uptake remain unaddressed; a combined protein-plus-mRNA product multiplies CMC burden across ELP molecular weight, purity, impurity profile and phase-transition behaviour and mRNA sequence integrity and stability, then payload ratio, condensate characteristics, batch consistency and storage; and the team lists the expertise it does not have (toxicology, regulatory affairs, clinical development, IP, market access). Opportunities are equally concrete - the modular Pum2/PRS-tag design means a new payload needs no new carrier, CAS institutes supply the analytical capability they lack, and China's pay-for-performance medical insurance pilot offers a reimbursement pathway for a therapy that can demonstrate efficacy. They commit to re-reviewing the SWOT at each development milestone.

**For GEMS:** Steal the RCSF cycle: UCAS-China gave human practices the same named, repeatable four-step loop (Reflect, Connect, Share, Feedback) that engineering gets with DBTL, mapped every stakeholder into one of six communities with a stated reason for including them, and then showed nine iterations where the loop closed - including dropping a cargo gene because one researcher said it does nothing in adults. A school research centre can run that loop on any project, and the second lesson is just as cheap to copy: publish what failed, as they did with the microbial painting that never grew, and the reasons why.

### Princeton — SymPleco: Making Precision Sequestration Sym-ple
Undergrad · United States · https://2026.igem.wiki/princeton/
SymPleco attacks a trade-off that runs through all remediation chemistry: activated carbon captures a lot but cannot tell similar molecules apart, while monoclonal antibodies bind precisely but need harsh pH or chaotropic salts to release and cannot be recovered or scaled. Princeton's answer is a filamentous M13 bacteriophage used as a programmable adsorbent: sortase A-mediated ligation staples engineered fusion proteins onto the N-terminus of every pVIII copy (making 'furry' phage that bypass classical display size limits), with pIII carrying a Cg-Defensin anchor for PLA filter attachment, a VHH7 nanobody for macrophage clearance, and an AsLOV2 optomonobody that holds cargo in the dark and lets go under 450 nm light. Because swapping the target means swapping only the displayed binder, the team paired it with SymPlify, a de novo binder design pipeline, so a new target does not wait on a new antibody. It won on foundational-advance logic: a genuinely modular chassis demonstrated across three deliberately unrelated applications (melanoma exosome sequestration, Parkinson's alpha-synuclein interception, microcystin/BPA water remediation), backed by an unusually self-critical ODE model and an IRB-approved patient engagement programme.

**frameworks.** Two distinct computational efforts. SymPlify is a de novo protein binder design pipeline that routes a target by type: a protein chain goes to BindCraft (AlphaFold2-multimer hallucination with gradient descent on logits through softmax, SolubleMPNN sequence design, AF2-monomer re-prediction as a deliberately harsh filter, then PyRosetta physical metrics for binding energy and surface hydrophobicity), while a small-molecule or macrocycle chain goes to RFdiffusion3 all-atom diffusion plus LigandMPNN (eight sequences per backbone) and an independent complex-prediction model. PeSTo supplies hotspot residue scoring, RDKit renders structures and finds pharmacophores, and freesasa computes hydrophobic patch fraction. Separately, the measurement work is backed by a mechanistic ODE model of the recursive Phage Jumpstart Assay (jumpstart.py, jumpstart_mechanistic.py, passage.py, phase2.py, recursion.py) tracking naive, infected and free-particle pools with superinfection exclusion (sigma = 0.05), saturating infection, carrying capacity, and a hybrid-coat infectivity a_h derived from real pIII gene dosage (a_h ~0.729 at m13ko7_copies=20); the 1:11 passage step samples each particle pool by Poisson rather than plain division so a lineage can genuinely go extinct.

**datascience.** The Jumpstart assay turned a single colony-ratio readout into a trajectory: because each recursion is both a manipulation and a measurement, repeated rounds on a population being driven toward one genotype reveal behaviour a single ratio cannot. Statistics are handled carefully — intervals bootstrap over wells, leave-one-well-out checks are reported, panels yielding 0-2 Amp colonies out of 165-272 are reported as upper bounds rather than measurements, and a chi-square test (197 on 5 df) establishes that the six Run B constructs are not interchangeable while the team explicitly declines to lean on the ordering because the bottom four are indistinguishable from zero. They also report that three magnitude-based titer estimators disagreed by up to 20,000-fold on the same panel, which is why they built a ratio readout instead. Most notably the model documents its own error history: an initial m13ko7_copies=200 was simply the wrong figure (wild-type M13 rolling-circle copy number rather than M13KO7's actual p15A-driven one), corrected to 10 and then 20 as evidence improved, with the admission that the corrected model is more parameter-sensitive, not less.

**dataviz.** SymPlify's web interface is the visualisation centrepiece: an RDKit 3D viewer colours the target by PeSTo binding probability, lists top hotspot residues with confidence scores, lets the user delete low-scoring ones with an x to tighten the patch, and recomputes the difficulty breakdown (spread, hydrophobic surface fraction, globularity) live as the selection changes — plus a warning when residues sit more than 30 A apart, because one binder cannot reach them all. A run-status page shows pipeline stage, target type, elapsed time, auto-resubmits, design count and job ID, and a final ranking screen lets the user click through designs and download .pdb files with or without GS linkers. The model page is unusually transparent as data presentation: it prints the full command reference, labels every parameter as measured, derived or assumed, and ranks assumptions by their sensitivity on the round-2 plate ratio.

**software.** SymPlify, an integrated de novo binder design pipeline with a web interface, hotspot prediction, cluster job submission with auto-resubmission, and post-design filtering and ranking; released for the wider synthetic biology community and wet-lab tested on the team's own targets. Team repository: https://github.com/dianalluu/puigem2026, with an AlphaFold deployment for the Princeton Della cluster at https://github.com/09aaronl/alphafold_princeton-della. The ODE model ships as a Python package with 52 automated checks in test_model.py (~80 s full run, ~8 s in fast mode) covering mass-balance and neutrality invariants, the hybrid-coat gene-dosage derivation, the Poisson passage statistics and pinned regression values. Hardware: a 3D-printed PLA gyroid biofilter cartridge whose two winning PITCCH designs are published as downloadable source STEP assemblies.

**ihp.** This is the strongest documented chain of design changes of any team here, and several of them cut capability rather than adding it. Dr Bowen Jing's technical advice seeded SymPlify and his steric clash filter was adopted, but the team then cut AlphaFold3 from the pipeline entirely because Dr Martin Pacesa argued it often mispredicts binding sites; Pacesa also supplied PeSTo as the hotspot engine and, after the team ran competing designs to compare, AF2 monomer was implemented on his side of the argument. Dr Reynold Panettieri talked them out of sequestering IL-6 — their original software benchmark target — by pointing out IL-6's dual-sided effects on blood cell production and T-cell regulation, redirecting them toward a niche where cheaper-than-mAb production is the real advantage and toward naming one indication and working from there, which is exactly how the final applications are framed. Dr Douglas Galasko's distinction between biomarkers and toxins moved them off amyloid-beta for Alzheimer's and into the Parkinson's and rabies work. Two multiple myeloma patients, interviewed under Princeton IRB Protocol #20003, independently said the word 'virus' for a bacteriophage was a problem — one noting roughly 80% of myeloma patients are treated in community settings and take their doctor's word — which changed how the team describes the project in all outreach. A former FDA biologics deputy director, Dr Celia Witten, pointed them to CBER's phage therapy work; EPA Office of Pesticide Programs and OPPT staff sent them to the statutes; and marine microbiologist Dr Stephen Giovannoni plus phage ecologist Prof Forest Rohwer turned the Cg-Defensin antimicrobial worry into a specific planned avidity-comparison assay. Dr John Wnek, who conserves Diamondback terrapins, chose their environmental targets: microcystins and BPA, because nearby New Jersey plants discharge effluent half a mile offshore with no process for xenobiotics.

**publicEngagement.** PITCCH, the Princeton iGEM Team CAD Competition for Hardware, is the standout: entrants were given a real open engineering problem from the project — design a 3D-printable gyroid biofilter, 20 mm diameter by 25 mm height, maximising contact surface area — along with the team's actual print parameters. It ran free, fully asynchronous and online in a junior division (grades 5-12) and an open division (18+), explicitly permitted responsible AI use, and drew 42 registered submissions from the United States, United Kingdom and Mexico, of which 26 passed dimensional and printability screening before being sliced and computationally ranked by total surface area. Announcement emails went to thousands more via high school superintendents, undergraduate engineering directors and makerspaces, each carrying a project description and iGEM links. The team frames it as citizen science and backed that framing with credit: two winning designs appear on the wiki with the designers named on the attribution form, and the registration terms stated plainly that the team reserves the right to draw inspiration from submissions with attribution. They also postered at symposiums and presented at bioethics exchanges, and at the US-China iGEM Human Practices Summit showed their halted immunology work as a case study in how to pivot.

**realWorld.** The regulatory path is mapped rather than asserted: phage therapy under FDA CBER for the clinical arms, and statute-level grounding for the environmental arm after meetings with EPA Office of Pesticide Programs and Office of Pollution Prevention and Toxics, with the team careful to state that nothing should be read as EPA guidance. Containment is designed for deployment — the phage stays inside a closed water treatment facility bound to a biodegradable PLA filter so it is retrievable and localised, with macrophage clearance via VHH7 as the biosafety route for therapeutic use. The commercial argument is reconfiguration cost: because capture specificity lives in one genetic part on pVIII, changing target means changing that part and not the media, housing, attachment chemistry or capital cycle, which is the case made against granular activated carbon for PFAS where GAC retains poorly over realistic service lifetimes. Work is mapped to SDG 3.4, 6.3 and 9. Continuation is concrete: further IRB submissions to interview melanoma patients and Parkinson's patients and caregivers, the Rohwer avidity assay, qPCR of M13KO7 copy number to settle the model's most sensitive parameter, and phage hydrogels as an alternative anchor that would remove the Cg-Defensin concern altogether.

**For GEMS:** Copy PITCCH: hand the public a genuine, unsolved sub-problem from your own project with real constraints and real print parameters, judge entries computationally on a single objective metric, then credit the winners by name and actually build their design in. It converts outreach into contributed engineering at almost no cost, and it works for high-school students because spatial creativity, not synthetic biology training, is what the task rewards. Pair it with Princeton's habit of writing down which model parameters are measured, derived or merely assumed — and publishing the history of their own corrected mistakes — which is the cheapest credibility a student dry lab can buy.

### GEMS-Taiwan — ReLEAF
High School · Taiwan · https://2026.igem.wiki/gems-taiwan/
ReLEAF closes a loop: field sensors and weather forecasts feed a stress-index model, the model sets a green-light dose, green light drives the cyanobacterial CcaSR two-component system in Bacillus subtilis WB800, and the cells secrete ACC deaminase into a hollow-fiber perfusion bioreactor that lets protein out and keeps cells in. The unit is about 40 x 24 x 62 cm, designed to stand beside a Taiwanese smallholder paddy where the average agricultural manager is 63.8 years old and precision agriculture is otherwise out of reach. It swept the high-school technical awards (Measurement, Hardware, Integrated Human Practices) largely on provenance discipline: four self-built devices with release build manuals, a digital twin that caught a failing photometer 26.7 hours before it died, a pre-registered growth forecast scored against a later run, and an input ledger that marks every number as measured, cited or modelled. Its distinguishing quality is honesty — the wiki repeatedly withdraws its own claims, and that is also where its dry-lab weaknesses are visible.

**frameworks.** Four strands. (1) A fitted crop-stress index: rather than weighting temperature, water and light by expert judgement, they fitted weights to Taiwan's own harvest record — 25 years of county rice yields from the Agriculture and Food Agency against ERA5 daily reanalysis weather (2001-2025), treating a season below the county trend as a stressed season, and exhaustively scoring all 2^15 - 1 = 32,767 combinations of fifteen candidate stress terms on held-out years. First and second rice crops were fitted separately; the second crop pays for wind, light and badly timed water, and heat adds nothing once those three are in — which the wiki notes undercuts the wet lab's heat programme. County error over 2016-2025 was 365 kg/ha against 419 for a plain trend line (32% error reduction on the second crop). A genuinely prospective test was frozen on 26 September 2026 before any county published; four of sixteen counties reported at 7.9% error against the trend's 8.8%, which the team correctly calls too few to establish performance. (2) Protein design (the GRAFT methodology: Generate, Restraints, Assembly, Flex, Triage) selected and shaped three protectants before any cloning — BoPEP4 (a 23-aa Brassica oleracea plant elicitor peptide docked against the PEPR1 receptor and run as nine all-atom MD trajectories), LEA14 (151-aa late embryogenesis abundant protein, five N-His constructs including a borrowed K-segment membrane-binding motif joined by a GGGGS linker), and ACC deaminase. The standout findings are negative and caught in time: a C-terminal 6xHis purification tag that every earlier check had approved was shown in simulation to cap the chemical group forming the peptide's strongest receptor contact, so the tag moved to the N-terminus; an Asn23 clamp was found to be five contacts rather than one salt bridge; a truncation ladder identified 9-23 as the production length (33% less mass) with the grip holding 98.5% of frames for 7-23 against 77.1% for the next rung down; and an AlphaFold confidence gate set before the result came back was failed for LEA14 with its partner, so by prior agreement no structure was handed on. For ACC deaminase no mutant was ordered at all, because the modelling said the enzyme meets far less substrate than it could handle and the largest available gain is a change to the medium (apoplast pH 5.5, where the Glu12-His227 contact holds in 99.9% of frames). (3) A reactor digital twin: an autoencoder trained on the healthy first 120 hours of a 434-hour run, scoring a sensor axis (the reference beam, which never passes through the culture) separately from a process axis (specific growth rate), so it can distinguish a culture event from a failing instrument; plus a Kalman-filter batch forecaster and a logistic growth prior fitted from the light plate. (4) Dose and fleet models: an arithmetic ledger from millilitres on a petri dish to US dollars per hectare, and a payback curve plotted across the whole efficacy axis.

**datascience.** Three practices lift this above typical high-school dry lab. First, pre-registration: on 1 October, before any WB800 bioreactor run, they registered a specific growth rate of 0.2986 h^-1 with a 90% interval of 0.2705-0.3300, a logistic curve shape with an NRMSE pass threshold of 15%, and inoculum-conditional times to OD 0.5, together with stated pass criteria. Run 6 gave 0.286 +/- 0.010 h^-1 (R2 0.978), inside the interval; the curve-shape endpoint was recorded as not scored because the prior misses the first seven hours by 30% and the run passes the prior's ceiling before hour 7. Run 7 was explicitly excluded from scoring because its three-hour lag has no term in the registered logistic and its fitted rate swings 0.16-0.46 h^-1 with the window choice. Second, anomaly detection with a diagnostic split: the autoencoder flagged the photometer at 216.3 h, 26.7 h before the OD channel failed at 243.0 h, and the window table shows the sensor axis at 100% alarms with the process axis at 0% during the drift — the model names which subsystem is broken, not just that something is. Third, forecast benchmarking against persistence rather than against nothing: the Kalman filter beat a no-change baseline by 41% at 2 h on the September run and by 24% at 8 and 12 h on run 7, with global-linear, exponential and local-linear alternatives reported as losers and the honest caveat that most of the run is above the photometer's linear range so the model forecasts the reading, not biomass. Other measurement work: the in-line photometer tracks a benchtop BioDrop with slope 1.018 (R2 0.995) to OD 1.2 across 45 paired TiO2 points and an iGEM silica protocol run in 2.5 mg steps, with a dilute-and-restore test returning within 0.2%; wall shear computed from pressure sensors and from the flow meter agree to 2.8%, so each sensor checks the other; and leaf-sensor bench characterisation found a +0.47 to +1.71 degC site-dependent offset against the air reference across 540 paired readings, with the conclusion stated that a 1.2-1.9 degC bias can hide or invent the very water-stress signal the twin would act on. Honest dry-lab weaknesses, stated by the team: a secreted-activity figure of 7.25 mU/mL at n = 1 and below quantitation; two induction runs that disagree on the sign of activity change over hours; the published CcaSR Hill curve (Castillo-Hair et al. 2019) assumed valid at 20 L when every induction was run at a single light intensity, so nothing tests it; a rice canopy correction of x2.44 that is modelled, not measured, and spans 1.68-3.52; a minimum effective dose that is unknown because the spray experiment varied salt and timing but never the applied amount; a withdrawn efficacy coefficient of 0.58; and only 17 of 25 modelled seasons ever crossing the trigger, so a ten-unit fleet runs on 4.3% of the calendar.

**dataviz.** The wiki's signature device is provenance colour-coding. The M4 dose ledger is drawn as a single top-to-bottom chain from 1.67 mL on a 10 cm plate to US$3800 capital per hectare, with a rail down the left that is green while every row still rests on a measurement and turns amber at the rice canopy correction, so a reader can see exactly where measurement stops and modelling begins; rows below inherit the model and two add assumptions of their own. Every model input is tabulated with a provenance column (seven from their own bench, four public records, two published constants, one from Geospatial Analysis, one neither measured nor cited), and the five assumptions get a table of 'what rests on it' and 'what would overturn it'. A timing diagram overlays the three-day Central Weather Administration forecast horizon, the three arrival arms the plant team ran, and the 5.4-day reactor lead time on a days-from-stress axis to show visually that they do not fit. The three disagreeing timing runs are shown side by side with the third panel re-reading the middle panel's own tubes as total chlorophyll instead of per gram, so the ranking visibly reverses — the figure argues against the team's own earlier claim. Decay figures plot both candidate interpretations through the same 28-hour reading and label the 22-fold divergence ('What one endpoint cannot say'). The payback plot marks their own 68-years-at-efficacy-1 point and Geospatial Analysis's 4.9-year estimate on the same axis and names the disagreement rather than hiding it. The digital twin UI itself puts optical density, pH, four pressure traces and the pump and valve controls on one screen; the description page opens with an interactive seven-block system map and a GIS choropleth of county nighttime temperature with circles scaled by rice yield trend.

**software.** The digital twin is released MIT-licensed at https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/gems-taiwan/digital-twin. It reads live OD600, pH, four pressure channels and turbine flow from the reactor loop, drives a pinch valve and four Luer valves, runs the autoencoder sensor alarm and the Kalman batch forecast, computes lumen pressure drop, transmembrane pressure and a fouling ratio through a hydraulic model, and applies the BLASTAM leaf-blast infection rule (a wet period counts when the leaf stays wet at least 10 hours at a mean of 22-25 degC, no infection below 15 or above 25 degC, past hours from the sensor and future hours estimated as wet at 90% relative humidity) to tell a grower to look for lesions five to ten days later. The team is clear about what is not wired up: green-light induction is tested but not integrated, dissolved-oxygen calibration did not hold, the protectant amount cannot be read in-line and comes from hand-drawn ELISA and DNPH samples, and every model so far has run on recorded data after a run with a person making every decision — so it is honestly a digital shadow moving toward a twin. Four open hardware devices ship with build manuals and print files: the hollow-fiber perfusion bioreactor (10-page assembly guide, 17-page brochure, 16-page user manual), a Pro and a Slim in-line photometer (12- and 13-page guides), and a 24-tube dual-wavelength light plate apparatus (10-page guide), plus a floating hydroponics plate with 13 seed positions, a 6.5 MB hardware notebook covering 23 March to 17 October 2026, and an LLM-assisted QGIS geospatial workflow over 346 farming townships with the data-preparation prompt published. Also contributed: 35 Registry parts in five SubtiToolKit Golden Gate modules, a 15-page plant protocol, a twentyfold scale-down of the ACC deaminase DNPH activity assay onto a 96-well plate, and waste-media protocols (hay, okara and sugarcane extracts benchmarked against LB).

**ihp.** 31 stakeholders over seven months, structured as a project evolution map in four stages with named dates, plus four thematic expert pipelines (deployment, protectant design, plant and stress biology, bioreactor and hardware) and continuous engagement with five core experts. The decisive change came at the very start: the original design released engineered Bacillus subtilis into the soil with a DesK-DesR system reading temperature directly. Prof. Chen Wen-Liang (10 April) and bioprocess experts said two things were wrong — the bacteria could not be contained, and biological sensing was neither precise nor controllable enough — so sensing moved out of the cell into electronic sensors and an AIoT model, and a hollow-fiber perfusion bioreactor was built to hold the bacteria in while letting the protectants out. That one conversation produced the entire architecture. Other changes with a clear before/after: Dr. Paul Verslues (Academia Sinica, 3 April) argued that supplying pure proline is inefficient and risks suppressing the plant's own P5CS1 biosynthesis and proline-redox balance, so they abandoned proline delivery for a plant-regulation framework using bacterial signals and precursors, shifted from stress recovery to early detection, and re-scored outcomes on root growth and biomass. Dr. Elizabeth Sattely (Stanford, 27 June) told them their proof of concept was too broad and to do one stress very well instead of many superficially, and to look at peptides — which is why BoPEP4 entered the panel and why plant testing narrowed to heat and salinity. CH Biotech (9 July) pushed them toward computational screening to optimise protectants, comparison of root irrigation vs foliar vs drone spray, production cost per area, and Taiwanese regulatory research before acting. Prof. Huang Chieh-Chen (NCHU, 28 July and 6 August) moved the reactor from continuous to periodic operation, raised seedling-stage application, warned that excessive protectant concentrations harm plants so thresholds must be validated, and supplied the B. subtilis WB800 strain the project now runs on. Prof. Cheng Mei-Chun (28 August) found that inconsistent plant ages and treatment conditions meant earlier results may have reflected unintended stress rather than treatment, and the protocols were standardised in response. Yes Health iFarm (11 August) prompted reconsidering the 8/16 light cycle for 12/12, adding DO and OD to parameter planning, switching from pure oxygen to gentle aeration, and minimising transplants because transplantation itself is a stressor. Most interesting is the natural-farming thread: at a public forum co-hosted with Green Media on 5 September, Dr. Li Hsu-Ying and Ms. Chen argued that a plant protected from every stress never builds tolerance — 'raising a crop is like raising a child'. Rather than dismiss it, the team made that the specification for M1: the reactor should fire only when a threshold that genuinely reflects crop condition is crossed, which is why the 32% error reduction matters as evidence for a release rule rather than as a number. A farmer at the same forum asked whether the system breaks organic certification; the team researched the regulations and concluded it cannot be used on organic farms, then interviewed Mr. Chen Ke-Wei of the Lanyang River Friendly Farming Production Cooperative to work out what that means commercially. The project's origin question came from Ghanaian farmers via Gilbert Nkpeniyeng of Ubuntu Social Enterprise Ghana (1 February).

**publicEngagement.** 140 students across 5 schools in tiered lessons for elementary, junior high and high school audiences, with pre- and post-Kahoot surveys per cohort and the results published as per-question accuracy charts — including the failures, such as DNA base pairing where only 30% of students answered correctly. Everything is released on a dedicated education website: three lesson plans, three slide decks, two card games, two online games and a plant stress simulator (CropShield), free to download, with the stated aim of making the lessons work without the team in the room. Hands-on activities included plant stress experiments, planter making, an ATCG card game and vocabulary work. The team also edited its own claims down for honesty — a visible wiki comment records removing a '49-point' improvement claim and a 'standard teaching methods' comparison, and correcting a student count from 144 to 140. Separately, a Taiwan-specific engagement channel: a LINE official account called 'Nong You Zhu Shou' (Farmer's Assistant) with six functions — latest news, product introduction, crop stress alerts, a crop assistant AI chatbot keyed to terms like salinity, heat stress and pests, a Farmer's Diary where users post weather, crop photos, soil moisture and pest conditions and earn tokens redeemable for LINE stickers, and a Google Form feedback loop — built because interviews at the Farmer Expo and with Ms. Chen Hui-Wen showed smallholders could not reach the information that already exists online. A public event at Taipei Water Garden Organic Farmers' Market on 5 September 2026 (Taiwan Coffee x Cocoa Gelato Festival) drew over 400 visitors with over 200 registered participants, running a forum, booth activities including a data-physicalisation installation and a ring toss, and a plant stress event.

**realWorld.** Positioned as a social enterprise with the vision 'every farmer is a biomanufacturer', deployed through farmer collectives and pilot cooperatives rather than direct sales, because the fleet analysis shows a reactor owned by a single farm is idle most of the season. The MVP is costed component by component: current bioreactor US$2280, leaf humidity sensor US$125, a drop-in sealed bacteria cartridge US$90 that opens automatically once seated so no one handles an open culture, and a Field Console mobile app; capital works out at about US$3800 per hectare before refills, service or labour. The regulatory target is contained-use answers in Taiwan by October 2027, and the team worked the pathway with Director Wu Tzu-Hsien (12 October), who pointed out their cost model was missing factory, labour, bacterial cultivation and waste-management costs, and with Prof. Chang Hung-Hao (31 August), who told them to narrow the initial application to a specific stress and crop. A conversation with Bioeconomy Corporation at BIO Asia-Taiwan redirected expansion research toward Southeast Asia, where agricultural sectors are large and GMO rules looser than the US or EU. Smart Agriweek Taiwan identified young farmers as the realistic early adopters and flagged that older farmers need a separate persuasion route. SWOT and PESTLE analyses name the real threats plainly: unclear regulation for cell-free agricultural biologics that may fall between biological pesticide and synthetic-biology-derived compound; protectant washing away; biofouling reducing yield; and the fact that only 3.47% of Taiwan's farmland was organic or eco-friendly by 2024, which both bounds and shapes the market. The payback analysis is the most commercially honest thing on the wiki: on their own loss figure of US$138 per hectare per crop, no point on the efficacy axis returns the capital on a useful horizon — 68 years even at perfect efficacy — while Geospatial Analysis reaches 4.9 years from a net benefit of US$1931 per crop, and the team states that the two do not yet price the same hectare rather than quietly adopting the favourable number. Deliverables include an 85-page business plan, a farmer-friendly user manual, and the three bioreactor documents.

**For GEMS:** The transferable asset is the provenance discipline, and it is cheaper than it looks: tag every number in a model as measured-by-us, cited, or modelled; publish an assumption register that states what would overturn each step; and when two of your own runs disagree, show both and name the disagreement instead of picking the flattering one. Pair that with one pre-registered, date-stamped prediction scored against a later experiment — GEMS-Taiwan's registered growth rate is the single highest-credibility item on its wiki, and it cost nothing but committing in writing before the data arrived.

### Cornell — Klothos
Undergrad · United States · https://2026.igem.wiki/cornell/
Every scar treatment on the market today starts after the scar has formed — silicone sheeting, intralesional steroid, laser and grafts are all passive or reactive, and none addresses fibrosis biology during the critical healing window. Klothos intervenes during healing instead: engineered bacteria secrete 810A, a 12-amino-acid peptide that binds the exposed C-terminal domain of CTGF (CCN2) and blocks fibroblast-to-myofibroblast activation, and expression is held behind a two-input AND gate built from the Pseudomonas syringae hrpR/hrpS/hrpL system so the peptide is only made when reactive oxygen species (via TrxC) and hypoxia (via Pfnr) are both present — the signature of unchecked remodelling. The bacteria are encapsulated in an alginate/PEO nanofiber matrix spun on a coaxial electrospinner the team designed and built themselves, because commercial instruments cost far more than an undergraduate team can reach. It won Best Hardware and Best Presentation on the strength of that open, flat-packable, interlock-protected electrospinner plus a modular 3D-printed coaxial spinneret adapter, and Best Fashion & Cosmetics on a project that is unusually complete end to end: 20-plus risk-rated commercialisation analysis, a six-phase FDA path, and a human practices programme built around people who actually live with scars.

**frameworks.** Cornell's modelling splits cleanly into wet lab and product development. On the biology side: a production-degradation ODE (dF/dt = alpha*X - delta_F*F) for SUMO-His-810A accumulation against biomass; a Hill function for Tet and future inducible promoter activity; Michaelis-Menten kinetics for SUMO protease cleavage to recover active peptide; an ELISA-based Hill-Langmuir binding isotherm for 810A against CTGF/C, fixed at n=1 because there is a single site, with an explicit note that a fitted n far from 1 would indicate error rather than cooperativity; and a quadratic ligand-depletion model for the regime where accessible CTGF and peptide concentrations are comparable and the ordinary Langmuir assumption breaks. Downstream of binding they built a reduced-order dynamic systems model of fibroblast state transition, parameterised from a protein interaction network assembled in STRING v12.5 — filtered on the Scarring Human Phenotype Ontology term HP:0100699, recovering 48 weighted edges, merged with CCN2's 20 nearest first-degree and 10 nearest second-degree neighbours, surfacing SMAD3, FN1 and TGFB2 as major nodes. Those nodes and weights were then run in Netflux as a logic-based ODE network (normalised node activity with a time constant, modified Hill activation and inhibition functions) using COL1A1 accumulation as the proxy for extracellular matrix hardening, and the simulation tracks the downstream TGF-beta inhibition reported in Xiao et al. 2020. Wound environment is modelled explicitly: ROS as a transient peak function calibrated against Carney et al. 2019 time-series qRT-PCR of SOD1, MGST1 and PRDX6 in hypertrophic scars, oxygen as an exponential recovery function, each feeding a Hill-function promoter. AlphaFold was used to render 810A and the CTGF/C-810A-6xHis complex. On the hardware side: a semi-empirical predictor of shell-solution viscosity (polymer overlap and entanglement statistics via Mark-Houwink), conductivity (mobile ion contribution) and surface tension (surfactant adsorption with a CMC/CAC plateau), the Fridrikh scaling law for terminal jet radius from flow rate, jet current and surface tension, plus continuity-based flow rate and stepper-motor plunger speed models.

**datascience.** The classifier is the clearest case of turning data into a predictive tool: rather than measuring solutions after purchase, Cornell predicts viscosity, conductivity and surface tension from formulation inputs (alginate concentration, PEO concentration and molecular weight, surfactant type and concentration, salt or buffer content, temperature) and uses the prediction to avoid spinning runs that cannot work. They name candidate implementations — logistic regression, random forest, or Gaussian process classification, favouring the Gaussian process on a small dataset because it returns uncertainty — and define a two-level validation plan: property-level (mean absolute error for viscosity, percent error for conductivity, absolute error in mN/m for surface tension against held-out measured formulations) and outcome-level (whether predicted-green formulations actually produce stable shell-only fibres, judged on Taylor cone formation, current stability, bead formation, dry deposition and fibre diameter distribution). They say outright that the classifier matters more than exact numerical accuracy, and that literature Mark-Houwink, CMC and adsorption constants are starting estimates to be recalibrated against the team's own measurements. Fibre morphology was quantified by image analysis: tortuosity as the ratio of fibre contour length to end-to-end distance, with a >1.10 threshold defining 'curly', giving 8% curly and 92% straight. Failure diagnosis was also model-driven — droplet breakup was traced to insufficient PEO chain entanglement at 100 kDa, leading them to raise PEO from 1.5% to 2% and cut back PS80 surfactant.

**dataviz.** The standout is the Unified Readiness Classifier, which collapses three separate property predictions into a single green/yellow/red call on whether a formulation should go to the electrospinner at all — green means proceed to voltage-window testing, yellow allows one short trial or minor reformulation, red means reformulate first. It is rendered as a spinning-viability contour map over sodium alginate and PEO weight percentages produced by Monte Carlo sampling against literature results, so a reader can see the spinnable region rather than read a table of numbers. The alginate molecular-weight analysis is similarly well-framed: one plot puts viscosity on the left axis spanning more than four orders of magnitude while conductivity and surface tension on the right axis stay flat, which makes the whole argument visible at a glance — conductivity caps how much alginate you can dissolve, molecular weight decides whether that limit is reachable, and the optimum is interior rather than monotonic. The STRING network is shown as a force-directed layout and the Netflux run as normalised activity curves for CTGF, TGFB1, FN1, COL1A1, SMAD2 and SMAD3 together. The wiki itself is a scroll-driven 3D island journey ('scroll to travel, click an island to explore') with an interactive AND-gate widget letting the reader switch each input signal on and off, and a WebGL model of the electrospinner.

**software.** No standalone software release; the released artefact is the hardware. The electrospinner is published openly as a bill of materials, CAD files, circuit diagrams, assembly documentation, an operation manual and a dedicated safety manual, designed to be disassembled and flat-packed for transport by teams in shared or temporary workspaces. Control is an ESP32 DevKitC microcontroller driving an AHV24V30KVR5MAW high-voltage module (24 V in, up to 30 kV out) for digitised control in place of a potentiometer, with an access-door interlock and emergency stop that cut power and ground the high-voltage circuit. A separate contribution is the modular 3D-printed coaxial needle adapter, which keeps metal needle tips for conductivity while 3D-printing the structure, adaptable across needle gauges and core-shell flow configurations. They also publish a disulfide-bond-optimised SHuffle expression protocol (6xHis-SUMO fusion, SUMO as chaperone and clean cleavage handle) framed for reuse on other hard-to-express proteins such as insulin-like growth factors, antibody fragments and venom peptides, plus protocols for alginate preparation, crosslinking viability testing, escape testing, light microscopy ImageJ analysis and spectrographic bacterial settling.

**ihp.** Several interviews changed the project rather than decorating it. The clearest is hardware: advised not to build their own high-voltage power supply (especially from microwave parts) because the electrical risk is serious, the team dropped the homemade supply entirely, consulted Cornell's Afridi Lab, and bought a commercial regulated unit while sourcing other parts through Digi-Key and Mouser to hold cost down — the advice was that boosting voltage is easy but a stable regulated DC output is the hard part. Dr Insoo Hyun reframed safety itself: he introduced weighing risks and benefits against existing alternatives rather than assuming absolute safety, and warned that familiarity with a microorganism from food use does not demonstrate safety in an open wound, also pressing them to choose experimental models that resemble real wound conditions rather than the most convenient ones. Dr Joseph Fins pushed on preclinical evidence and asked whether delivering the peptide directly, without living bacteria, would be safer and simpler — which the team now carries explicitly as a documented de-risking architecture, with the trade-off (a pre-loaded matrix gives a fixed dose and loses the AND-gated release) stated rather than hidden. Dr Andrew Leask's input on CCN2/CTGF signalling shaped the target rationale, and reviewer pressure to confirm H2O2 is still detectable at the wound stage they target led them to work on sensor sensitivity and add the hypoxia AND gate for specificity. Burn survivor and former burn nurse Amy Acton and Andrea at the Phoenix Society for Burn Survivors changed how the team talks: survivors need support long after wounds heal — financial help for compression garments and procedures, emotional support, connection with others — treatments are costly, uncomfortable and variable, so do not promise how much a treatment will reduce scarring. Roughly 20 older adults and visitors at open events taught them that a scar's size or appearance does not predict its personal impact, and that open conversation surfaced concerns their structured survey questions missed; they concluded existing scales describe the scar but not what the person would want improved. Alison Bateman-House at NYU identified composition and method-of-production as their strongest patent claims and walked them through the one-year US grace period and PCT economics, which fed directly into the commercialisation plan. A kelp-farming conversation moved the sustainability case from biodegradability to sourcing, noting that North American kelp farmers' binding constraint is finding buyers rather than growing kelp since wild-harvested seaweed is substantially cheaper — a point that complicates rather than flatters their own narrative.

**publicEngagement.** Cornell ran an unusually wide and genuinely iterative education programme. Plasmid Pals, their own educational game, was playtested with Big Brothers Big Sisters participants who then suggested how to make it more interactive. Plasmid bracelets plus an open-ended idea board asking visitors how they would use synthetic biology to change the world evolved into age-adapted versions for daycare, the Sciencenter and the State Fair — and when reading and spelling turned out to be barriers for roughly 20 preschoolers, the team switched to a cooking analogy (DNA as cookbook, RNA as copied recipe, protein as finished dish), writing up the lesson that activities must match developmental ability. A summer-camp session had about 80 students debate which scientific problems deserve funding using live polls, and a 30-minute lesson drew another 20-25 minutes of student-led questions about research careers and contributing without lab access. STEM Her Way was a four-session series in which high school girls learned synthetic biology and presented their own research proposals, rated 4.7/5 by 15 respondents across seven countries with every respondent recommending it. A shadowing programme drew more than 260 applications from the US and 17 countries for six high school scholars, later extended to five international students whose own project proposals the team helped assess for feasibility — a participant from Uzbekistan brought soil salinity as a community problem and the students developed Salt Guardians around it. They also ran a worldwide synthetic biology governance competition (regulatory pathways, biosafety and containment, access and equity, plus an open governance challenge), produced a narrative synthetic biology podcast, taught Lambert iGEM how to prepare stakeholder questions by sharing their own Human Practices deck and brainstorming guide, and swapped children's books with NUGEM — NUGEM translating Cornell's into Kazakh and Russian while Cornell translated NUGEM's into Mandarin, Spanish and French.

**realWorld.** This is the most developed commercial package of the five. Target market is quantified: burn centres and academic hospitals in the American Northeast, where 2,255 medical institutions — 26 verified burn centres, 604 hospitals (31 with ACGME dermatology residencies) and 1,625 medical spas — serve an estimated 1.8 million addressable patients per year, or 2.2 patients per institution per day, with academic hospitals and verified burn centres targeted first as likeliest to trial new technology. The regulatory analysis identifies the real hazard: Klothos is a combination product (alginate nanofiber device plus engineered live bacteria), so FDA assigns a primary mode of action deciding whether CBER leads via IND/BLA or CDRH via 510(k)/PMA, and misclassification could force a restart costing an estimated 18-24 months and $500K-plus — hence a formal Pre-RFD consultation with the Office of Combination Products before committing development resources. They cite Azitra's engineered S. epidermidis with an open IND and FDA Fast Track as precedent that CBER will accept an IND for topical engineered bacteria. A six-phase plan runs from prototype and fibroblast assays, through an IND/IDE-enabling package with dermal safety, immunogenicity, biodistribution and microbial containment, to Phase I (with viable-organism monitoring because it is a live biotherapeutic) and a Phase II randomised controlled trial in surgical, burn, hypertrophic-scar-risk and revision-scar settings scored on POSAS, VSS and SCAR-Q. A freedom-to-operate analysis covers ten patents across four technology areas, with specific flags (the University of Manitoba colour-changing antibacterial nanofiber US20220047523A1 and NYCU's pending pH-sensitive electrospun bandage would need review before adding a pH indicator), plus PCT costs of roughly $17K to hold in 150 signatories and $20K per country thereafter. They map regulatory strategy across seven regions, including the MHRA consultation on modernising the GTMP definition (closed 22 June 2026) and Korea's MFDS review reforms cutting target timelines from about 420 to 295 days. Over 20 risks across technical, market, financial and regulatory categories are rated on severity, likelihood and detectability with mitigations and rendered as a heat map; a skill gap radar names what the 45-plus member team cannot yet do (pricing, physician adoption, launch strategy, clinical trial design) and how they would fill it. Reimbursement is treated honestly: novel combination products often lack an established billing code, so they model unit economics under both self-pay and reimbursed scenarios. The team won an ANSA grant and flagged Cornell's technology transfer office licensing terms as a Year 1 gating factor for any spinout.

**For GEMS:** Build the cheap version of the instrument and publish it properly. Cornell's winning move was deciding that an electrospinner — normally a specialised commercial purchase — could be made from stock parts and 3D prints, then releasing the bill of materials, CAD, circuit diagrams, assembly guide, operation manual and a separate high-voltage safety manual with interlocks and an emergency stop designed in. For a school-based centre the paired lesson is the readiness classifier: predict a formulation's viscosity, conductivity and surface tension from its recipe, label it green/yellow/red, and spend scarce lab time only on green — a cheap model that saves expensive experiments is worth more than an elaborate one that does not change what you do next.

### GU Frankfurt — HIDE
Overgrad · Germany · https://2026.igem.wiki/gu-frankfurt/
Around 183,000 transplants a year are followed by lifelong immunosuppression, which protects the graft by weakening the whole patient. HIDE attacks the cause instead: a synNotch receptor carrying a computationally designed binder recognises the donor organ's mismatched HLA class I alleles, triggers production and export of shRNA in extracellular vesicles, and silences only those 'non-self' HLAs by RNA interference, leaving the rest of the immune system intact. Three research fields are bridged at once (synNotch, RNAi, exosome delivery), with the binder and the shRNA both designed in silico by the dry lab and validated by FACS, qPCR, western blot and nanoparticle tracking analysis. It won Best Part Collection and Best Education because the by-products are as usable as the therapy: HUSH, an open-source RNAi design framework for polymorphic gene families, and TRUST, a framework for communicating about death and grief that iGEM did not previously have.

**frameworks.** Two pipelines solving an allele-discrimination problem that has no off-the-shelf method. For the binder, the team deliberately picked the harder target: HLA-A*01 (allele frequency around 15%) rather than the more common HLA-A*02, because A*01 carries fewer polymorphisms relative to other common alleles and therefore makes a specific binder harder to design; an IPD-IMGT multiple sequence alignment of HLA-A*01:01:01:01 against A*02:01:01:01 and A*03:01:01:01 located the usable mismatches, concentrated in and around the peptide-binding groove of the polymorphic alpha1 and alpha2 domains. They then generated roughly 2,000 de novo binders with BindCraft and RFdiffusion3, scored affinity and specificity against target and off-target HLAs with Boltz-2 and AlphaFold, and carried the eight most promising designs into molecular dynamics simulations for stability, across six design batches with combined MD results. For the shRNA, sequence alignment identified nucleotide-level discriminating positions, candidates were designed and evaluated with siDirect, and every candidate was screened against the human genome for off-targets in other human mRNAs. HUSH then added 150 further shRNAs with alignment-aware targeting.

**datascience.** HUSH exists because the team audited the tool landscape and found it stagnant: commercial RNAi designers are proprietary black boxes whose algorithms and option sets are undocumented, and even non-commercial siDirect is neither open-source nor pipeline-integrable, while recent published advances for discriminating highly similar sequences had been implemented nowhere. HUSH therefore folds multiple sequence alignment into the design step itself: a target sequence plus an optional panel of related sequences (the alleles to spare) switches on allele-aware targeting and an MSA stage, and the tool inspects the input up front (molecule type, length, GC content, panel size) and warns, for example, that a GC-rich target may cause the seed filter to reject every candidate, then offers to relax that filter in the criteria step. Protein input is flagged because it must be resolved to a transcript first. Safety is a scoring stage, not a disclaimer: candidates are aligned with Bowtie against NCBI human RefSeq, and the team proposes extending the standard off-target check to known single-nucleotide polymorphisms that could create unwanted off-targets. Designed siRNAs convert to shRNAs with hairpin-loop guidance and thermodynamic evaluation of structure integrity.

**dataviz.** The wiki is built as an explorable system rather than a document. The dry-lab overview is a hover-and-click hitbox diagram where each component (Binder, shRNA, HUSH) reveals its rationale and links through to its own results page. The HLA class I architecture is a draggable 3D structure coloured by domain (alpha1, alpha2, alpha3, beta2m) so the reader can see for themselves that the variation sits in the groove. The MSA is shown in classic dash notation against the A*01 reference so each mismatch is countable. MD runs are published as per-binder, per-allele animations (for example binder FR57 against HLA-A*01, A*02 and A*03 side by side), which makes specificity visible rather than tabulated. The HUSH page embeds a working mockup of the five-stage wizard with sample data that the reader can step through, and the mascot Heidi narrates each step. Human practices is an interactive stakeholder map filterable by affiliation and by part of the construct, so a reader can ask 'who shaped the binder?' and get an answer. Education statistics are presented as before-and-after pairs, not totals.
