**frameworks.** Design-Build-Test-Learn applied separately to the assay, to the 3D-printed emulsification device (v0 to v8) and to the course materials; an explicit 'problem -> approach -> solution -> outcome' framing on every major page; measurement treated as a prerequisite for enzyme screening rather than a reporting step; Human Practices feedback logged as 'feedback -> action' pairs that changed protocols.

**datascience.** The core contribution is an ATP assay that was validated before it was trusted. Three quench methods were compared head to head (cold dilution, 95 C heat stop, EDTA chelation) by sampling a DrPPK2 reaction at fixed reaction times and then varying the hold time before adding CellTiter-Glo; a flat line means the reaction stopped, a rising line means it did not. EDTA was chosen because it scales to 16 enzymes in pre-poured plates, and the concentration was then tuned from 10 mM to 5 mM when enzyme load dropped from 50 to 7.5 ng/uL. The team then defined the assay's reliable ATP range by testing whether they could extend Promega's 10 nM to 1 uM window in either direction, found they could not (0.061 nM ATP still read above 10,000 RLU; the 100 uM standard deviated from linearity), and committed to reading only inside that range and never extrapolating, discarding data that fell outside. Because EDTA, AMP and ADP all suppress luciferase, every sample is compared against ATP standards prepared at the same pre-reagent EDTA concentration and the same substrate concentration, and the ratio of slopes gives per-condition correction factors (tabulated for all eight AMP and ADP levels at both 1:25 and 1:50 dilutions, e.g. AMP CF 0.0822 at 2 mM and 0.6113 at 0.0156 mM) that are hard-coded into the published Excel templates. Correcting recovers the kinetic trend that inhibition had destroyed: the same DrPPK2 AMP dataset moves from Km 0.020 mM / Vmax 5.66 uM/min uncorrected to Km 0.139 mM / Vmax 23.2 uM/min corrected, and the 2 mM AMP point is openly excluded from the fit because the correction does not fully recover it. Benchmark kinetics are reported with R2 (DrPPK2 ADP Km 0.985 mM, Vmax 11.7 uM/min, R2 0.9894; ManPPK2 ADP Km 2.67 mM, Vmax 42.6 uM/min, R2 0.9993; FtPPK2 ADP Km 3.16 mM, Vmax 80.05 uM/min, R2 0.9963). Reproducibility was tested as an experiment in its own right: three team members ran the same full-range assay on the same enzyme aliquot on the same day, giving Km 0.0775 +/- 0.0145 mM and Vmax 8.62 +/- 1.39 uM/min, and the team states plainly that these do not match the earlier full-range values and lists the candidate causes (different purification batch, new polyP lot, new AMP lot) as unresolved. Microscopy is handled by a named pipeline, CellScope, which runs Cellpose segmentation at 1.332 um/pixel after 4x downsampling, exports one row per object per timepoint to parquet (over a million objects on one plate), applies a QC gate on diameter 5 to 60 um, circularity 0.80 to 1.25 and no saturated pixels, reports each well as fold over its own background, and runs a two-mode (delta-BIC) test for subpopulations; a dedicated figure documents a case where the segmentation silently failed on a visibly good well, which the team published rather than hid. Every bulk plate carries a 0.125 uM fluorescein well as a dye reference, and the wiki maintains an explicit glossary distinguishing RFU (plate reader) from AU (microscope) as non-comparable units.

**dataviz.** Interactive charts embedded in the wiki (per-condition time courses, Michaelis-Menten fits, reproducibility datasets) with selectable conditions; side-by-side uncorrected vs corrected Michaelis-Menten fits; log-scaled ATP standard curves; per-cell log10 GFP scatter plots across 24 timepoints with per-timepoint median lines and a dashed per-plate subpopulation threshold; a two-clock explainer diagram teaching readers how to read the quench-validation figures; SolidWorks drawings of every finalized 3D-printed part.

**software.** OpenTrons OT-2 Python protocols for dilution-plate creation and dilution execution (full-range and confirmatory, four enzymes), published as .py downloads; Excel analysis templates for the full-range AMP, full-range ADP and confirmatory assays with correction factors built in; a master-mix calculator, titration design workbooks, plate-map template and osmolarity worksheet; the CellScope image-analysis pipeline (Cellpose segmentation, OzaLabCP/Imageanalysis) with a published vesicle_pipeline.txt; STL files for the washboard insert and rubber-band sled; raw time-course data and raw image data/masks released. All downloads are collected on https://2026.igem.wiki/calpolyslo/downloads and the lab manuals are released under CC BY 4.0.

**ihp.** Consultations with ethicists, legal and biosecurity scholars and industry scientists were run as feedback-to-action pairs. Dr Hank Greely advised publishing safety and containment thinking before starting work, so the team published aims, protocols, lab manuals and safety forms. Dr Ryan Jenkins recommended survivability testing as risk-assessment evidence, so the team tested whether synthetic cells survive outside the tube across pH, salinity and real environmental water samples (Los Osos Creek wetland, Avila Beach ocean water, campus pond, tap and deionised water) and found the cells lyse outside pH 7 +/- 1, at seawater salinity and in every environmental sample; he also prompted a lab-notebook safety checklist. Dr Keith Robison raised dual-use scenarios, which produced a benefits-vs-misuse framework. Dr Tae Seok Moon raised public perception, which produced IRB-approved surveys (Cal Poly IRB #2026-194 and #2026-195) of 10 CSHL Summer Synthetic Biology participants and 30 Cal Poly FSURP students on comfort, trust and regulation. Dr Zachary Sun's view that education may be the realistic near-term application reshaped the project's scope toward enzyme characterisation and teaching.

**publicEngagement.** The team designed CHEM 471: Engineering Synthetic Cells, described as the first known undergraduate synthetic-cell course in the US, wrote and tested ten open-licence (CC BY 4.0) lab manuals plus an instructor packet with prep lists, reagent costs, timing and common failure points, taught it to ten students in spring 2026, and surveyed them before and after. Confidence rose in 9 of 12 skills; the three that did not became design inputs. Students rated fluorescence microscopy lower at the end than at the start, so the microscope protocols were rewritten and re-tested by the team's least experienced members; manual cytosol-recipe maths was replaced by auto-scaling Excel calculators; NanoOrange/A280 protein quantification was replaced with a Bradford assay plus BSA standard curve; and the Promega AMP/ADP protocol was replaced with the team's own real-time assay. A student's suggestion became the tip-wipe oil-removal method that was then tested against the standard method.

**realWorld.** The framing throughout is cost of access rather than novelty: PPK2 plus polyphosphate is pursued because it lowers the price floor of cell-free protein synthesis, and the 3D-printed washboard replaces a hand-raking step that varies between operators. The course is explicitly packaged as a template other undergraduate institutions can adopt, with reagent costs and set-up in an instructor packet, and the full protocol set released so other programmes can either reproduce the six enzyme-characterisation experiments or swap in their own enzymes. Six characterised PPK2 enzymes and sixteen candidate-panel enzymes are deposited as registry parts with their datasets linked.

**For GEMS:** Before comparing anything, prove the measurement: validate the quench, establish the instrument's honest linear range and refuse to extrapolate outside it, then build a separate standard curve for every interfering condition and hard-code the resulting correction factors into the analysis template you ship. Then test reproducibility by handing the written protocol to people who have never run it, and publish the disagreement when their numbers differ from yours.

### DTU-Denmark — Enzymatic degradation of wind turbine blade epoxy
Overgrad · Denmark · https://2026.igem.wiki/dtu-denmark/
DTU engineered laccases (ItL-03 from a spruce bark beetle gut metagenome, CueO variants and homologues) and unspecific peroxygenases (PaDa-I, WamPa, PabUPO-II, MroUPO, Fett) to attack the amine crosslinks of cured epoxy from wind turbine blades, layered on top of a published acid-plus-peroxide solvolysis pretreatment. They used NNBT, a small water-soluble molecule carrying the tertiary amine of the crosslink, as a defined model substrate, and showed by MALDI-TOF that PaDa-I performs N-dealkylation on it with Purpald confirmation of lactaldehyde release. The decisive work is a prospective comparative life-cycle assessment in SimaPro (ReCiPe 2016 Midpoint H) of five end-of-life routes, which found their own enzymatic route is NOT the best option on almost any indicator - and they published that. Seven interviews across DTU Wind, DTU Sustain, DTU Chemistry, SDU and industry, plus documented non-responses from Siemens Gamesa, Orsted and MAKEEN Energy, drove changes to the chemical target, the model substrate, the host organism, the enzyme-ranking criterion and the project's stated goal.

**frameworks.** Three parallel enzyme-discovery pipelines agreed after advice from the 2025 team's dry-lab head: an 'easy' track of literature enzymes known to oxidise the relevant bonds, a 'medium' track of homologue mining, and a 'hard' track of rational engineering and generative design. Plus a prospective comparative LCA (SimaPro, ReCiPe 2016 Midpoint H, functional unit of blade mass with cutting/transport/metal separation excluded as identical across routes) and a Kremser-equation model of the countercurrent solvent extraction stage.

**datascience.** Sequence mining of UniProt, Pfam and BLAST rather than metagenomic libraries; multiple sequence alignment to transfer organic-solvent-tolerance mutations from PaDa-I onto GroGu and PabUPO-II; a novel substrate-access-channel discovery pipeline used in place of docking affinity ranking; molecular dynamics; generative enzyme design on the DTU HPC. Every LCA parameter is published with its source, the mismatch between source and use, and a 'weakest link' label (e.g. partition coefficients taken from a 1980 phenol-extraction paper using MIBK rather than ethyl acetate, flagged explicitly).

**dataviz.** An interactive clickable process-flow diagram that zooms from the five-route overview into the enzymatic routes with every parameter on the box (acid molarity, temperature, residence time, enzyme loading in mg/L, number of reuses, recovery fractions); one SDG per plot with burdens above zero and credits below; an interactive stakeholder map where each pin opens the interview, colour-coded by engagement status so non-responses stay visible.

**software.** LCA input data, assumptions and mapping code released open source so other teams can rebuild the model in SimaPro or another tool; lectures, workshops and guides collected on the contribution page.

**ihp.** DTU's IHP is built as a decision trail, not a visitor log: every interview card carries an explicit 'Implementation' list, and there is a separate section on approaches they chose NOT to pursue. The single biggest change came from Dr Javier (Postdoc, DTU Sustain, one of the few in his group working on resin chemistry rather than glass-fibre recovery) across two interviews on 3 March and 24 June 2026. He posed what the team calls the sharpest experimental question raised in the project - can an enzyme replace the cleaving solvent, acting on a swollen but still crosslinked network? - and told them to start from a well-documented literature pretreatment rather than invent one and layer enzymes on top. The result was a hard reframing: the enzymatic step stopped being a standalone degradation claim and became a complement to solvolysis, with a new explicit objective of testing whether enzymes could substitute for part of the solvent-cleavage step, and a second research line on engineering solvent tolerance into the enzymes. Justine Beauson (Senior Researcher, Composites Manufacturing and Testing, DTU Wind) was the first contact; she confirmed thermoset epoxy is what is coming down now, referred the team to a turbine OEM, and in a 6 October email follow-up explained that the Blade Material Passport is compiled independently of any thinking about disposal and will tell you a blade is epoxy but never the formulation - which is why the team abandoned any attempt to match real blade resin and why 'collaboration between the production and the waste-management industries' became the organising claim on the sustainability page. Jesper Kjaer Jorgensen (Postdoc, Composites, DTU) then supplied fully cured SWANCOR 2519-1A/BS, a commercial non-NDA amine-cured bisphenol-A epoxy, and agreed with the team's hypothesis that the tertiary amine crosslink is the vulnerable point: the team writes plainly that 'without those cubes we would have had either no workable material or a different one', and the target shifted from the epoxy backbone to the amine crosslinks, changing which bonds they went after, how they measured degradation and which products they hoped to recover. Robert (PhD, Eukaryotic Molecular Cell Biology) delivered the hardest reality check - thermoset degradation is heavily researched, the field contains many low-quality papers with missing controls and uncharacterised substrates, and a six-month student project cannot run a metagenomic discovery campaign - and the team's response is laid out item by item: they screened roughly 33 enzymes rather than thousands, worked from public databases rather than metagenomic libraries, used a colorimetric assay rather than a fluorescent reporter, added MALDI-TOF, and had a postdoc rather than students perform the hazardous epoxy pretreatment. Carlos G. Acevedo-Rocha (Senior Researcher, Computational Protein Engineering, BRIGHT) told them not to base findings on docking affinity values because there is no significant correlation with experimental activity, and endorsed their early-stage channel-discovery pipeline: they abandoned the plan to filter homologue candidates on Boltz-2 affinity scores and rebuilt candidate selection around channel geometry plus molecular dynamics. Cecilia Castellvi Domingo (PhD, heterologous expression of UPOs) changed the chassis and the protocol - Komagataella phaffii on an episomal AP17 backbone rather than S. cerevisiae or E. coli, harvest at day 5 instead of day 6 to reduce proteolysis, lower induction temperature, and the CO-difference spectrum assay that gave them a direct measurement of correctly folded heme-containing enzyme (0.019 uM in a six-fold concentrated sample) that activity assays could not. Lykke Margot Ricard (Associate Professor in Sustainable Innovation, SDU, who had mapped Danish blade treatment options for the Danish EPA) asked who the retaker is, and in response every workstream was required to name a recoverable product, the quality it would need and a potential buyer - which is also why the team says the ideal process recovers a product rather than incinerating residues. The European Environment Agency answered that it holds no data on retired blade management, that the WEEE Directive does not cover wind turbines and that no dedicated EU legislation exists, so there is no reporting obligation; the team then marked the landfill share as an unverifiable input in the LCA rather than quoting a number. Most unusually, they publish their failures of access: Siemens Gamesa never replied to email and had no relevant expert at the DSE careers fair, nobody at Orsted could speak to blade end-of-life, MAKEEN Energy did not reply, and the team states outright that the groups with the greatest influence over adoption 'were therefore among the least represented in our discussions, limiting our analysis' - and makes those gaps visible on the stakeholder map, which rates each group by influence over adoption and interest separately, including 'unknown' for potential buyers of recovered compounds because no market has been shown to exist.

**publicEngagement.** Education was pointed at the specific blind spot the project exposed rather than at synthetic biology in general: visits to international high schools taught the wind sector's end-of-life emissions and the idea of thinking in full sustainability circles early, and a Lifelong Learning workshop took the same low-impact recycling discussion to an audience of working professionals. For the iGEM community they ran a BioBrick workshop, an intellectual-property introduction ('Protecting Your Ideas'), a World Cafe team-to-team roundtable and a podcast, and presented at the Nordic iGEM Conference. State of Green gave them a platform to put the blade-waste problem to people from ministries, academia and the energy sector.

**realWorld.** The need is a quantified bottleneck rather than a slogan: Danish blade waste currently goes to mixed-waste landfill or is shipped abroad by lorry and ferry, the Danish wind industry's voluntary landfill ban took effect on 1 January 2026, a Danish EPA screening detected bisphenol A in every tank leaching test on blade material, and the EEA confirmed there is no EU legislation or reporting obligation for wind-turbine waste at all pending the WEEE revision in the Circular Economy Act. SDGs are justified target by target with numbers from their own LCA, and the headline finding is one most teams would hide: in the base industrial scale-up scenario (projected to about 2035) the enzymatic route emits 2.1 kg CO2 eq per kg of blade against 1.4 for solvolysis and 0.9 for pyrolysis, adds 0.38 person-equivalents of human carcinogenic toxicity against 0.022 for solvolysis, uses about 36% more water, and cement co-processing is best on almost every indicator - so they state that enzymatic and solvolysis are the only routes with clear net burdens, trace the hotspot to the H2O2 supply chain and UPO production, and convert that into a research direction (make UPO production more efficient, recover a product instead of incinerating residues, reuse immobilised enzyme and compute the break-even number of reuses). SDG targets are matched one-to-one with their own data on SDG 3 (illness from hazardous chemicals), 6 (water-use efficiency), 7 (renewable share and clean-energy research cooperation), 8 (the Energy Transition Alliance estimate that a UK blade-recycling segment could add 20,000 jobs to offshore wind's 60,000-by-2030 target), 9, 12, 13, 14, 15 and 17. Limitations are declared inside the SDG analysis rather than buried: unknown reaction product, no demonstration of enzyme performance on real blade material, one blade type only, transport excluded by the system boundary, microplastic and BPA leaching not characterised by ReCiPe, and no penalty in the cut-off model for losing glass fibre as a resource. What happens next: the LCA inputs, assumptions and mapping code are open source, the OEM's requirements (handle multi-material blades at reasonable cost and pace) are recorded as requirements for future development rather than achievements, and relationships with State of Green, the Center for Biosolutions and DTU are described as collaborations that can continue beyond iGEM.

**For GEMS:** Run a comparative LCA against the incumbent technologies early enough that it can still change the research plan, and publish it even when it says your own route loses - then convert each losing indicator into a named engineering target, and record the stakeholders who never replied so the gaps in your evidence base are visible rather than invisible.

### GreatBay-SCIE — Expelliodor — Expel the Odor, on Your Terms
High School · China · https://2026.igem.wiki/greatbay-scie/
Axillary odour arises when Staphylococcus hominis imports the odourless precursor Cys-Gly-3M3SH through the peptide transporter PepTSh and converts it to 3M3SH. Rather than killing skin bacteria, GreatBay-SCIE attacked the uptake step three ways: a de novo small-molecule binding protein that sequesters the precursor, a de novo protein binder designed to lock PepTSh in its inward-facing conformation, and a cyclodextrin glucanotransferase engineered to glycosylate the precursor so the transporter no longer recognises it. This is the most sophisticated de novo protein design campaign of any high school team in the cohort — RFdiffusion3, Proteina-Complexa, ProteinMPNN, RoseTTAFold3 co-folding, 50-ns MD with MM/GBSA, and SPURS-guided thermostability engineering — organised around two frameworks they invented: a Characterize stage prepended to DBTL, and a funnel-shaped decision-gated workflow that spends expensive methods only on candidates that survive cheap ones. Nine precursor binders and five transporter binders were actually tested in vitro, with 4 of 9 and 4 of 5 significantly reducing 3M3SH.

**frameworks.** Two methodological contributions frame everything. The CHARACTERIZE-DBTL framework inserts a stage before Design with four substages — Problem Definition (what the design must achieve, in what context, with what intervention points), Target Definition (the exact molecule, protein, conformational state, interface or reaction to engineer, with boundaries), Mechanistic Characterization (assess the plausibility of the proposed mechanism against experimental, structural and computational evidence), and Design Specification (translate all of that into explicit requirements that become the literal inputs to the design tool). The DECISION-GATED WORKFLOW is a funnel in which each successive evaluation is more expensive than the last, so a large generated set is cut by cheap co-folding metrics before anything reaches molecular dynamics and only a handful reach the bench — explicitly chosen because they are a high school team with limited wet-lab resources. The Characterize stage paid off concretely in each of the three routes. For the PRECURSOR BINDER, characterisation established that 3M3SH exists as two stereoisomers with different smells, that the sweat-and-onion-like (S) form is the odour-relevant one, and that deep-learning design tools frequently introduce stereochemical errors — so the design specification became 'use Cys-Gly-(S)-3M3SH with explicitly defined stereochemistry as input and verify ligand chirality after structure generation before any candidate advances'. Two independent design routes were run in parallel for comparison: RFdiffusion3 (via Rosetta Foundry, with ProteinMPNN sequence redesign and RoseTTAFold3 co-folding validation, ranked by RF3's own ranking_score) and Proteina-Complexa (a partially-latent flow-matching model, ranked by a custom composite score). Top binders from each route went to 50-ns MD scored on ligand RMSD and MM/GBSA binding free energy. For the TRANSPORTER BINDER, characterisation drew on published MD showing that the inward-to-outward transition is the rate-limiting step of PepTSh's transport cycle, so stabilising the inward-facing state should block transport; they took the experimental inward-facing crystal structure (PDB 6EXS), built an outward-facing homology model in SWISS-MODEL, and compared them to find extracellular electrostatic networks (K64-E323, and the R184/D182/E340/R337 cluster) and hydrophobic patches present only in the inward-facing state — those became the target interface, with a specification of an 80-120 residue binder and a preference for compact designs to improve accessibility through a Gram-positive cell wall. Design was RFdiffusion3 backbone generation, ProteinMPNN sequence design, RF3 co-folding, interface-placement filtering, then a composite score of 0.50 x normalised ranking score + 0.25 x normalised pLDDT + 0.25 x normalised inverse PAE, then MD. For CGTase, characterisation enumerated the three modifiable groups on the precursor (amino, carboxyl, hydroxyl) and selected reactions by compatibility with the actual application environment — mildly acidic human skin with no external supply of ATP or NADH — which ruled out cofactor-dependent chemistry and left hydroxyl transglycosylation by CGTase; molecular docking from the 1CXL template with cluster analysis of poses, followed by MD of the wild-type complex, showed the non-native substrate stays stably accommodated in the catalytic pocket and identified which interactions were weak (around the carboxylate group and the hydrophobic tail), which became the rational-design targets for nine point mutants, each re-evaluated by MD. Two further optimisation campaigns followed: CGTase thermostability via SPURS (an AI stability predictor) after excluding conserved, ligand-binding and calcium-coordinating residues, with FireProt-style pairwise compatibility filtering and a diversity-preserving beam search assembling multi-point mutants at depths of 2, 4, 6 and 8 substitutions; and precursor-binder affinity via an adapted LASErMPNN neural-proofreading strategy, saturating point mutations within 5 Angstrom of the ligand, averaging probabilities across decoding orders and dropout to reduce sensitivity to individual predictions, ranking by delta-NLL = ln[P(a)/P(b)], and filtering out buried polar residues introduced without a suitable hydrogen bond.

**datascience.** The genuinely unusual thing here is that the team treat their own scoring metrics as hypotheses to be tested against wet-lab data, and publish the result honestly even when it undermines them. Of 22 planned binders (11 per design tool), 9 were tested; 4 of 9 significantly reduced 3M3SH production, and 4 of 5 transporter binders did, with a maximum 21% reduction. Correlating metric against outcome gave a route-dependent answer: in the RFdiffusion3 branch the interface metrics agreed with experiment and all three MD metrics (MM/GBSA delta-G, and the mean and SD of ligand RMSD over 10-50 ns) showed the expected trend, while in the Proteina-Complexa branch the custom composite score correlated best (Pearson r = 0.76, Spearman rho = 0.60) but the MD metrics did NOT agree — and the team propose a specific mechanistic reason, that RF3 (a diffusion model, like RoseTTAFold3) may predict Proteina-Complexa outputs (partially latent flow matching) less accurately, so ligand RMSD may partly measure relaxation of a poor predicted pose rather than true instability. For the transporter binders they draw the sharper statistical lesson: 'in a filtered set of candidates, a single metric may have too little variation to support confident prediction of actual experimental performance' — i.e. gating on a metric destroys the variance you would need to validate it. They state plainly that the small candidate set 'cannot establish statistically significant relationships', that the results 'cannot concretely verify the usefulness of the single metrics and the weighted metrics we set', and they name the fixes: more independent MD runs, explicit entropy correction, an implicit membrane model in the free-energy calculation, a second folding tool such as AlphaFold, and larger datasets to recalibrate weights. The thermostability work produced a real, interpretable result in both directions: for the T370R/F183W parent, WR2, WR4 and WR8 all improved over the parent with WR8 best, suggesting SPURS (trained on pairwise mutagenesis data) can learn patterns that extrapolate to multi-point mutants and that the design introduced beneficial epistasis; but for the T370K parent only KR2 improved and the higher-order mutants did not, which the team diagnose as the beam search's path dependence — an ineffective mutation introduced at depth 4 is inherited by every deeper mutant. They are equally candid about build failures: the intended T370K mutant came back as T370L, so only T370R/F183W was tested as designed and the rational-design hypothesis is 'not fully verified because of the limited dataset'.

**dataviz.** Structural figures are used as arguments rather than decoration. The inward- versus outward-facing PepTSh comparison is drawn as four aligned panels — the inward structure, a close-up of its intact electrostatic network with dashed contacts and named residues, the outward homology model, and the same close-up showing those contacts broken — so the reader can see for themselves why the inward state is the one worth stabilising, with consistent colouring (green C-terminal bundle, blue N-terminal bundle, orange TMA/TMB) carried across every panel. The target interface is then shown three ways: the region highlighted on the whole structure, a side view with the extracellular direction arrowed, and a close-up with hotspot residues in orange bordering a green hydrophobic patch. The Characterize stage and the funnel-shaped decision-gated workflow are each drawn as schematics, the funnel visibly narrowing through each evaluation gate. MD trajectories are embedded as videos for all three systems. Most valuable of all, Figures 7 and 11 plot computational metric against experimental outcome — A412 signal reduction, calculated as 100 x (1 - mean binder A412 / mean control A412) — with each tested binder as a point, OLS regression lines, and both Pearson r and Spearman rho reported, separately for the two design routes. Every caption gives the n (n = 4 for RFdiffusion3, n = 5 for Proteina-Complexa and for transporter binders) and the full composite-score formula with its weights written out, so the figure can be re-derived. Assay figures carry error bars (+/- SD, n = 3) with significance asterisks defined.

**software.** FoundryUI, a node-based visual programming workbench for de novo protein design, explicitly inspired by ComfyUI (and by Blender and GameMaker as precedents for making technical workflows accessible). It wraps four Rosetta Foundry tools — RFdiffusion3, RoseTTAFold3, ProteinMPNN and LigandMPNN — as connectable nodes for input, generation, sequence redesign, folding, filtering, visualisation and saving, with typed connections that refuse incompatible links, 3D selectors so residues and atoms can be picked directly off a structure in the GUI rather than typed as indices, and sessions and runs so results survive a dropped connection. It ships pre-built workflows for ligand-binder design, protein-binder design, enzyme design, MPNN sequence design and folding prediction, and reads and writes PDB, FASTA, mmCIF, SMILES, JSON and CSV so outputs stay usable elsewhere. The stated motivation is collaboration as much as accessibility: a command line does not show why a step was chosen or how data moved between stages, whereas a graph does — making a workflow easier to explain, modify and hand to the next team. They tested it by teaching it: FoundryUI was used in a school club education activity so students could approach protein modelling through biological decisions instead of commands. All automation scripts are uploaded as reusable workflows for future iGEM teams.

**ihp.** 46 stakeholder interactions across local and international surveys, potential-customer interviews, expert discussions, industry meetings, written proposals and community seminars, organised into a five-stage framework with stakeholders classified into four groups by how they affect the team and how the team affects them, plus a closing 'Feedback to Future' section that explains how they decided which feedback to prioritise and revisited stakeholders to reflect. The clearest evidence that the integration was real is that it changed the project's own name: they started with 'Expelliodor — Expel the Odor', then, prompted by social scientists on stigma, asked whether 'expel' implied that odour is something everyone should eliminate, and why axillary odour should be judged differently from hair or eye colour. They concluded that underarm odour is a natural physiological trait rather than a flaw to be corrected and that managing it should be a matter of choice, and changed the slogan to 'Expel the Odor, on Your Terms' — keeping the scientific goal while adding personal autonomy. Medical experts pushed safety, industry professionals pushed real-world feasibility, and the whole design philosophy of not broadly suppressing skin bacteria or blocking sweat glands follows from that engagement.

**publicEngagement.** Inclusivity Award winner, and the work is built on a framework (LIFT+: Learn, Intervene, Feedback, Transfer, Beyond) with six named target groups reachable in China who face barriers to synthetic biology — the blind community, the Deaf community, children on the autism spectrum, people from low socioeconomic backgrounds, modelling beginners, and older adults with limited formal education. Each group is introduced by a real scientist from that community paired with a sourced statistic: Wanda Diaz Merced, the blind astrophysicist who pioneered sonification of astronomical data, alongside the finding that only 2.1% of blind children globally have access to specialised education services; Temple Grandin alongside the 14.95% four-year-college enrolment rate for individuals with autism; Derek Braun, the deaf geneticist who built Gallaudet's first molecular genetics laboratory, alongside the ~80% of school-age deaf children out of school in low- and middle-income countries; Gabriel Reyes, founder of FLi Sci, alongside OECD data that 37% of disadvantaged students are low performers in science versus 12% of advantaged; and Jia Lanpo, the Zhoukoudian paleoanthropologist who had only a high school education, alongside the 17-point generational gap in tertiary education between adults aged 55-64 and 25-34. Deliverables include 20 tactile biology graphics covering 20 topics across 5 categories for the blind community, and — connecting directly to their dry lab — FoundryUI used as the teaching vehicle for computational protein design beginners. The page itself has an interactive animated version and a text-based alternative, which is the inclusivity principle applied to their own wiki.

**realWorld.** The entrepreneurship case is grounded in population genetics rather than vague market size: the ABCC11 odour-associated allele occurs at roughly 99.99% in African, 97.48% in European, 96.05% in Oceanian, 92.42% in American, 62.22% in Southern Asian and 21.54% in Eastern Asian populations, so even in East Asia where it is least common the absolute population means tens of millions may be affected — and limited public awareness compounds misunderstanding, stigma and discrimination. The team position Expelliodor against the actual failure modes of existing products (masking fragrances, aluminium-salt antiperspirants that suppress perspiration, and broad antibacterials that disturb the axillary microbiome) and argue their three strategies are complementary in time: the precursor binder captures what is already there, CGTase continuously modifies newly secreted precursor, and the transporter binder blocks uptake. CGTase thermostability optimisation was undertaken specifically for industrial production and transportation, which is why heat resistance during storage was a design objective at all.

**For GEMS:** Add a Characterize stage before Design: write down the biological mechanism, the exact target and the application environment, and turn them into an explicit design specification that becomes the literal input to your tool — GreatBay's specification to use the (S) stereoisomer and verify chirality after generation prevented a whole class of silent AI-design error. Then plot every computational score you used against the wet-lab outcome and report the correlation, including the honest finding that gating on a metric removes the variance you would need to validate it.

### Oxford — NECTAR
Undergrad · United Kingdom · https://2026.igem.wiki/oxford/
NECTAR is a programmable RNAi pipeline: FORAGER (computational dsRNA design with off-target screening against the Apis mellifera transcriptome), microbial production in yeast, and delivery to hives in a pollen patty. Varroa destructor, the single biggest threat to honeybees, is the first real-world case study. The team built HIVE, an explicit four-step human-practices decision procedure (Hear, Investigate, Verdict, Evaluate) run over six open project questions with 28+ named stakeholders including US EPA/FDA/USDA staff, the Chair of the UK Advisory Committee on Releases to the Environment, and the Secretariat of the Convention on Biological Diversity. Stakeholder evidence changed the chassis (living engineered Snodgrassella alvi to heat-inactivated yeast), the delivery format, the off-target screening stage, the survey instrument and the definition of success.

**frameworks.** FORAGER, a three-stage standardised dsRNA design pipeline: target gene identification (most abundant transcripts of well-connected genes, weighted by known Varroa RNAi data), within-gene region selection (endogenous Varroa siRNA sequence features, guide competence, RNAplfold target accessibility, combined as three equally weighted complementary evidence layers rather than one fused score), and off-target analysis. Also a BEEHAVE-based colony population model and a bespoke partial-equilibrium economic model.

**datascience.** Construction of a clean Varroa destructor small-RNA dataset from public sequencing, basic population feature analysis of that sRNA pool, sequence feature analysis, whole-region homology and local exact-match screening against the honeybee transcriptome (16-nt strict mapping plus relaxed whole-region similarity), BLAST-based non-target screening, and a documented limitations table stating that the three evidence layers are equally weighted only because no Varroa RNAi efficacy data existed to fit weights.

**dataviz.** Hand-drawn mechanism illustrations throughout (FORAGER stages, the five-step path of a dose through the hive, the SDG goal map), a geocoded stakeholder map with latitude/longitude per interviewee, and per-cycle engineering tables; the wiki is a custom React/Astro-style build with light and dark themes.

**software.** FORAGER is released with one file per stage and a documented frontmatter/body contract so other teams can re-run it; the HIVE method and its full interview question bank are released under CC BY 4.0. Hive insert and PCR-tube feeding adaptor are downloadable 3D-printable hardware.

**ihp.** Oxford's IHP is the strongest kind: a documented decision procedure with a mandatory 'How we implemented the advice to change NECTAR' field on every one of 28+ interview write-ups, and a rule that 'We considered their feedback is not an implementation'. The largest single change is the chassis. Danny Le Feuvre (CEO, Australian Honey Bee Industry Council) and Mike Allerton (VP and Biosecurity Officer, Amateur Beekeepers Australia) both preferred a persistent living engineered Snodgrassella alvi gut symbiont because it minimises beekeeper labour; the team did not simply follow them but took the question to regulators, and Laura Bowden (GM manager, Science and Advice for Scottish Agriculture), Elizabeth Frost (NSW Department of Primary Industries), Tom Hartley (Senior Certification Officer, Soil Association Certification) and the Scottish Government Honey Bee Health Team pushed the opposite way, so the team switched to heat-inactivated, dried engineered yeast and stated plainly what that cost: the persistence that made S. alvi attractive, meaning repeat dosing and more beekeeper labour, against the preference of beekeepers they had interviewed. Austein McLoughlin of the Convention on Biological Diversity Secretariat then confirmed the inactivated product is not a living modified organism under the Cartagena Protocol, but also refused to let the team stop at SDG alignment, pushing them to ask whether NECTAR produces 'measurable improvement' - which is why the sustainability analysis widened to the whole NECTAR lifecycle and built baseline comparisons into the modelling. A joint meeting with Mike Mendelsohn and Alan Reynolds (US EPA), Adam Moyer and Laura Epstein (FDA) and Alan Pearson (USDA) then 'prevented us from treating our shift to heat-inactivated yeast as a universal regulatory shortcut', forcing jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction regulatory mapping instead of one global classification. The deepest economic chain runs through Prof. Wally Thurman (Agricultural and Resource Economics, NC State, interviewed 29 July 2026) and Prof. Brittney Goodrich (Agricultural and Consumer Economics, Illinois, 7 August 2026): Thurman set five methodological commitments (start from an average commercial operation not an industry aggregate; use existing treatments as the counterfactual; assess costs and revenues not survival rates; use simple partial equilibrium; restrict to paid pollination markets), and Goodrich's operation-level cost structure redefined the cost of Varroa to include labour, colony replacement and lost honey and pollination revenue rather than just the price of acaricide. The team then ran the chain backwards - what a beekeeper can afford, to allowable cost per dose, to allowable manufacturing cost, to required mass of intact dsRNA per gram of dry yeast - converting 'high expression' into a pass/fail wet-lab specification of 0.005 mg dsRNA per g yeast for US viability and 0.05 mg/g for both markets, against a fermentation cost of about 2.33 USD per gram. They also deliberately recruited dissent: the Oxfordshire Natural Beekeeping Group (about 20 chemical-free hobbyists) and treatment-free beekeeper Mark Sandham argued that treating removes the selection pressure that would produce tolerant bees, an argument against the entire premise; rather than abandoning the project the team narrowed its target user to commercial operations and wrote that OxNatBees changed 'not the molecular mechanism of NECTAR, but the problem we believed NECTAR should - and should not - try to solve'. Smaller but equally traceable: Lord John Krebs (first FSA Chairman) and Prof. Jim Dunwell (Chair, ACRE) made environmental fate and off-target effects explicit engineering requirements, moving non-target organisms into the FORAGER off-target screening stage and adding in vivo dsRNA-persistence experiments; Prof. Paul Lam (environmental chemistry, Hong Kong Metropolitan University) drove the adoption of BLAST off-target screening and reframed public engagement as risk management rather than promotion; Dr Michael Morrison (HeLEX, Oxford Law) rewrote the survey instrument so it asked separately about pollen patties, constitutively active engineered bacteria and inducible engineered bacteria rather than about 'GMOs' in general; Dr Théotime Colin's point about secondary pests prompted dsRNA constructs for wax moth and small hive beetle; Prof. Giles Budge's reassurance kept the adult-bee oral delivery route alive and produced the 300/500/700 bp length comparison; and Melanie Teece (Head of Technical, Hilltop Honey) and Wade Ford (Hive & Wellness) turned honey purity into a reason for additional in vivo work. The published HIVE guide names its own failure modes (interviewing agreeable people, treating 'the public' as one stakeholder, letting the Verdict drift into a summary, consulting regulators too late to change anything) and requires every Verdict to state what was decided, what was rejected and what that cost.

**publicEngagement.** Buzz In, a three-episode stakeholder podcast built deliberately to put stakeholders who disagreed with each other into contact rather than collecting views in isolation: episode 1 paired Varroa-resistance academic Prof. Stephen Martin with commercial beekeeper Paul Horton on whether to treat at all; episode 2 brought together the CEO of the Australian Honey Bee Industry Council, Amateur Beekeepers Australia and Hive & Wellness; episode 3 set the project against social, environmental and economic lenses with a social scientist, a bee researcher and an agricultural economist. GMO 101, a joint Zoom workshop with NYU Abu Dhabi iGEM on 8 October 2026, measured participation through Nearpod (24 participants, 83% took part). A beekeeper survey received a favourable opinion from a subcommittee of the Oxford Central University Research Ethics Committee (ref MS IDREC 3973787), with public task as the lawful basis and informed consent before questions; 100+ respondents, 63% reported struggling with Varroa at mean severity 5.74/10 and 70% said they would be open to a GMO-based treatment. School sessions at St Clare's summer course were run as a two-way choice exercise (present two delivery routes with honest trade-offs, ask which students would accept, measure the acceptance shift before and after) rather than a lecture. Plus street interviews, a bee campaign, Instagram and TikTok.

**realWorld.** The need is framed with numbers rather than adjectives: Varroa is an invasive alien species across most of its range and the most serious pest of the western honeybee; Australia's failed eradication attempt cost A$101 million and destroyed about 30,000 hives, and surveyed US commercial operations lost around 62% of colonies in 2024-25, estimated at over $600 million. SDGs are chosen, not collected: 15 (Life on Land) and 2 (Zero Hunger) are the primary goals with 17 and 4 as enabling goals, each mapped to named sub-targets (15.8 on invasive alien species is the headline, plus 15.1, 15.5, 15.9), and the analysis extends into the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework targets 7, 10, 11 and 17 at the CBD Secretariat's suggestion. The team then writes a dedicated negative-impacts section on goal conflicts - accessibility across economic status, pollution, ecological threat, and whether healthier managed colonies put pressure on wild pollinators (goal 15 against goal 2) - and admits an unresolved contradiction: stakeholders insisted cost was decisive while 48% of their own survey respondents ranked cost least important, with the honest line 'We have not resolved this'. Deployment rides on existing practice (dsRNA-bearing heat-killed yeast in a conventional pollen patty laid over the frames, plus a 3D-printable hive insert), the regulatory path is mapped per jurisdiction after the EPA/FDA/USDA conversation, and the cost model gives both a per-colony net private benefit and the titre threshold manufacturing must hit. They are unusually candid about what is not demonstrated: no dsRNA titre was measured against the model thresholds, the yeast could not be cloned and the E. coli route gave no detectable dsRNA, so 'this is a case for the approach, not a demonstration of the product'. Handover material - FORAGER, the HIVE cycle and question bank, the bee research guide, protocols and hardware files - is released CC BY 4.0 for future teams.

**For GEMS:** Make the write-up template itself enforce integration: every stakeholder record must carry a 'what this changed' field, and every verdict must name what was decided, what was rejected and what that cost - then run the affordability chain backwards from what the user can pay to a numerical pass/fail specification for the bench.

### BGI-College — BioH2
High School · China · https://2026.igem.wiki/bgi-college/
BGI-College took Clostridium beijerinckii S63, a strain newly isolated from sediment at Yundonghai Wetland Park in Foshan, Guangdong (a site of interest because of unusually high natural soil hydrogen in the Sanshui Basin), and turned a non-model anaerobe into a working chassis. They sequenced it to a single circular 5,870,246 bp chromosome, measured 40.20 plus or minus 3.45 percent hydrogen in its gas output, built a metabolic flux model that identified PFOR and HydA overexpression plus thl deletion as targets, and established an electroporation transformation system through three documented DBTL cycles, two of which failed outright. Their economic check then did something unusual: it proved their own original premise impossible, since breaking even on glucose alone would need 6.70 mol H2 per mol glucose against a hard biochemical ceiling of 4.0, which forced a redesign around byproduct valorisation. They won Best Alternative Platform in the High School section and were nominated for Best New Basic Part and Best Presentation.

**frameworks.** Explicit DBTL cycles used as the organising structure for platform development, each written as Design, Build and Test, then Learn, with the failed cycles kept in place. A metabolic flux framework integrating pathway stoichiometry, carbon allocation and electron transfer, released with a visual interface so non-modellers can use it. Hydrogen pathways benchmarked in a four-way comparison table (grey, blue, green, bio-green) on carbon footprint, levelised cost, supply-chain risk and commercial status.

**datascience.** The modelling is used as a decision tool, not decoration: it put theoretical yield at 2.46 mol H2/mol glucose for wild type rising to 3.60 under an idealised engineered scenario, and the HPLC product profile (acetate and butyrate dominant, little lactate) is what selected thl as the deletion target rather than a generic guess. The economic model is the standout piece of quantitative reasoning: industrial glucose at about 3,000 RMB per tonne against hydrogen at 40 RMB per kg requires 6.70 mol H2 per mol glucose to cover feedstock alone, which exceeds the 4.0 mol theoretical maximum of dark fermentation, so a hydrogen-only business is arithmetically impossible. Genome work includes ANI above 98 percent against C. beijerinckii DSM 791 (GCF_018223745.1), phylogenetic placement, whole-genome alignment and VFDB virulence screening, published as a separate PDF.

**dataviz.** Baseline versus engineered model runs shown side by side so the predicted yield change is legible, the full electroporation workflow drawn as a process diagram with voltages and buffers labelled, a parameter-sweep figure for the optimisation attempts, and, notably, photographs of the empty selective plates from the failed transformations alongside the successful ones. Field photographs of the wetland sampling site locate the strain in a real place.

**software.** A visual interface over the metabolic flux model, built explicitly to lower the barrier for researchers who do not routinely do computational modelling.

**ihp.** Human practices was run as a test of the project's core assumption rather than as outreach. They consulted academic researchers and industrial practitioners including engineers at China General Nuclear Power (CGN), and report the difference in how the two groups framed the problem: academics asked whether the pathway was technically feasible and rigorous, industry asked what it would cost and whether it would scale. Industry input on hydrogen's transport and storage barriers, combined with their own break-even arithmetic, is what turned a hydrogen-only project into a closed-loop biorefinery. A second consultation was decisive technically: after two failed DBTL cycles, Dr. Youduo Wu of Dalian University of Technology told them to reconsider anaerobic handling across the whole workflow rather than keep tuning electroporation parameters, which led them to move the electroporator inside the anaerobic chamber and finally obtain transformants.

**realWorld.** Three things here are worth copying, and the honesty running through all of them is the reason the platform is credible. First, the economics. Their break-even calculation is the single most useful piece of commercialisation reasoning in this cohort precisely because it falsifies their own premise: at roughly 3,000 RMB per tonne of industrial glucose and 40 RMB per kg of hydrogen, covering only the sugar feed needs 6.70 mol H2 per mol glucose, while dark fermentation cannot exceed 4.0 mol, so no amount of strain improvement makes a hydrogen-only product profitable. They state that plainly and redesign rather than hedge. The replacement model is coherent: HPLC confirmed the broth still holds organic acids after hydrogen evolution stops, so instead of paying for chemical waste disposal they use the spent broth as a free substrate to grow commercial Bacillus subtilis and sell it as a liquid biofertiliser, a secondary revenue stream that offsets the feedstock cost and sidesteps hydrogen storage and transport entirely. Note what is and is not claimed: they say the biofertiliser revenue 'substantially offsets' feedstock cost when scaled against raw material inputs, but publish no kit price, no biofertiliser price, no yield per litre of broth and no full P&L, so the loop is a validated concept with the unit economics still missing. There is no company, no patent and no investor. Second, the platform. What makes S63 genuinely reusable by other groups is that they published the route in, not just the destination: the full electroporation workflow with buffers, voltage and cuvette gap specified, the parameter sweep they tried (OD600 0.2 to 1.0, 600 to 1800 V, 100 to 400 microlitres, 1 and 2 mm cuvettes at fixed 200 ohms and 25 microfarads), photographs of the blank plates from both failed cycles, and the one change that actually worked. They also record a failure that did not resolve, stating that the Thl-targeting editing plasmid could not be assembled even though all four fragments amplified and sequenced correctly. Fifteen basic parts were cloned from S63 as native promoter plus CDS plus terminator triples across three HydA and two PFOR genes, which is the right format for a non-model host where heterologous regulatory elements may not work. The genome is published as a separate annotated report. And they label the limits precisely: the transformation system is 'an early-stage platform, rather than a fully optimised or universally reliable protocol', the model 'is not a validated predictor of experimentally achieved hydrogen production', and the oxygen hypothesis 'needs further controlled experiments' to confirm its specific contribution. Third, the safety reasoning, which is more sophisticated than most undergraduate work. The chassis was changed from C. butyricum to C. beijerinckii during an early safety review to avoid strain-dependent pathogenicity risk; they explicitly refuse to let a species-level BSL-1 classification (ATCC 35702) transfer to their own isolate, and instead confirm identity by ANI and phylogeny and screen against VFDB, while recording the correct caveat that a database match does not by itself show a functional virulence factor and that several hits were partial or low-coverage. They are candid that as high-school students they depend on instructors for safety decisions and authorised tasks, do not adjust gas-supply settings or gas-line connections themselves, and they report that three students failed the safety assessment on first attempt and had to re-sit before the team reached a 100 percent pass rate. Continuation is framed as community reuse: the model, the parts, the transformation protocol and the troubleshooting record are offered so that future dark-fermentation teams 'reuse our rationales, protocols, and lessons rather than repeat them'.

**For GEMS:** Run the break-even arithmetic against the biochemical ceiling before committing a year of lab work: BGI-College showed a hydrogen-only product needs 6.70 mol H2 per mol glucose while dark fermentation caps at 4.0, which killed their premise early and forced a byproduct-valorisation design that actually closes. And when publishing a platform for a non-model chassis, publish the failed cycles too — the parameter sweep that did nothing, the photographs of blank plates, the plasmid that would never assemble — because the route in is what another lab needs, not the destination.

### CAU-China — Fungal Sentinel, with the OptiX phone spectrometer
Undergrad · China · https://2026.igem.wiki/cau-china/
CAU-China built Fungal Sentinel, engineered yeast that senses mould volatiles such as 1-octen-3-ol through a GPCR and reports them as fluorescence, and then built the instrument to read it where the mould actually is. OptiX is a pocket spectrometer that uses the phone's own camera as the detector: a threaded interchangeable excitation source, a sample chamber with light-trap fins, a collection module, a frosted-glass slit, a transmission grating, and two USB-C reference lamps that calibrate wavelength and spectral response per device. The software is two programs implementing one written specification, a Python reference implementation and an Android deployment client, held together by a parity test suite that enforces numerical agreement between them. The result is quantitative fluorescence with a limit of detection of 0.81 nM purified EGFP on an early build with no emission filter.

**frameworks.** Five explicit hardware DBTL cycles, each stated as a bottleneck that the previous cycle exposed: separate wavelengths, reject excitation, calibrate wavelengths, block ambient light, collect fluorescence. The software is organised as one shared specification implemented twice, with a parity suite that holds the Python and Android implementations to identical expectations on the algorithms they share, so that a field result and a desk result are the same number rather than two approximations of it. Every validation result is accompanied by its limitations.

**datascience.** This is an unusually complete instrument-to-number pipeline. Raw pixel values are first made physical: exposure time is read from TIFF/EXIF tag 33434 and the sensor black level from DNG tag 50714, and the frame is normalised to (raw minus black level) over exposure time, so what leaves the first stage is proportional to a photon flux rate rather than to brightness. Wavelength calibration is two-point by design and validated on a held-out channel: blue and red LED peaks fit a linear pixel-to-wavelength model, the green peak at a nominal 522.5 nm is deliberately excluded from the fit and used only to turn a pixel residual into a wavelength error (reported as +15.3 px, i.e. +5.57 nm), with quality grades of PASS at 2.5 nm or better, WARNING to 10 nm and FAILED beyond, and a FAILED calibration blocking downstream steps unless explicitly overridden. Peaks are located inside valley-bounded windows and refined by a log-parabola vertex fit accepted only if the curvature is negative and the vertex falls inside the window, with a half-height edge midpoint as fallback, windows containing multiple local maxima tagged suspect, and the legacy intensity-weighted centroid still reported as a diagnostic so a reviewer can see how much the estimator choice mattered. Spectral response is measured per channel against a NICHIA white LED whose spectral power distribution the manufacturer publishes, inside a dual mask restricting the estimate to wavelengths both inside the usable 430 to 660 nm band and lit strongly enough, and the team deliberately does not smooth the response curves (smoothing fabricates detail the sensor never measured, exactly where the response is least trustworthy) and does not normalise them to each other (that would destroy the relative magnitudes that say which channel to trust where). Order of operations is enforced rather than suggested: blank subtraction is additive and clipped at zero before averaging so a noisy blank cannot produce a negative spectrum, then response division is applied only where the response exceeds 20% of its maximum and reported as zero elsewhere, because dividing before subtracting would multiply the background up as well. Spikes are removed by a local median-absolute-deviation test with a 2% amplitude floor so the filter does not fire on flat regions. Quantification uses spectral unmixing rather than band integration: the sample spectrum is fitted pointwise over an emission window as a linear combination of the measured reference emission shape (taken as the highest standard minus its own blank, on this instrument, not an idealised literature spectrum), the measured blank carrying scatter and Raman structure, and a constant offset, solved by ordinary least squares, with the metric being the fitted coefficient times the area under the reference emission. Because scatter and offset are fitted out before integration, the background no longer sets the detection floor, and with scattered excitation about 100 times stronger than EGFP emission at the lowest levels the unmixing gives a limit of detection ten times lower than blank subtraction alone (0.81 nM versus 7.8 nM). Three safeguards are built around it: automatic and auditable reference selection with a diagnostic naming every candidate's in-window area, a window that starts just beyond the measured scatter peak rather than a fixed symmetric band, and a t-test on the calibration slope (t below 3 is reported as not significant with the LoD and LoQ flagged unreliable rather than printed). Detection limits follow the IUPAC convention from the residual standard deviation of the fitted curve, LoD = 3.3 s_yx / slope and LoQ = 10 s_yx / slope, with weighted regression supported for the heteroscedastic, approximately Poisson character of fluorescence data, and the reported LoD taken from the lowest exposure block whose slope is significant with that provenance printed beside it. Saved calibration curves are re-fitted on import and rejected if the stored slope or intercept do not reproduce, so a hand-edited preset cannot silently change a result. Validation covers accuracy and dynamic range (0.81 nM LoD, linear 6.6 to 1684 nM, recovery 80 to 120%), EGFP in living yeast, mCherry in E. coli, OD600 against a bench spectrophotometer (R2 0.994, slope 1.02), absorbance spectra matched against a Nanodrop, and stability over 27 minutes at 0.30% coefficient of variation with all 14 stability criteria passed. Limitations are published alongside: the lowest standard was still detected so the LoD is extrapolated, and long 16-second exposures read lower than short ones for reasons not yet resolved.

**dataviz.** An interactive light-path simulation in which the reader drags a spectrum to trace a chosen wavelength through the instrument; an exploded CAD view with numbered, selectable components; row-wise intensity profiles of the three Bayer channels inside the automatically detected spectral band with dynamic peak windows shaded and fitted centroids marked, plotted against a converted wavelength axis; held-out-point calibration residual plots; per-channel absolute response curves inside a dual mask with the response-proportional fusion weights shown as a partition of unity and the channel crossover wavelengths labelled; standard curves with insets marking the limit of detection as a dashed line and the limit of quantification as dotted.

**software.** FSSA (Fungal Sentinel Spectral Analyzer), a Python desktop reference implementation requiring Python 3.10 or later with numpy, scipy, matplotlib and tifffile, with pytest for the test suite and no network access at any stage; MycoSpec, the Kotlin Android client built on Camera2 RAW that reimplements the validated pipeline natively so a RAW-capable phone performs the whole analysis on device; and a CSV Data Cleaner that prepares lamp spectral power distributions from plot-digitised datasheet points, clipping negatives, dropping duplicate wavelengths and resampling onto a 1 nm grid using shape-preserving PCHIP interpolation specifically because a natural cubic spline would overshoot and invent emission structure that is not in the datasheet. Both programs are released under the Apache License 2.0, on GitHub (github.com/LittleSky-CN/Fungal-Sentinel-Spectral-Analyzer and github.com/LittleSky-CN/Mycospec) and mirrored on iGEM GitLab (gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/cau-china/). The instrument itself is modelled and rendered from a Fusion 360 assembly, and the team cites the open-source smartphone spectrophotometer literature it builds on.

**ihp.** Integrated Human Practices is organised through an F-Ring model with four stakeholder groups (Fungal, Feasibility, Field, Future) and a Focus-Finding-Feedback conversation structure, with each conversation routed back into the DBTL cycle. The project's origin is a reported need rather than an assumed one: students in Science and Technology Backyards in Malawi and Zambia described smallholder farmers in remote and resource-limited communities relying on visual inspection because laboratory testing is too costly, large, maintenance-heavy and technically demanding, and missing early-stage or hidden fungal contamination.

**publicEngagement.** An age-inclusive education programme spanning a science summer camp, one-day lectures, science-themed orienteering and community talks, reaching preschool and primary children through to university students and older adults, with biosensor concepts tied to everyday mould-prevention practice and courseware tailored per age group. Every activity and its stakeholder feedback was documented and used to revise the next session.

**realWorld.** The entrepreneurship work treats the device as a product and tests that hypothesis against real users, opening with questions the lab cannot answer: who would own the device, a farmer, a cooperative, a warehouse or an extension station; who keeps it working after the pilot ends and who replaces a broken light source three hundred kilometres from the nearest city; how much a household living on stored grain would pay; and what happens if a farmer receives a warning they cannot act on. The technical case is framed around coverage as much as cost, since fungal contamination in stored maize is unevenly distributed by location, depth and batch, so a method that can only analyse a few transported samples cannot represent the warehouse. The hardware is explicitly dual-purpose, usable as a general pocket spectrophotometer, fluorometer or spectrometer by other teams simply by changing the light source.

**For GEMS:** Write the analysis as a specification first, then implement it twice and hold the two implementations to a parity test suite; and inside that specification, validate the calibration on a point you deliberately held out of the fit, fit the background out of the signal rather than subtracting a band, and refuse to print a detection limit when the calibration slope is not statistically significant.

### TU Darmstadt — UNRAVEL: Unlocking New Resources And Value from End-of-Life textiles
Overgrad · Germany · https://2026.igem.wiki/tu-darmstadt/
TU Darmstadt attacked mixed textile waste, of which roughly 92 million tonnes are generated globally each year and less than 1% is recycled back into fibres, by working with two thermophilic organisms: Acetivibrio thermocellus, a strict anaerobe with a cellulosome that degrades cotton at 60 C, and Geobacillus thermocatenulatus, whose carboxylesterase the team characterised and registered as GeoEsterase. Because those organisms need equipment the team did not have, they built it: a movable DIY anaerobic chamber for under 150 euros, a portable ESP32 oxygen monitor when resazurin proved too slow and cumbersome to verify the atmosphere, and two generations of orbital shaker to fit inside an existing 60 C incubator. What makes the work a measurement case study is the discipline of separating what was demonstrated from what was not, in both the enzymology and the hardware.

**frameworks.** Every hardware page is structured as motivation and design requirements, design decisions, bill of materials and costs, construction instructions, materials-processing lessons, testing, evaluation, limitations and conclusion, with a recurring distinction between what was built, what was tested and what has not yet been demonstrated quantitatively. The same discipline runs through the results page, where computational predictions are labelled as predictions and never presented as measured enzyme performance. The team frames its contribution to iGEM as the designs, methods and troubleshooting lessons for working with non-model organisms, so that later teams do not start from scratch.

**datascience.** Enzyme activity is measured against p-nitrophenyl hexanoate as a soluble stand-in for one of the two ester bonds in PET, with the released 4-nitrophenol quantified by absorbance at 396 nm using a stated extinction coefficient of 18,100 M-1 cm-1 under their conditions, so the readout is anchored to a physical constant rather than left in absorbance units. Conditions are fully specified: 0.5 uM enzyme (0.25 uM for the deep-eutectic-solvent comparison) against 0.5, 1, 2 and 4 mM substrate in 5 C steps around 37 C, every value the mean of a triplicate. The initial rate is defined operationally as the highest rate of product formation between two consecutive reads, identified automatically by their evaluation sheet rather than chosen by eye, and Vmax and KM are then fitted by minimising the sum of squared differences in Excel Solver, with kcat following from Vmax and enzyme concentration. Measurements for which no fit could be established are excluded from the table and the figure and said to be excluded, and one suspect value is flagged twice, at 47 C the Thermo MHETase trace shows a single jump in absorbance shortly after the start, so the team warns that the derived initial rate and the fit containing it should be treated with caution. Every plate's evaluation sheet is published as a PDF with the date, the enzymes, the temperature and the notes, including one where well D12 was excluded for air bubbles, so the chain from raw plate to reported constant is auditable. Thermal stability is measured by thermal shift assay with both enzymes on the same plate under identical conditions (2 uM protein, 5x SYPRO Orange, 1x LEW buffer with 10% glycerol, n = 3), and the negative result is reported with its statistics rather than buried: GeoEsterase 74.54 +/- 0.03 C and Thermo GeoEsterase 74.63 +/- 0.13 C by Boltzmann fit with R2 at least 0.998, a difference of +0.09 C with a 95% confidence interval of -0.21 to +0.40 C and a Welch t-test p of 0.34, from which the team concludes not merely that no improvement was seen but that the interval excludes any stabilisation larger than about 0.4 C. Material identity is verified before use rather than assumed, with ATR-IR on a PerkinElmer FT-IR with MIR TGS detector confirming the nylon is Nylon 6 and the polyester is PET against simulated references, and solvent extraction with methanol and acetone followed by repeat spectra used to test for additives and dyes. Particle sizing produced an honest dead end: cryomilling was optimised by ball diameter (25 mm adopted after 5, 7 and 12 mm failed), recovery across 24 runs ran from 79 to 100% with two same-day replicates at 100 and 79%, which the team reads as powder retained in the jar and funnel rather than as a result, saying explicitly it is not a degradation readout; DLS on a Malvern Zetasizer Nano with the serial number and software version recorded showed none of the samples monodisperse with much of the material above the 10 um measuring range, sonication changed nothing, and the team concluded cryomilling cannot produce the monodisperse dispersions repeatable kinetics need and abandoned the approach in favour of weighed fabric pieces. Microscopy covered the coarse end that DLS cannot reach, 3.1 to 40 um for polyester and 3 to 50 um for nylon, with the caveat that only two samples with few particles were imaged so no distribution can be fitted, plus an incidental warning that polyester autofluoresces without any dye because of optical brighteners, UV stabilisers and degradation products. Computational work is held to the same standard: 51 substitutions across five proteins are reported with the explicit statement that a DeepSTABp-predicted +9.27 C melting-temperature change and a +167% TemStaPro score gain answer different questions and must not be treated as equivalent, that 73% versus 97% binding-pocket residue overlap indicates similar identified residues but does not prove correct substrate positioning or catalytic activity, that a substitution 6.55 angstroms from the catalytic serine is active-site-adjacent and not a mutation of a catalytic residue, and that a 28.2 percentage-point increase in near-serine contact fraction across 100 ns trajectories is geometry, not a measured reaction rate, with the roughly 3.3-fold ester-to-amide contact ratio labelled a simulation-derived geometric comparison and not a change in catalytic specificity.

**dataviz.** Interactive parameter plots for kinetic constants with buttons to switch between kcat, KM and kcat/KM across temperature, and between temperatures on the initial-rate plots, with axes held constant so panels can be compared directly; dashed lines for fitted Michaelis-Menten curves and dotted lines explicitly marking measurements for which no fit could be established, so an unfittable dataset is visible rather than absent; absorbance-against-time traces with the blank subtracted and each trace shown relative to its first read; ATR-IR spectra overlaid against simulated reference spectra; collapsible result sections with open-all and close-all controls; an interactive 3D protein model on the landing page.

**software.** Hardware is released as build documentation rather than code: a full assembly procedure for the anaerobic chamber with bills of materials and per-item recorded costs, a step-by-step oxygen-monitor build with the complete I2C scanner sketch and both the simple and advanced Arduino display programs printed in full on the wiki, a wiring table mapping every OLED and sensor pin to its ESP32 pin, and an orbital shaker build with its own BOM, tool list and assembly steps. Nine 3D models and a seventeen-image gallery accompany the shaker, with bearing specifications listed. Plate-reader evaluation sheets are published per plate as PDFs, including the current version of the sheet with a worked example of the layout and calculation steps.

**ihp.** Human Practices treats textile waste as a humanitarian problem first: rich countries export their waste and the communities that handle it are never the ones who benefited from producing it. The team quantifies the flow, with EU exports of used textiles more than doubling since 2005 to over 1.4 million tonnes in 2025, Germany exporting approximately 462,500 tonnes in 2022 and second only to the USA, an estimated 30 to 40% of German exports ending in landfills in receiving countries, and Chile receiving about 131,000 tonnes in 2022. They also note that only about 15% of the EU's 6.94 million tonnes of textile waste was collected separately, with 85% going into mixed household waste where it can no longer be recycled, and they sought out textile companies and the local collectors, sorters and thrift stores who keep materials in circulation. Their stated position is that responsible science means asking who the work should be for, not only whether it can work.

**publicEngagement.** A sustainability page sets out the environmental case alongside the science, and the project's framing is that recycling is only part of the answer, with buying less and wearing clothes for longer mattering just as much.

**realWorld.** An entrepreneurship page addresses whether biological textile recycling makes economic sense, from cultivation and enzyme production costs to the practical obstacles of bringing the approach out of the laboratory, on the argument that scientific ideas often fail to leave the lab for economic rather than technical reasons. The hardware is the most directly reusable output: the anaerobic chamber is costed at 134.30 euros in materials against roughly 3,000 euros for a cheap professional chamber, a 95% reduction and the cheapest DIY solution the team could find, with the oxygen monitor at 114.60 euros per unit (the sensor being about 83% of that) and the orbital shaker at 68.08 euros. The build guides are written for reproduction, including which parts must be matched to each other, and the team says what it would record differently next time, specifically hole centres, hole diameters, edge distances and fastener lengths, to reduce another team's trial and error.

**For GEMS:** Report a null result with the interval that bounds it: measuring both enzyme variants on the same plate under identical conditions let the team say not just that the engineered variant was no more stable, but that the data exclude any stabilisation larger than about 0.4 C, which is a usable constraint rather than an absence of evidence.

### Tsinghua-T — GALATEA
Undergrad · China · https://2026.igem.wiki/tsinghua-t/
Glabridin is 0.08-0.35% of licorice root dry weight and all three Glycyrrhiza species are on China's National Key Protected Wild Plants Catalogue, so one gram of the skincare active corresponds to roughly 286-1,250 g of dried root; GALATEA replaces that extraction route with Saccharomyces cerevisiae. The team built tunable protein condensates - an FTH1-24 ferritin iron core as nucleation seed, intrinsically disordered regions, and an SH3/PDZ scaffold at 3:1 recruiting the OC and DMT enzymes - instead of relying on random co-localisation. Their integrated human practices is organised as a four-act loop (Define, Optimize, Calibrate, Echo) in which each act must produce a change, and the loop closes by returning the engineering improvements to the same 96 street respondents for re-validation. Advice from Tsinghua chemical engineering professors reordered the biosynthetic pathway itself, and seven company visits rewrote the project's definition of success.

**frameworks.** A six-module dry-lab pipeline run over four engineering rounds: M0 evidence collection, M1 sequence-level screening, M2 structural and assembly screening, M3 enzyme recruitment and partitioning, M4 pathway kinetics, M5 experimental comparison. Every module states explicitly what a negative screen does NOT establish (for example, 'M1 flags sequence and topology risks for structural follow-up; a negative screen does not establish enzyme activity or scaffold assembly'). Outputs were deliberately changed from a single yield prediction to 'recommended conditions + sensitivity ranking + uncertainty interval + failure criteria'.

**datascience.** A 1,397-DOI literature analysis, a 16-compound computational safety screen against a fixed skincare reference panel, and a three-tier evidence table (Production, Skin Health, Safety) in which each entry records the experimental system, concentration range, source and evidence grade. Sequence screening uses IUPred2A disorder, SignalP, DeepTMHMM, PSIPRED, net charge per residue and mean hydropathy; all external data on the wiki carry source and experimental-condition labels, with literature values visually separated from the team's own measurements.

**dataviz.** A before/after paired bar chart of the same 96 street respondents' judgments; a stakeholder-by-theme emphasis matrix (eight engagement records x five themes, graded not highlighted / mentioned / discussed in depth); an interview coding grid (seven participants x five themes); consumer-needs and technical-concerns word clouds; a three-stage deployment-path diagram; and a two-column 'Measured Results / Next-Step Validations' format applied to every presentation slide.

**software.** GALATEA-Caelum, an integrated platform combining a literature-retrieval algorithm with an Agent harness that turns a researcher's prompt plus registered tools into a reviewable dry-lab plan grounded in the project's own wet-lab data. The retrieval algorithm queries OpenAlex, Crossref and Europe PMC, then ranks with BM25 (k1=1.5, b=0.75) plus BAAI/bge-m3 semantic embeddings, fuses with Reciprocal Rank Fusion, deduplicates by Jaccard, diversifies with MMR, rereads the full text of top records to extract numerical parameters, and runs AI-assisted quality evaluation. Built to be reused by future iGEM teams.
