**ihp.** GALATEA states its IHP function in one sentence - 'at each decision point it brings external stakeholders into the process and converts their judgment into concrete changes' - and then shows the conversions. The deepest chain runs through Professor Zheng Liu and Professor Chong Zhang of Tsinghua's Department of Chemical Engineering, who were shown the team's initial plan of directly fusing enzymes and relying on random co-localisation. They made three objections: random co-localisation cannot stop intermediates diffusing away before reaching the next enzyme; the DMT enzyme has high substrate promiscuity and poor selectivity, with a reported extracellular fraction of the intermediate demethylvestitol of 88.4 +/- 4.2%; and OC is hydrophobic, so it can be recruited into relatively hydrophobic droplets, and since OC is the rate-limiting step the OC:DMT ratio is the lever. The team changed four things: they replaced direct fusion with a tunable FTH1-24 ferritin-seeded scaffold plus IDR condensate and SH3/PDZ recruitment at 3:1 that keeps local OC concentration above DMT; they moved the DMT demethylation step to the very end of the biosynthetic pathway so promiscuity cannot contaminate intermediate steps; they expanded readouts from 'final yield only' to product identity, purity, intra- and extracellular intermediates, by-products, batch-to-batch stability and functional relevance; and they embedded red and green fluorescent markers in the scaffold so droplet formation and enzyme co-localisation are observed under the microscope rather than inferred. That is a stakeholder conversation changing the reaction order of a metabolic pathway. The seven company visits, sampled deliberately across supply-chain roles (Blue-Peptides and INNOBIO upstream in Dalian; WuXi Biologics and Zerun Biotech as CDMO in Shanghai; CHANDO Beauty Science City and Guyu Beauty as end brands in Guangzhou; IMEIK against medical-device standards in Beijing), were run with the same four questions each time, and each produced a specific change: Blue-Peptides' line that 'an unrepeatable yield figure equals zero in industry' added a batch-to-batch variation column to the experimental records; WuXi Biologics' thresholds of purity >= 95% and +/- 5% batch variation went into the wet-lab detection items; CHANDO's raw-material gate (efficacy, safety, cost and supply stability all must pass) and Guyu's four-document procurement logic split efficacy evidence into in vitro cellular and formulation tiers so in vitro results are never presented as efficacy claims; IMEIK's insistence that a complete data package matters more than any single impressive metric produced a data-package checklist consolidating all seven companies' requirements with a tick-box for whether the team currently holds each item. Together these rewrote the judgment chain from 'LLPS works -> leakage falls -> yield rises -> success' to that chain plus product identity and quality evidence plus functional relevance to specific skin problems. NUS professors' critique that partition coefficient, leakage rate, linker flexibility and effective enzyme concentration were implicit and invisible drove the model-output change and the three-tier evidence table. Peer iGEM teams each closed a specific gap: Nanjing Normal University on genomic integration versus plasmid expression to reduce batch variation; Nankai University on platform scope and the scale-up bottleneck, which the team admits they could not answer at the time and then added to the public project description; Beijing Institute of Technology on provenance, pointing out that an unlabelled 88.4% leakage figure would read as the team's own measurement - which is why every external number on the wiki now carries a source label. Conference feedback was treated the same way: NCIM made them split every slide into 'Measured Results' and 'Next-Step Validations'; CCiC's objection that a single leakage percentage without a stated loading ratio is meaningless added the three comparison groups (free enzyme, random co-localisation, LLPS scaffold) and the 1:1 / 1:2 / 2:1 recruitment gradient to the formal protocol; APiC moved the fluorescence co-localisation data out of the appendix and into results; and a question at the Peking-Rice Summit about skin-tone controversy produced the impact-boundary assessment. They also adopted Beijing Institute of Technology's HP process discipline - preparation, execution, review, with a named note-taker per phase - so every visit produced minutes in a fixed format.

**publicEngagement.** Public engagement is built as a measurement instrument rather than a broadcast. Two rounds of street interviews (118 then 96 participants) bracket the engineering work: round one asked 'what do you need', round two revisited the same sites, gave respondents a short questionnaire, showed them the improved plain-language cards and the engineering evidence, then asked the same questions again - acceptance of biosynthetic ingredients rose 54.2% to 78.1%, the belief that a titre number alone is enough to judge success fell 71.9% to 22.9%, and willingness to pay 10% more for traceable production rose 26% to 51%. A 286-response campus questionnaire (18 items, two open-ended) plus 7 young-consumer interviews and 137 Q&A exchanges run with NUS supplied the baseline. Also four on-campus seminars (210 attendees), an offline outreach session at Beijing 101 High School, 23 articles on the WeChat account 'Tanwei iGEMer', two contributed pages in a science-outreach artbook with Rice iGEM, and the organisation of Tsinghua University's first Synthetic Biology Innovation Contest (62 teams from 21 universities).

**realWorld.** The need is quantified at the resource level: 0.08-0.35% glabridin content in licorice root, all three Glycyrrhiza species protected under Chinese law, 286-1,250 g of dried Uzbek root and stolon per gram of product assuming complete recovery, and documented habitat degradation from overharvesting. Only three SDGs are claimed - 3 Good Health and Well-being, 9 Industry Innovation and Infrastructure, 12 Responsible Consumption and Production - and each is tied to a specific question (what makes the ingredient useful, how it should be produced, how materials are used responsibly). Crucially, the sustainability page contains a table mapping each HP concern to its source participant or specialist, to the assessment dimension it created, to what was actually included in the analysis, and to the SDG connection, so the SDG link is derived from stakeholder evidence rather than asserted. The regulatory path is checked item by item against Chinese cosmetic law: spot-fading and whitening claims require human efficacy evaluation trials, naming follows the Cosmetic Classification Rules and Catalogue, biotechnological raw materials fall under YY/T 10001-2026, and new ingredients require registration and filing - from which the team concludes that efficacy claims are their most constrained category because their evidence stops at the in vitro and yeast level, far below what the claim would require. A negative-impacts table lists who is affected, under what conditions, the residual uncertainty and the team's own boundary for three topics including colorism, committing to never rank skin tones by lightness and to use specific skin-problem wording instead. Deployment is staged with a cost target: 1-2 years to prove platform portability to other high-value molecules, 2-3 years to pilot-scale fermentation with dry-lab models recalibrated against the industrial parameters collected on the visits, aiming to bring cost from about RMB 100,000 per kilogram at lab scale to below RMB 30,000, then 3-5 years into cosmetics, traditional Chinese medicine and nutraceuticals via licensing and joint development. Most tellingly, the one thing public communication could not fix is reported unfixed: 56.3% still regarded price as a major barrier after seeing the cards, so the team wrote price back into the Part 3 cost targets 'unchanged' and added 'efficacy claims running ahead of evidence' to its red lines for future communication.

**For GEMS:** Close the loop by measuring it: take the engineering changes stakeholder feedback produced back to the same respondents, ask the same questions before and after, and publish the one metric that did not move - then convert industry's hard thresholds into the project's own definition of a successful design, so a higher titre alone can no longer count as success.

### William-and-Mary — BROKEN: Building Resilient Optimized Engineered Networks
Undergrad · United States · https://2026.igem.wiki/william-and-mary/
William & Mary argued that synthetic biology measures whether a circuit works and almost never measures how long it keeps working. BROKEN therefore ran longitudinal experiments on four previously engineered circuits in laboratory cultures and in seawater microcosms, following them through serial passaging to deterioration rather than stopping at initial success. The team paired functional readouts (OD600, beta-carotene production, GFP, biofilm morphology, starch hydrolysis, colony-forming units) with molecular verification (PCR, restriction digests, gels, NanoDrop) and with multi-omics (RNA-seq, genomic DNA sequencing, long-read plasmid sequencing), then built mechanistic ODE models and machine-learning approaches to predict time to failure. The reliability framing came directly from Integrated Human Practices and turned safety into the project's central motivation, which is reflected in its Safety and Security Award.

**frameworks.** A stated measurement philosophy of multitiered (population, circuit output, viability, DNA integrity, transcription), multimodal (optical, biochemical, microbiological, sequencing) and redundant measurement, with the explicit rationale that a falling fluorescence signal could equally mean circuit dysfunction, reduced growth, altered reporter maturation or changed physiology. An extension of the standard Design-Build-Test-Learn cycle so that engineering does not end at a functioning construct but continues through systematic longevity and failure testing in both laboratory and realistic environmental conditions, with results feeding back into design.

**datascience.** The headline measurement contribution is absolute-style fluorescence calibration: the team prepared concentration series of fluorescein and sulforhodamine 101 in PBS, measured four replicates at each concentration with PBS blanks to assess solvent background, fitted linear regressions of fluorophore concentration against RFU with reported R2 greater than 0.99, and then used published extinction coefficients and quantum yields to estimate conversion factors between the calibration dyes and S65T GFP, mKate2, mCherry and cpGFP, so that plate-reader readings could enter the mathematical models as concentration-like variables instead of instrument-dependent arbitrary units. They state the limitation plainly, that because dye and protein optical properties differ these conversions are estimates contingent on the correction factors. Normalisation is handled explicitly: beta-carotene is reported as A454/OD600 so that per-cell production is separated from cell number, uncontaminated LB is measured as a blank, and OD600 is used both to standardise serial transfers and to interpret every fluorescence comparison. Where optical turbidity cannot answer the biological question, the technique changes: CFU counts are used for kill-switch viability and for thymineless death and rescue, on the advice of Dr Andrei Kuzminov, with plating on thymidine-supplemented medium so that the assay does not itself impose further starvation. Reporter maturation delay was built into measurement timing after Dr Sean Sleight pointed out that a delay in fluorescence is not a delay in transcription. The RNA-seq pipeline is specified end to end: fastp for adapter trimming and quality filtering, SortMeRNA for residual rRNA removal, HISAT2 alignment against combined host-plus-plasmid references built as merged FASTA and GFF files, featureCounts for gene-level assignment and DESeq2 for differential expression; genome assemblies from Plasmidsaurus were annotated with Bakta in Geneious Prime and variant tables exported. Modelling carries uncertainty properly: SciPy least-squares fits of the lambda-repressor model give R2 = 0.82 and chi2/dof = 0.88 at 30 C, and the team reports that the 42 C prediction degrades to R2 = 0.55 with chi2/dof = 7.57, six to eight times worse than the in-sample value and therefore larger than measurement noise explains, rather than presenting the prediction as validated. A light-responsive fit is reported as poor at the assumed error (chi2/dof = 4.7, p = 0.0009) with the specific failure described (the dark curve fits, the light curve is flat then bursts). Because the labelled dataset is tiny (N = 16), model selection uses leave-one-out and leave-one-series-out rather than a train/test split, with benchmarking across OLS, Ridge, Lasso, Elastic Net, random forest and Gaussian process; Ridge on circuit fraction plus stress genes gives leave-one-out R2 = 0.61, and a classifier reaches AUC 0.880 and accuracy 0.830, both reported with the caveat that 16 samples cannot establish a general predictor.

**dataviz.** Longitudinal fluorescence and beta-carotene time-course figures, kill-switch and thymineless-death assay panels, DNA mutation tables for the corrosion-prevention construct, leakiness panels and circuit-expression comparisons across experiments, all numbered as a continuous figure series across the results and measurement pages.

**software.** All modelling and analysis code is published with documentation on the team's iGEM GitLab, with instructions for both terminal use and a web interface. A Guidebook for Circuit Failure Measurement is released as a PDF, offering a tiered approach scaled to a laboratory's budget, from accessible functional assays through molecular diagnostics to sequencing and multi-omics. Longitudinal RNA-seq and DNA-seq datasets are released for the community, paired with functional, growth and viability measurements so that molecular change can be linked to observed performance. The hardware, software, alternative-platform and entrepreneurship wiki pages remain unfilled iGEM templates.

**ihp.** Integrated Human Practices reframed the project three times over. Contributors from aerospace, civil and electrical engineering backgrounds pushed the team to adopt not only the methods of failure engineering but its mindset, that failure should be anticipated and designed for rather than observed after the fact. The most consequential shift was the recognition that circuit failure is a biosafety problem, not a performance problem, which moved safety from a secondary consideration to the central motivation and underpins the team's Safety and Security Award. Technical guidance entered the DBTL cycle directly: Dr Alex Porter pressed the team on the gap between laboratory performance and behaviour under realistic environmental conditions, which produced the seawater microcosm experiments; Dr Sean Sleight raised fluorescent-protein maturation, which changed measurement timing; and Dr Andrei Kuzminov argued that OD600 and fluorescence could not measure survival during thymineless death, which replaced the planned readout with CFU-based viability.

**realWorld.** The project's deliverables are aimed at the field rather than at a product: an open-source set of standard operating protocols written so that someone who was not present can follow them, a tiered Guidebook for Circuit Failure Measurement scaled to different budgets, publicly released longitudinal multi-omics datasets for comparative failure analysis and model validation, and a proposed extension of DBTL that adds systematic longevity and failure testing. The team also models building on previously published circuits rather than treating initial characterisation as an endpoint, and frames kill switches and other safety-critical circuits as the components that most need the failure analysis mature engineering disciplines already apply.

**For GEMS:** Calibrate fluorescence against a dye concentration series before any number leaves the plate reader, and report model fits with chi2/dof against the measurement error rather than R2 alone, so that an out-of-sample prediction that is six times worse than the in-sample fit is visible as a failure instead of being dressed up as a moderate correlation.

### Bist-China — PyrLac Glow
High School · China · https://2026.igem.wiki/bist-china/
PyrLac Glow reads the Warburg effect directly: two allosteric fluorescent biosensors, built by inserting YFP into the transcription regulators PdhR (pyruvate) and LldR (L-lactate), report the concentrations and the ratio of the two metabolites through a dual-lock mechanism. The project targets a specific structural gap in Chinese cancer screening - CT, endoscopy and liquid biopsy are accurate but inaccessible at grassroots level, while conventional serum tumour markers are cheap but not specific enough - with fewer than 10% of patients diagnosed early. The team ran 16 in-depth interviews across clinical practice, research, industry, public health, insurance, education and engineering, plus two questionnaires (208 and 113 valid responses), organised into five sequential stages each answering one question and each closing with a 'What we changed' statement. The biomarker architecture, the product category, the deployment scenarios, the hardware scope, the software permission model and the outreach strategy all changed as a direct result.

**frameworks.** A multi-evidence computational screening workflow to choose YFP insertion breakpoints in each sensor, combining conserved domain annotation, static structural rigidity assessment, physicochemical profiling, molecular docking and molecular dynamics. For PdhR they built a five-feature weighted scoring model that scores and ranks every residue along the full-length sequence, with C-terminal oligomerisation residues included but penalised by steric hindrance and conformational tolerance terms, and high-scoring candidates still requiring manual secondary verification. For LldR they started from experimentally validated insertion hotspots reported in patent CN113004420A rather than scoring blind.

**datascience.** Questionnaire analysis with explicit sampling-bias reporting: 78.37% female respondents, 91.83% urban, income above 20,000 RMB per year, and the team states outright that the sample under-covers rural, low-income and elderly male populations and makes those groups a target for later outreach. Hardware requirement data were gathered in a second, deliberately non-overlapping questionnaire. Apo-to-holo conformational modelling explains the sensing mechanism: hinge flexibility distorts the embedded YFP beta-barrel for low basal fluorescence, and ligand-induced contraction rigidifies the hinge so YFP refolds and fluorescence rises.

**dataviz.** An interactive five-stage IHP architecture diagram with collapsible numbered nodes, a four-group stakeholder classification map (end screening users, clinical practitioners, industry and technical developers, public health and policy regulators) with each group's concerns attached, and a closed-loop summary figure pairing core achievements, key limitations and future plans.

**software.** A modular data processing backbone designed with a former Microsoft vice president: signal acquisition, data buffering, data quality verification, sample labelling, separate processing pipelines for CMOS sensors and photoresistors, data storage and visualisation, with anonymous sample IDs, full retention of both raw and processed data, spreadsheet export at prototype stage, and module decoupling so sensors or verification algorithms can be upgraded without rebuilding the system.

**ihp.** Bist-China's five-stage structure forces each stakeholder round to produce a change, and the changes are substantial rather than cosmetic. The single biggest one is the biomarker architecture: the initial design used lactate alone, and a pathologist at a hospital in Zhuhai, Guangdong told them that many benign physiological fluctuations produce fluorescent signals resembling malignant signatures, so a single-marker assay 'would not be clinically accepted for large-scale pre-screening' - the team abandoned the single-lactate scheme and adopted combined lactate-pyruvate detection, making specificity and anti-interference the primary optimisation goals. Dr Feiran Han (Director of the Institute of Science and Technology, LC-Bio) then confirmed dual-marker feasibility but told them two markers were the right number for a high-school project because a third would dilute validation depth, so they locked the panel at two and built standardised SOPs with replicates and standard curves converting fluorescence into metabolite concentrations. Stage 1 produced a product-category change: cancer survivors described the 1-2 year early warning window missed through fear of positive results, and oncologist Dr Wu Qing explained that fewer than 10% of cases are caught early and that clinicians fear false positives triggering public panic - crucially, Dr Wu partially contradicted the patient interviews, saying patients often refuse screening not because of cost but because they do not know how to interpret an ambiguous result, which the team records as shifting their attention 'from reducing cost to designing unambiguous result communication'. PyrLac Glow was repositioned from a diagnostic device to a risk pre-screening tool that refers high-risk individuals onward, with an explicit trade-off rule carried forward into Stage 2: prioritise reducing missed diagnoses while tolerating interpretable false positives. Staff at Cuiyuan Community Health Service Center in Xihu District, Hangzhou killed the household self-test idea outright - community centres have no high-precision instruments or full-time pathologists, send samples out for 3-7 day report cycles, have overloaded general practitioners, and will only adopt after official medical device certification - so the team abandoned household positioning and fixed three deployment scenarios. Prof. Ying Xiao of Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine changed the report interface: avoid absolute 'cancer / no cancer' conclusions and use physical-examination-style wording (metabolic abnormality, potential risk, re-test recommended), and treat constitution information as auxiliary explanation only since using it to reduce false positives remains a hypothesis. The most consequential safety change came from Erika Ferreri (Bellevue College, Washington State Department of Health, 21 years in medical laboratory education), who found the prototype could output cancer risk conclusions directly to ordinary users: the team re-scoped it as a bench-side research prototype for trained professionals, stripped risk judgments from the device interface so it reports only raw concentrations and quality-control status, added unique sample IDs, full raw-data retention and error-triggered automatic re-testing, separated the operator backend from the doctor and patient report interface, and deferred patient-facing reports until clinical validation - 'this transformed the prototype from an open prototype to a controlled medical research device'. A mechanical manufacturing chairman stopped them wasting the season on shell appearance and tolerances, imposing a core-function-first rule and forward design from commercially available standard components. Commercially, an AIA insurance specialist's view that insurers will not lead on immature technology and barely accept results from private organisations directly removed insurance as a primary channel, redirecting the strategy to corporate physical examinations and public medical screening; a corporate HR director with a 500-RMB-per-employee annual budget set a 200-RMB consumable cost target and added the third deployment scenario the team had missed; an IVD company chairman located the real gap between student prototype and product in batch stability and clinical validation rather than principle verification, turning a 5% to 15% CV benchmark into a quality-control design target. Most tellingly, they record advice they declined with reasons: they rejected educational psychologist Margaret's suggestion to invest in short-video platforms because a high-school team lacks the resources for continuous content production and the compliance capacity for medical-adjacent content, substituting a school health-curriculum lecture series and printed booklet; and they only partially accepted Erika Ferreri's multi-language recommendation, supporting Chinese and English now and deferring the rest. They also resolved a genuine disagreement among the iGEM teams they consulted about whether to validate biology before building hardware by choosing a middle path with a stated rule - hardware parameters must be re-validated against final Stage 2 experimental parameters before freezing.

**publicEngagement.** Outreach is unusually self-critical for a high school team. They produced two differentiated brochures (a children's version with illustrations and simple language, and a systematic middle/high school version covering experimental principles), ran an activity at Suzhou Science and Technology Town Foreign Language High School for about 60 ninth-graders using a Kahoot quiz to build the prerequisite cell-biology concepts before introducing the project, and a themed lacquer-fan creation exercise so students re-expressed the science visually. A shopping-mall event reached a broad cross-section but returned only three completed questionnaires from high foot traffic, and the team published that failure with a diagnosis: a mall suits short accessible outreach rather than detailed survey collection, their material distribution lacked interactive elements and 'often raised suspicion', and next time they would lead with their school and iGEM identity to build trust and standardise the introduction between team members. For a professional audience they rewrote the talk, cutting health-management content and expanding the Warburg effect, dual-biomarker and protein-expression material, then coded the questions received into knowledge and attitude dimensions. A 30-student pre-study tested whether a single outreach event can shift awareness at all.

**realWorld.** The need is quantified against the system that would have to absorb the product: roughly 50% of cancers worldwide diagnosed at advanced stage, fewer than 10% of Chinese patients diagnosed early, 3-7 day report turnaround at community centres with no on-site pathologist, and 58.65% of their own 208 respondents unfamiliar with or completely unaware of early screening - from which they draw the sharpest framing in the project, that the bottleneck is the public 'does not know screening is needed' rather than refuses screening. Cost targets come from stakeholders rather than guesswork and are triangulated across two independent sources: public expectation of under 1,000 RMB per test from the questionnaire, and a per-person threshold of 200 RMB from the corporate HR budget of about 500 RMB per employee per year. Hardware constraints are equally specific: results within 30 minutes, wireless transmission to a phone (62.83% called this very necessary), disposable preloaded disc cartridges, single-use safety (76.11% support), and professional-scenario priority. The regulatory path is laid out concretely - medical device registration and official certification as the precondition for community adoption, POCT specifications for the operating manual, and prospective clinical trials enrolling high-risk populations with 1-2 years of follow-up to establish consistency and positive and negative predictive value, with a staged roadmap of top-tier hospital pilot, data-driven validation, then guideline endorsement, and a stated commercialisation horizon of 3-5 years (5-10 for widespread adoption). No SDG is claimed anywhere on the wiki, which is a genuine gap for a project that frames itself in public-health terms. The limitations section is honest and specific: laboratory validation only with no large clinical sample set for threshold training, no medical device qualification, the science communication plan still at design stage, and the questionnaire sample biased toward urban populations. Future work is committed to a clinical-pilot-first route before any market expansion.

**For GEMS:** Record the advice you declined and why, alongside the advice you took: Bist-China's refusals (short-video outreach beyond their compliance capacity, multi-language deferred to commercialisation) and its openly flagged stakeholder contradictions are what prove the engagement was deliberation rather than endorsement-collection.

### BASIS-China — HEAL — Hairball Elimination and Lysis
High School · China · https://2026.igem.wiki/basis-china/
BASIS-China engineered E. coli to express keratinases and proteases (p-Ker, Protease 1, Protease 2, MGY1820, MGY4907) with thioredoxin and thioredoxin reductase as synergistic helpers and LGOX plus KatG as gut antioxidant modules, aimed at digesting cat hairballs. The safety engineering is the standout: a bile-acid-responsive suicide switch in which membrane sensors TcpH and CadC-TcpP activate the pCadBA promoter to produce the unstable CcdA antitoxin, while the stable CcdB toxin is expressed constitutively, so the cell survives only where bile acid is present. Four Anderson promoters (J23100, J23102, J23104, J23114) were built to tune CcdB strength, and the response threshold was measured at roughly 0.1-0.2 mM taurocholic acid, then compared against feline duodenal bile salts at 15-42 mM and against published sewage and soil bile-acid levels orders of magnitude below the threshold. They won the Safety and Security Award in the High School section and were nominated for Best New Basic Part.

**frameworks.** A published five-step characterisation framework for environmentally responsive kill switches, written because the team found limited end-to-end guidance in existing iGEM wikis: confirm construction by gel and sequencing; tune toxin expression across promoters of differing strength to find an operating window; characterise the concentration-dependent growth response by time course; compare the measured response range against published signal concentrations in both the intended host and the likely receiving environments; and add an orthogonal reporter readout alongside growth. Alongside it, a transferable design concept (use an endogenous molecule abundant in the target host's intestine and scarce outside it) with the caveat that bile-acid composition varies by species so adopters must establish their own host's signal profile.

**datascience.** The containment claim is quantified on both sides, which is what distinguishes it. The switch threshold is placed at approximately 0.1-0.2 mM TCA, with limited growth below 0.2 mM and similar growth rates above 0.4 mM. That is then set against feline duodenal bile salts at 15-42 mM (Reber and Mosley), sewage total bile acids at 184-356 micrograms per litre, which they convert to roughly 4.7 x 10^-4 to 9.1 x 10^-4 mM using a representative molecular weight of 392.6 g/mol (Sebok et al.), and soil deoxycholic acid at 13.3 pmol/g in archaeological soil from Pompeii, converted to 1.33 x 10^-5 mmol/kg (Porru et al.). They show the unit conversions and then state that total bile salts and soil-associated bile acids are not directly equivalent to TCA in culture medium.

**dataviz.** Circuit diagrams for the switch in both the bile-acid-present and bile-acid-absent states, a promoter-variant design figure, assembly gels against the expected 3,704 bp fragment, OD600 growth curves at 0 and 30 mM TCA, serial-dilution spot plates across six TCA concentrations (0, 0.1, 1, 10, 15, 30 mM) for all four promoter variants plus empty vector, 270-minute time-course growth curves per promoter across 0-1 mM, fluorescence panels for all four variants, and a supplemented-versus-depleted sfGFP comparison. The iGEM approval email and a 17-page laboratory safety rules PDF are embedded.

**ihp.** An interview with an experienced stray-cat rescuer from Xiaobabenben in Shenzhen reframed the product requirement: limited volunteer capacity, poor acceptance of existing remedies and stress-related overgrooming pushed the team toward palatable formats cats would take voluntarily, minimising restraint and forced administration, and made gastrointestinal safety and animal comfort explicit evaluation priorities. The more unusual engagement was with iGEM itself: knowing that the Animal Use Form is not available to high-school teams, they contacted the iGEM Safety and Regulatory Committee before collecting any samples, and Chris Isaac, Director of Responsibility at iGEM HQ, approved the collection without an Animal Use Form on the basis that routine grooming causes no harm, which they then documented on their official Project Safety Form as instructed and published the approval email.

**realWorld.** No company, no patent, no pricing and no funding here, so the material worth taking is the safety practice, and it is the most rigorous high-school biocontainment work in this group. Four features make it serious. First, the switch is engineered as a tunable system rather than a single construct: four Anderson promoters of differing strength drive CcdB so the operating window can be matched to a required kill sensitivity, and all four variants are characterised in parallel in every assay, with empty vector alongside. Second, the containment claim is tested against the actual release pathway rather than a lab abstraction. They ask where the bacteria would end up after excretion, find published bile-acid concentrations for sewage and soil, convert them into the same units as their assay, and show the receiving environments sit three to four orders of magnitude below their measured threshold. Third, the evidence hierarchy is stated explicitly and never collapsed. They separate 'evidence of construct assembly, conditional growth suppression, and reporter expression' from 'evidence required to demonstrate containment in real-world settings', and they list, in their own words, what still stands in the way: residual bile acids in faecal material, differences between laboratory medium and environmental conditions, circuit drift over time, and possible horizontal transfer. They add two caveats most teams would omit, that genetic containment neither removes extracellular DNA nor replaces waste decontamination, and that their delivery microcapsules are designed to release bacteria in the intestine and therefore must not be counted as physical containment. They also note sfGFP tracks the circuit but does not independently establish viability, and that soil and sewage total bile acids are not equivalent to TCA in medium. Fourth, the chassis plan is honest about its own role: BSL-1 E. coli is declared a proof-of-concept model only, chosen because high-school teams may not use untested wild isolates or run animal trials, with the translational chassis identified as GRAS feline-native probiotics (Lactiplantibacillus plantarum, Lactobacillus acidophilus, Bifidobacterium animalis) to be ported into only after validation and under veterinary compliance. Enzyme safety is argued mechanistically rather than asserted, noting that gut mucus is glycoprotein-based while keratinases target cross-linked keratin disulfides, and substrate safety is covered by using washed, sterilised naturally shed hair and pharmaceutical-grade beta-keratin. Laboratory risk management is reagent-specific rather than generic, naming beta-mercaptoethanol (fume hood only, sealed tubes), unpolymerised acrylamide (pre-cast gels preferred, dedicated hazardous waste), kanamycin and ampicillin with the resistance marker on each vector identified and media neutralised and autoclaved before disposal, and Ni-NTA nickel waste segregated for hazardous recycling, plus a preference for blue LED over UV transilluminators. Waste is bleached at 10 percent for at least 30 minutes or autoclaved at 121 degrees C for 30 minutes before discharge. Continuation is community-facing: the five-step framework, the design concept, and characterisation data for the circuit and all four promoter variants submitted to the Registry as a reference for future teams building bile-acid-responsive kill switches, with the honest framing that the data are 'a starting point for further validation, rather than a claim that this circuit is ready for unrestricted deployment'. No animal trials were conducted, and they say so repeatedly rather than once.

**For GEMS:** Characterise any containment switch the way they did: tune the toxin across a promoter series to find an operating window, measure the response threshold as a number, then look up the signal concentration in the actual receiving environment, convert it into your assay's units, and show the gap — a containment claim is only as good as the comparison behind it. Pair that with their evidence ledger, a 'what our results establish' section beside a 'what remains before real-world use' section, and with asking the governing body in advance rather than assuming an unavailable form means the work cannot be done compliantly.

### HUST-China — IRIS
Undergrad · China · https://2026.igem.wiki/hust-china/
HUST-China built IRIS to resolve an ethical problem inside a Chinese intangible cultural heritage: Dian Cui, the court craft of inlaying kingfisher feathers into metal jewellery. Rather than finding another animal substitute, they went after the physics - keratin-and-air microstructures producing angle-dependent structural colour, with melanin absorbing stray light to raise saturation - and reproduced it by growing bacterial cellulose from discarded cotton textiles, converting it to cellulose nanocrystals and self-assembling those into an ordered photonic structure, layered with pigment-based functional layers. Their design philosophy, formed in dialogue with artisans and conservationists, is 'retain the aesthetic core while abandoning the outdated carrier'. They won the peer-voted iGEMers Prize, and the reasons are legible on the wiki: they hosted a regional forum for other teams modelled on the Jamboree itself, and co-produced open science-communication materials with multiple other teams rather than only publishing their own.

**frameworks.** A published 'Who / Why / What / How' stakeholder engagement matrix, offered explicitly as a reusable blueprint for ethical technology research, plus a value-system analysis with value-oriented task execution. Education is organised as a three-dimensional positioning matrix of audience age against outreach domain, so every activity occupies a named cell (for example 'community teenagers x synthetic biology x Dian Cui culture x ecological conservation') and gaps in coverage are visible. SDGs 4, 11 (target 11.4), 12, 15 and 17 (targets 17.16, 17.17) are mapped individually with the specific partner that delivers each.

**datascience.** Public surveys run as design instruments with reported n and percentages: 257+ then more than 400 valid responses (409 valid samples cited for the product-form survey), showing 63% had heard of Dian Cui but only 4% claimed in-depth understanding, 54.1% preferred recreating Dian Cui with substitute materials, 74.08% supported using synthetic biology to reproduce the structural colour, and 61.5% of science information reaching respondents came through short-video channels. The key analytic conclusion reshaped the whole programme: 'the inheritance dilemma stems from a lack of science communication, not public indifference', which produced tiered rather than uniform outreach.

**dataviz.** A three-dimensional positioning map of educational practices (audience age x outreach domains); survey-result charts of public preferences for Dian Cui inheritance and conservation approaches; molecular dynamics trajectory analyses with reported standard deviations.

**software.** Molecular dynamics work on an engineered disulfide tether: the S38C/T101C pair was simulated across oxidised and reduced states sharing coordinates and differing only by the SSBOND entry, with pdb2gmx closing the specbond from a 4.0 A Cbeta-Cbeta start to S-S 2.027 A (100% of frames inside 0.18-0.22 nm); reduction released the C-terminal region (CTR-to-core centre-of-mass distance 1.39 +/- 0.05 to 2.41 +/- 0.70 nm, CTR RMSF up ~1.9x). In a six-chain 100 ns per state run the tether settled at 2.96 +/- 0.04 A, 45% beyond its unstrained length, with no frame inside the relaxed 1.95-2.15 A window, so the team explicitly reclassified it as an extended covalent tether rather than a textbook disulfide and modelled it as a deliberately softened harmonic SG-SG bond - a careful negative-result reinterpretation.

**ihp.** Human Practices is described as the strategic engine and compass rather than a parallel track, and the evidence supports it. Early dialogue with Dian Cui artisans, cultural scholars and conservationists produced the zero-animal-harm ecological baseline and the design philosophy of retaining the aesthetic core while abandoning the outdated carrier. Expert consultation on the in vitro film-formation difficulty of reflectin triggered a decisive wet-lab pivot: the reflectin module was abandoned entirely for the fashion-waste-to-CNC route. Further expert feedback produced protein tag modifications for easier detection and optimisation of the BC-to-CNC conversion. Market research and public surveys redefined the product from a museum replica into mid-priced Bio-Fashion daily-wear jewellery, which in turn drove the team to design custom cost-conscious hardware for better environmental control during film casting. Stakeholder findings were specific: Teacher Liu Yang at Beijing 798's Slow Time Handicraft Workshop showed that peacock-feather imitations are too green and bright and crack and peel; the manager of the Guangzhou Yuequ Intangible Cultural Heritage Inheritance Institute explained that natural peacock feathers carry high loss and raw-material cost, that Dian Cui has high social-media popularity but far fewer offline experience visits than mother-of-pearl, that goose feathers and blue pattern paper cannot replicate the iridescence, and that a real Dian Cui sealing layer destroys the iridescence - a pain point that became the team's core engineering goal of reconciling film durability with structural-colour retention. Systematic museum benchmarking at the Palace Museum, Hong Kong Palace Museum, Zhenbao (Treasure) Museum and Hubei Provincial Museum set the optical performance target and informed film pitch and colour-gradient tuning; at the Hubei Provincial Museum the absence of genuine Dian Cui and the crudeness of the gift-shop imitations pushed them away from motif reproduction toward material reproduction. Government engagement produced a written reply from the Wuhan Bureau of Landscape Architecture and Forestry confirming Wuhan has no traditional Dian Cui manufacturers and no records of illegal hunting or trade, which deliberately shifted the team's narrative from 'solving current poaching' to 'preventing potential poaching risks' via positive biodiversity publicity; a dedicated symposium with the Wuhan Ecology and Environment Bureau on 10 September 2025 brought in solid-waste, ecological-protection and environmental-industry experts and standardised lab waste management and compliant waste-cellulose sourcing.

**publicEngagement.** HUST-China's education programme is built as a matrix, not a list: a three-dimensional map of audience age against outreach domain, with each activity placed in a named cell so coverage and gaps are both visible. The analytical basis was their own survey work - more than 400 valid responses showing 63% had heard of Dian Cui but only 4% understood it in any depth - which produced the diagnosis that drove everything else: the heritage inheritance crisis is a science-communication failure, not public apathy, so outreach must be tiered rather than uniform. The youngest cell is remote-area online teaching: joining the HUST Graduate Teaching-Support Group in Long'an, Guangxi, they delivered online science classes to local primary-school students, using sharks as the narrative thread to explain a species' importance to marine ecosystem stability and how synthetic biology can produce substitute materials ('Microbial Superheroes: Protecting Sharks'). The most grassroots cell is the Huanyu Cup street outreach, 'Huanyu Together - Reviving the Ancient Craft - Guarding Kingfisher Vitality', run in three staged phases: a community street booth explaining Dian Cui heritage in age-appropriate language with physical replica samples and correcting misconceptions through quizzes and on-site Q&A; close-range handling of craft replicas followed by guided hands-on Dian Cui-style handcraft so children experienced 'listening, seeing and making'; and distribution of science handbooks and souvenirs to consolidate learning. This reached over a hundred community children free of charge and, in the team's own framing, broke the 'waiting for audiences' limitation of traditional lecturing and proved lightweight grassroots outreach is feasible. The 'Colorful Vacation' summer childcare class at the Zisong Yijing Huating neighbourhood in Wuhan deliberately opened three topics in one classroom - synthetic biology, Dian Cui culture and ecological conservation - using science-aesthetic integration and accessible metaphors, with feedback collected during the handcraft session feeding back into the design of activities for younger groups. For secondary students choosing their majors, team members ran an alma mater revisit programme over the winter vacation, delivering lectures at five schools: the First Affiliated High School of Central China Normal University, Zhengding High School in Hebei, Foshan No. 1 High School, Yali High School and Yongji County Experimental High School, covering synthetic biology basics, kingfisher conservation and competition-experience sharing as career guidance. On campus they ran outreach classes and science booths with IRIS culturally inspired creative products. Ecological education left the classroom entirely through joint birdwatching with the HUST Bird Association, explaining kingfisher habitat and wetland ecology in the field, alongside an agreement with the Wuhan Birdwatching Association (President Ming Liang) on data linkage and university-society outreach. Internationally, three rounds of overseas interviews plus cultural exchange in Singapore, the United Kingdom and France carried Chinese aesthetics and kingfisher conservation abroad, with an explicit stance against 'piling up fragmented Chinese symbols or catering to stereotyped Western imaginings of the East', and the narrative strategy drawn from those interviews was 'emotional connection first, transparent technology second'. The work most likely to explain the peer-voted iGEMers Prize is what they did for other teams. On 12 July 2026 HUST-China independently hosted the First Central-China iGEM Forum (CCiF) at the Qiming College Maker Space, deliberately replicating the structure of the international Jamboree - opening speeches, thematic keynotes, a LiveStage presentation block, judge comment sessions and poster-booth free communication - with 15 online and offline teams, invited iGEM senior consultants, former gold medallists and industry guests; 14 teams presented in sequence and received targeted commentary on experimental design, human practices arrangement and logical completeness, then moved to poster booths for peer feedback, and every attendee left with a certificate and themed souvenirs. They also attended Grand APiC, the first Asia-Pacific Synthetic Biology Youth Conference (16-19 August at Southern University of Science and Technology and the University of Hong Kong), joined NAU-CHINA's nationwide ICII (Into China, Into iGEM 2026) community initiative and explicitly borrowed ICII's community-construction logic when designing their own CCiF, and won a Gold Prize at SynBio Challenges 2026 - exchanging with more than ten teams including Jilin University, Wuhan University, Nanjing University and the University of Hong Kong. Three concrete co-productions followed. With Beijing University of Chemical Technology they co-created the science picture book 'Wukong Asks the Way: A Pilgrimage Through Biological Science', and separately contributed specialised content to BUCT's air-to-protein popular-science publication addressing public misconceptions about electro-biocatalytic protein production, jointly refining the argument that proteins made from CO2 and N2 are biologically derived rather than hazardous industrial chemicals and that purification and toxicological evaluation are mandatory before deployment; the text was reviewed by both teams and published on BUCT's wiki as a shared output. With JLU-FBH they joined 'Together with iGEM: Across Villages, From Myths to Facts', a community-driven myth-busting handbook where JLU-FBH acted as chief editor coordinating submissions from over 17 global iGEM teams; HUST-China independently wrote a complete entry debunking the pseudoscience claim that blackened silver ornaments can detect heavy-metal poisons, which after mutual review and format alignment was integrated into the collective handbook and released publicly as a shared anti-misinformation resource for student synthetic biology groups worldwide. Finally, and unusually, the team benchmarked itself against past Best Education winners and published six named next-iteration commitments, each crediting the team it learned from: establish pre/post classroom tests following GreatBay-SCIE's accuracy-based pre/post design; standardise and open-source the Huanyu Cup and childcare-class courses into reusable course packages following RWTH Aachen's open course model; build an online matrix of short videos, graphics and online classrooms to match the 61.5% short-video share found in their survey; turn picture books, handbooks and posters into continuously updated open resources; explore parent and family participation models following GreatBay-SCIE's parent workshops; and keep recording 'whom we asked, what we learned, and what we changed accordingly', writing education as a traceable decision log rather than a list of activities.

**realWorld.** Four reusable outputs are named explicitly: the value-system analysis and value-oriented task execution framework; the documented Who/Why/What/How stakeholder engagement matrix as a blueprint for ethical technology research; open-source educational resources co-created with other teams; and low-cost hardware promoted so other teams and industry can fabricate structural-colour films more consistently on a limited budget. Market positioning was derived from field evidence: Wuhan SKP luxury retail (Louis Vuitton, Rolex) as the high end, the Tanhualin district in Wuhan and Chongqing cultural-creative markets as the affordable end, where the team found Dian Cui and imitation products essentially absent and most blue ornaments made from pigment, mother-of-pearl or spun thread - establishing the mid-tier sustainable jewellery gap IRIS targets.

**For GEMS:** Earn peer goodwill by building infrastructure for other teams, not just audiences: HUST hosted a regional forum that replicated the Jamboree's own format (keynotes, LiveStage talks, judge commentary, poster walk) for 15 teams, then wrote entries into two other teams' open publications - and publicly benchmarked its own education against past Best Education winners with six named, credited improvements for next year.

### Labi-Taiwan — BlueCatcher: a cell-free electrochemical biosensor for MDD-associated circulating microRNAs
High School · Taiwan · https://2026.igem.wiki/labi-taiwan/
Labi-Taiwan built BlueCatcher, a portable cell-free electrochemical biosensor for circulating microRNAs associated with major depressive disorder, intended as objective biological evidence alongside clinical assessment rather than as a diagnosis. The signal chain is deliberately long: a three-way junction recognises the target miRNA and releases a trigger strand, the trigger activates a toehold switch that expresses a nuclease, the nuclease cleaves a methylene-blue-labelled DNA reporter, and the released reporter is captured on a gold-modified screen-printed carbon electrode and quantified by square-wave voltammetry. Because a final signal alone cannot show that every step behaved, the team built a stepwise measurement framework in which each stage is independently validated before integration, with the degree of calibration deliberately matched to each measurement's role. The project also carries a machine-learning design suite and a strong education programme grounded in its own 432-respondent survey; it won the iGEMers Prize in the High School section.

**frameworks.** A stepwise measurement framework that follows the sensor from target recognition to electrochemical readout, with a published table listing for each method its purpose and its reusable output. Each measurement is classified by the question it can answer: structural validation, relative comparison under matched conditions, or absolute quantification. Three modular measurement workflows are released separately from the project so that another team can adopt one without adopting BlueCatcher. The software follows a Design-Predict-Test loop in which predictions are returned to the wet lab and the results are used to judge where the model performed well.

**datascience.** The calibration philosophy is stated explicitly and is the most transferable thing here: different measurements are calibrated to different degrees according to what they are for. FRET measurements, used only for comparison under matched conditions, are reported as a background-adjusted response (delta F equals fluorescence with target minus fluorescence without target) and are explicitly said to be in arbitrary units, intended for within-experiment comparison and not for absolute cross-instrument quantification. Toehold-switch fluorescence is interpreted against a three-way control framework of sensor-only, trigger-only and sensor-plus-trigger, with fold change calculated as (sensor+trigger minus trigger-only) over (sensor-only minus trigger-only) so that background and OFF-state leakage are separated from activation; this is what revealed a 43.4-fold response in BL21(DE3) against 3.6-fold in pLysS and justified the strain choice. Native PAGE is used only as qualitative structural validation, and the team states that the paired plus- and minus-target lanes are different experimental conditions and not independent replicates, with quantitative reproducibility deferred to the replicated FRET measurements. Only the final electrochemical step is developed as an absolute quantitative endpoint: SWV on functionalised Au@SPCEs across 0 to 500 nM methylene-blue reporter gives a nonlinear full-range response but an approximately linear relationship against log concentration, Ip = 2.313 log10(C) - 2.028 with R2 = 0.9457, and the limit of detection is derived properly from the blanks as I_LOD = I_blank + 3 sigma_blank then inverted through the calibration to give 7.53 nM, with the 0 nM condition serving both as the blank for the threshold and as the negative control. Reproducibility is measured at the level that actually varies, the electrode: three independently fabricated batches of Au@SPCE were measured against the same 200 nM reporter, showed no statistically significant difference, and gave a combined coefficient of variation of 10.66%. Upstream quality control is explicit and non-binary: UV absorbance (A230, A260, A280) is used as a checkpoint rather than a pass/fail gate, with the full table of ratios published including a sample flagged for an anomalous A230 of 1.097 and a 260/230 of 0.048, and samples carried forward to Sanger sequencing as the higher-resolution arbiter in a declared chain of plasmid extraction, purity check, restriction digest, sequence confirmation, then functional measurement. Electrode fabrication itself is characterised stepwise by cyclic voltammetry, chronoamperometry and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy across bare SPCE, Au@SPCE, probe-modified, MCH-blocked and reporter-hybridised states, with EIS used as interface characterisation rather than as the quantitative readout. Statistics are named: two-way ANOVA with Tukey multiple-comparisons for the cell-free screening, with significance levels reported alongside n = 3 and individual points. The team also states what has not been done, that the toehold-switch-to-AciI construct is not yet built so the system is not integrated, and refuses to claim that BlueCatcher is faster, more sensitive or more accessible than qRT-PCR until it is, marking every projected time in its comparison table with an asterisk.

**dataviz.** A heatmap of background-adjusted fluorescence response across all 25 three-way-junction probe combinations, measured every five minutes for 30 minutes; time-course FRET curves with mean +/- SD (n = 3); dose-response and specificity bar panels with individual data points overlaid and significance annotated; overlaid baseline-corrected SWV voltammograms across the reporter concentration series with an inset log-linear calibration; batch-to-batch SWV bar charts with individual measurements shown; an interactive experimental-design flow diagram mapping every assay onto the stage of the sensor it validates.

**software.** The BlueCatcher Software Suite, with independent design modules for three-way-junction probes (trained Random Forest) and toehold switches (trained XGBoost), available through a browser interface and as a local install. A user supplies a target or trigger sequence, the suite generates candidate designs, computes sequence, structural, thermodynamic and interaction features using NUPACK and custom scripts, applies the trained model, and returns ranked candidates with prediction confidence plus the complete sequence components needed to order and test them, exportable as CSV. Documented limits of applicability are published: 18 to 25 nucleotide targets for the TWJ module and up to 30 nucleotide triggers for the toehold module, stated as the sequence spaces represented in training rather than as biological limits, together with a discussion of dataset coverage, how prediction confidence should be interpreted, and the NUPACK dependency that constrains distribution. Supporting material includes complete Sanger sequencing datasets as PDFs and three standalone protocol documents (nucleic-acid characterisation, toehold-switch cloning and expression, electrochemical signal generation).

**ihp.** Stakeholder work spans healthcare professionals, researchers, regulatory specialists, potential users and investment professionals, and fed an entrepreneurship roadmap covering regulatory planning and market analysis. The project's framing, that BlueCatcher complements rather than replaces clinical evaluation, comes from this engagement, as does the explicit statement that the device detects signals and does not diagnose.

**publicEngagement.** Education began with research rather than assumption. An anonymous online survey, preceded by an informed-consent statement and screened for careless or too-fast responses (12 excluded, 432 retained), used translated versions of three validated instruments: the six-item Depression Literacy and eight-item Misconceptions subscales of the DepSter scale and the nine-item perceived-stigma subscale of the Depression Stigma Scale, with internal consistency reported for this sample (alpha 0.66, 0.84 and 0.72). Literacy was high (mean 25.1 of 30) and misconceptions were broadly rejected (15.7 of 40), while perceived public stigma sat in the moderate-to-high range (29.3 of 45), with the highest-scoring items describing expected social exclusion. The team's conclusion, that the gap in Taiwan is stigma rather than knowledge, redirected the education programme; a saturated path model was estimated to test how education and personal contact relate to literacy, misconceptions and the perceived limits of counselling-only assessment. The programme that followed used different approaches for different audiences: a flipped classroom, a summer laboratory camp whose toehold-switch protocol is published as a reusable four-day workflow, family information sessions, a podcast, TGEM community-building among Taiwanese teams, and social media.

**realWorld.** The clinical gap is stated concretely: MDD assessment depends on interviews, symptom reporting and professional judgement, and patients face irregular follow-up because of stigma or access, no quantitative way to assess recovery or relapse, and trial-and-error treatment selection. The long-term aim is a portable format operating closer to the point of care in settings without centralised laboratory infrastructure, avoiding the reverse transcription and PCR amplification that qRT-PCR requires. The hardware is specified down to the reader's internals: an insertable electron reader module carrying the electrode pad and a cellulose overflow pad, a battery, a polyimide flexible heater, a lever that mechanically breaks a separation membrane in a two-chamber microtube to release the second reagent, and an ESP32 module that processes the signal and transmits results by WiFi and Bluetooth to a companion application that reports Low, Moderate or High biomarker variation with timestamped metadata rather than a binary diagnosis.

**For GEMS:** Match the amount of calibration to the job each measurement does: screening comparisons can stay in background-subtracted arbitrary units if you say so, but the one measurement you report as a concentration needs a real calibration curve, a blank-derived limit of detection, standardised baseline correction and a between-batch coefficient of variation. Treating every signal as equally quantitative is where overclaiming starts.

### MIT-MAHE — MAHEK
Undergrad · India · https://2026.igem.wiki/mit-mahe/
MAHEK addresses the fragrance industry's dependence on petrochemical synthesis and wasteful seed extraction by producing cuminaldehyde biologically. The chassis is Pseudomonas putida F1, a solvent-tolerant soil bacterium that already makes cuminaldehyde as an intermediate in p-cymene degradation; CRISPR-Cas9-mediated homologous recombination knocks out cymC, the p-cumic aldehyde dehydrogenase, arresting the pathway exactly at the target compound. The dry lab's deliverable is NetFlux, a React + FastAPI web application that compresses a genome-scale metabolic model into a readable 'production corridor' using a novel extraction algorithm (SCOPE) and then pools OptKnock and OptForce into one co-ranked list of knockout and regulation strategies, each traced to the gene and linked to BiGG. The team also won the Inclusivity Award for work with visually impaired learners that ended in Vision Empower adopting their tactile models for use in schools across India.

**frameworks.** React + TypeScript single-page frontend split into three modules (parameter panel, pathway map viewer, interventions table) sharing one run state; FastAPI backend with Pydantic request/response schemas, auto-generated OpenAPI 3.1 documentation and a Swagger UI at /docs; a JobManager running strain design on a bounded background worker pool so heavy requests do not time out; SQLite (mfghub.db) as the model/reaction/metabolite/gene/medium catalogue, rebuilt from the GEMs on every server image build; and Docker Compose bringing up database, API and web client together. Core science runs on COBRApy.

**datascience.** Benchmarked without a ground truth by defining what a useful pathway must do and measuring that instead. SCOPE was run on 9 GEMs with up to 5 target products each, 40 organism-product pairs in total: 100% of extracted pathways were fully connected from substrate to target, and the mean corridor was 55.1 reactions against a mean model size of 934, i.e. 7.8% of the network (models up to 1,762 reactions reduced to about 55). Essential reactions were identified independently with FVA and then checked for recall: 20.3 essential reactions per product on average, 17.5 retained, overall recall 0.863, above 0.90 in five of nine organisms, with the weakest cases (iJN1463 at 0.616, iJN1026 at 0.719) reported rather than hidden. Eleven curated GEMs ship with the tool, covering bacteria, a cyanobacterium, an archaeon, yeast and a diatom. The metabolic model behind the wet lab extended iJN1463 with the full p-cymene degradation route (cymA, cymB, cymC, cmtA-cmtE), linking to native metabolism through OP4ENH.

**dataviz.** Pathways are drawn as interactive metabolic maps flowing strictly left to right, with line width proportional to mass flow, metabolites as nodes carrying compartment suffixes, reactions as arrows colour-coded by their FVA annotation, and the substrate-to-target corridor explicitly highlighted. Hovering a reaction opens an inspection card with reaction name and ID, knockout-candidate status, flux and FVA range, coupling and bounds, subsystem, gene associations and gene rules, and its producers and consumers. Each click of Generate opens its parameters in a new tab so settings can be compared side by side. Results export as GraphML, JSON and CSV straight from the browser. The interventions table shows a baseline header (wild-type growth rate, yield floor and ceiling) against which every ranked design is judged, and separates committed 'Ranked Designs' from weaker single-reaction 'Hypotheses (leads)', with the wiki telling users not to compare yield numbers across the two tables.

**software.** NetFlux solves two linked problems in metabolic engineering: genome-scale models are too large to read, and strain-design algorithms waste most of their compute on reactions that can never carry flux. Its five-stage pipeline is the substance. Stage 1 solves FBA then pFBA and converts the flux distribution into a Mass Flow Graph (nodes = reactions, edges = metabolite mass flow). Stage 2 applies FASTCC against a fixed consistency threshold to strip blocked reactions, which the team identifies as the single largest source of computational expense. Stage 3 is SCOPE, their GUDIE-derived extractor: log-normalise the heavy-tailed edge weights, compute a flux-coupling score per reaction against the target, seed an interest signal at the target and propagate it with Personalised PageRank, combine coupling and interest into a per-edge score, expand outward over a bounded number of hops admitting reactions above a threshold anchored to the target's immediate neighbourhood, then an optional repair step that closes a broken corridor with a flux-weighted shortest path. Stage 4 annotates the corridor with FVA so each reaction is typed as essential-and-fixed, flexible, or a natural up/downregulation candidate. Stage 5 pools OptForce and OptKnock and co-ranks their proposals into one ordered list, resolving each to a gene linked to BiGG. Two design decisions stand out for reuse: the REST API is versioned, OpenAPI 3.1-specified and language-agnostic with async job polling (submit, get a job_id, poll), and all compute is deliberately RAM-only, with uploaded models referenced by short-lived tokens, a 30-minute SessionCache, and nothing a client submits ever written to disk or database. Users can upload their own GEM as .json or .sbml. It is self-hosted rather than publicly deployed: 'git clone https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/mit-mahe/netflux && docker compose up --build', then http://localhost:5173/, with stated system requirements of 2-4 GB RAM, any modern multi-core CPU and no GPU. A video guide and a step-by-step interpretation guide are on the wiki, and the limitation is stated plainly: constraint-based predictions describe what the network allows at steady state, not kinetics or regulation, so every strategy is a wet-lab hypothesis. Repo: https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/mit-mahe/netflux (team repo https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/mit-mahe).

**ihp.** Stakeholder analysis walked the whole cumin supply chain, from traders who buy directly from farmers to internationally working perfumers, finding that each group holds a different version of the same problem. Hard numbers anchor the premise: India supplies about 70-80% of world cumin, the 2026 crop was projected at 9.0-9.2 million bags against roughly 11 million in 2025 (a 15-20% decline), hydrodistillation yields about 2.56% essential oil, and cuminaldehyde is a fraction of that. The decisive conversation was with Givaudan, which revealed that fragrance houses procure whole cumin essential oil rather than isolated cuminaldehyde; this redirected the team's target customer from fragrance houses to aroma compound manufacturers, where demand for isolated, sustainably produced cuminaldehyde actually exists. The inclusivity work was itself integrated rather than decorative: conversations with Vision Empower (IIIT Bangalore) identified that Indian educational structures restrict visually impaired students from science, and the team then built tactile models, trialled them with Mrs Nagarathna, a visually impaired educator, revised on her feedback, and tested with a ninth-grade student. Fixes were deliberately minimal and buildable from cheap materials: the existing DNA model distinguished bases only by colour, so each base got a texture instead (adenine smooth tape, thymine jute, guanine bubble wrap, cytosine velvet) wrapped around the existing model so it did not need rebuilding; the mitosis model's components were only drawn on, so they were rebuilt in clay with pipe-cleaner chromosomes. Vision Empower approved both the content and the models and will use them across their associated schools. A separate conversation with an Indian Sign Language expert established that, unlike ASL, ISL has no centralised place to learn it, which the team records as a gap they did not close.

**publicEngagement.** Sessions were run across India in English, Hindi, Telugu, Kannada and Marathi so language would not be a barrier, and deliberately extended beyond students: the team visited old age homes to learn how residents' associations with traditional scents had changed over their lifetimes, then introduced them to synthetic biology. Workshops included household-materials DNA extraction from bananas at Purple Space Library Manipal (50 students, grades 1-7, split by age group), recombinant DNA via insulin at GenWise Camp, and deeper project discussion with grade 11-12 biology students at Vidya Mandir Chennai. Teachers were walked through each protocol step so they could keep running the demonstration after the team left. 'Beyond Sight', an audio-only podcast, carried five conversations with visually impaired professionals (a radio jockey, a geneticist, the founder of assistive-technology company TorchIT, an ophthalmologist, and one of only three blind women to have submitted before the Supreme Court of India). A Colourblind Awareness Day Instagram series ran on 6 September.

**realWorld.** A consumer survey found the barrier is information rather than opposition, with respondents already aware of land use, extraction and climate pressures and nearly half willing to pay slightly more for lower environmental impact, though more were worried about long-term effects of ingredients made by engineered microorganisms. Producer-side work found that Indian companies import aroma compounds from China, the UAE and France despite domestic cumin dominance, and that price is the deciding factor for buyers because raw material cost passes straight to consumers. The team wrote 'An iGEMer's Guide to Upscaling', a structured upscaling and biomanufacturing guide, after finding no iGEM-oriented resource bridging flask scale to industrial scale, and 'The Aroma Atlas', a catalogue of everyday scents, their active ingredients and current production methods, as a starting point for teams looking for compounds worth making sustainably. Six cym operon genes were submitted to the Registry as basic parts (BBa_26CFFF0H, BBa_26R7VUFV, BBa_26MJ8EI9, BBa_26SS8791, BBa_26AS8UG2, BBa_26AW7YAF).

**For GEMS:** When there is no ground truth to benchmark against, define what a correct output must satisfy and measure that: NetFlux's credibility rests on three published numbers (100% corridor connectivity, 7.8% of the network retained, 0.863 recall of independently FVA-derived essential reactions), with the weakest organisms named. A research centre should also copy the ephemeral-compute design, user-uploaded models held in RAM behind short-lived tokens and never written to disk, which makes a shared analysis service usable with data people will not hand over.

### NCKU-Tainan — Capture: detecting and inhibiting Pseudomonas aeruginosa quorum-sensing signals
Undergrad · Taiwan · https://2026.igem.wiki/ncku-tainan/
NCKU-Tainan targeted the acyl-homoserine lactone signals that Pseudomonas aeruginosa uses to coordinate toxin release and biofilm formation in healthcare-associated infections, with two systems reading the same molecule: one that detects the signal and reports the infection, and one that inhibits it with published single-stranded DNA aptamers acting as molecular sponges. To read their GFP reporter without booking a shared plate reader in another building they built CAPTURE-Screen, a single-cuvette fluorescence reader in two versions, 3D-printed and laser-cut, costing 21 to 65 times less than an open-source plate reader. LasReader, a browser application, completes the chain by fitting a weighted four-parameter logistic calibration, deriving limits of detection from the blanks and returning each sample's concentration with an approximate confidence interval.

**frameworks.** The hardware page opens by deriving its requirements from the assay rather than from an instrument wish list: 200 uL of sfGFP culture per reaction, read every hour for six hours at 37 C, benchmarked against the plate-reader standard of 485/510 nm, and cheap enough to rebuild. The modelling is split into three parts that each serve a different part of the team (an inhibition model for the wet lab, an imaging model for the software, a fluorescence model for the hardware). Software, hardware and model are written as one workflow, with LasReader checking the reader, showing which tube to read next, and keeping every saved curve with its limit of detection and usable range.

**datascience.** The instrument is honest about what its numbers are. Readings are raw sensor counts from an AS7341 ten-channel spectral sensor, with F4 (515 nm) as the emission channel and F3 (480 nm) reported beside it as the scatter channel, because the team found that dense suspensions give a few counts of F4 with no reporter present once F3 passes about 46 and none below about 33, so a few counts alone are not evidence of GFP. Excitation and emission are separated by angle (detection at 90 degrees) and by colour (the sensor's own bands), with no emission filter, and a light trap whose end wall slopes at about 41 degrees turns transmitted blue up into the roof rather than back at the sample. Every measurement cycle begins and ends with a dark read, and under the shield every channel must read exactly zero or the cycle is void. Repeatability is quantified at the level that actually varies: five re-insertions of one tube gave 0.76% standard deviation at about 50 counts. Validation is comparative rather than self-referential, with one batch of sfGFP culture at five dilutions plus medium and a non-fluorescent culture read on the team's reader and on a SpectraMax M3 on the same day, ranking the tubes the same way, with the green reading rising from 2.44 to 86.44 counts and about 104 counts per unit OD600 across the three denser tubes. The team states plainly that counts from the two readers are not interchangeable, and reports the failures: the laser-cut build could not distinguish the AHL sensor strain from cells without sfGFP, and the 3D-printed build read zero on its emission channel for that strain. LasReader carries the statistics. It requires at least four concentrations and two blanks as the minimum for a four-parameter curve and a limit of detection, and fits a weighted four-parameter logistic in which EC50 is fitted as its logarithm to keep it positive and the Hill slope is bounded between 0.05 and 20, with blanks entering at zero concentration so they fix the baseline directly. Weighting is used because replicates scatter more at high signal than at low, and the uncertainty of the fitted curve is propagated through the Jacobian of the model derivatives with a diagonal weight matrix, which is what produces the approximate 95% confidence interval on every reported concentration. Detection limits follow the blank-based convention, LOD as the inverse curve evaluated at the blank mean plus three blank standard deviations and LOQ at ten, with documented fallbacks when every blank reads identically, and the usable range starting at whichever is higher, the LOD or the lowest standard, so that a sample can clear the LOD and still be reported as below the usable range. Exports are auditable: one CSV with every reading, every exclusion and its reason, and every result, plus the curve as a PNG, with a curve's own exclusions kept with the curve in its JSON backup. The mechanistic modelling matches this care, with two parameters fitted to swarming data and uncertainty assessed by 400 joint draws combining plate-level bootstrap resampling with uncertain model inputs and refitting each time (296 successful), reporting 5th to 95th percentile ranges, PRCC sensitivity indices, and the explicit statement that these are effective values and not confidence intervals for measured biochemical constants.

**dataviz.** Plan-view and cut-away optical diagrams drawn to scale with a stated pixel-to-millimetre ratio; an interactive exploded view of the instrument; counts-versus-condition plots that always show the emission channel beside the scatter channel; a calibration page in the app that renders the fitted curve as a PNG alongside the CSV export; a step bar at the top of every CAPTURE-Screen page showing the reader status, the number of calibration runs, how many produced a usable curve, and whether Measure is ready.

**software.** LasReader, a browser application with nothing to install, released under the MIT License with source on iGEM GitLab, carrying a research-use-only disclaimer that it reports concentrations inferred from a calibration curve and is not intended for diagnostic use. It works either with CAPTURE-Screen, where the instrument becomes part of the workflow, or with data from any plate reader through the same steps, and the analysis never uses the target's name so it transfers to other biosensors whose rising response suits a 4PL fit. The hardware is released as 53 STL files covering 66 pieces across both versions, with firmware that controls LED timing and integration, plus the laser-cut design, wiring and schematic.

**ihp.** A meet-with-experts programme fed the project's scope and its claims. Prof. Nan-Si Li's framing, that at this stage the project detects signals and does not diagnose infections, is quoted directly in the software's own disclaimer, so the limit on the claim is visible inside the tool rather than only on the wiki.
