Specific conversations changed specific decisions: Savannah Shumaker (chemist, co-founder and CEO of Eight Count Cosmetics) pushed branding toward audience values and simplified their science communication, and suggested contacting cosmetology schools, which led to Rachel Lu; Lindsay Menzer and Yun Yong Jang (L'Oreal Hair North America, Head of Hair Color Lab) flagged patenting during early testing, which launched the US patent-strategy investigation; the Boeke Lab at NYU Langone recommended storage conditions for chromoproteins, prompting a preservation study; and a question from another team at the Mid-Atlantic Meetup about pH and temperature sensitivity, which they had deprioritised, is what sent them to the Boeke Lab in the first place.

**publicEngagement.** Surveys were deliberately multilingual, translated into Chinese and Filipino to reach their own communities, and the results split cleanly by language and age in ways that changed the product thesis: younger English-speaking respondents wanted fashion blues, pinks and purples, which happens to be what their chromoproteins produce, while older Chinese and Filipino respondents wanted grey coverage and natural shades. They also found that the phrase 'genetically engineered' on a label worried more respondents than it attracted, with several linking it to harmful chemicals or illness, and responded by planning a consumer FAQ booklet distributed through partner salons instead of a call centre. They presented at the July 2026 Mid-Atlantic Meetup alongside eight other regional teams.

**realWorld.** This is a credible early-stage venture plan with the finance section still hollow. What is genuinely strong is the execution scaffolding. The OKR table is the best artefact: it sets falsifiable targets with costs and durations attached, including catalogue 15 salons statewide, a minimum of 10 qualitative interviews, at least 5 Letters of Intent, 10 investor pitches, 10,000 dollars from stakeholder investment plus research grants, cell viability above 70 percent in cytotoxicity assays, dye longevity of 40 wash cycles, protein stability at 50 degrees C, 1,000 sales per month and two new production labs in other mid-Atlantic states. Named funding targets are real and local (Wexford SciTech Venture Fund, TEDCO grants, Connect Labs at 4MLK as prospective lab space, youth competitions such as Blue Ocean, Paradigm and Slingshot). Crucially, every one of these is still an aspiration: the Letters of Intent are a key result, not a signed document; the grant is applied for, not won; there is no registered entity, though forming an LLC is floated inside the liability risk row. The regulatory path is the most concretely researched part of the whole analysis and is credible: they identify that the FDA Office of Cosmetics and Colors certifies coal-tar and synthetic colour additives but that a chromoprotein appears to fall into neither bucket, name 21 CFR parts 73 and 74 subpart C, name the Color Certifications Inquiry Branch as the body to ask, and note that certified and uncertified colours carry legally distinct names. The IP strategy is equally specific and actually actionable: a provisional patent on the aeblue-keratin fusion first, converted to a non-provisional within twelve months, with USPTO micro-entity status claimed for an 80 percent fee reduction, and they check their own eligibility against the 262,380 dollar gross-income threshold. Market sizing, by contrast, is the weakest link, resting on Grand View Research hair-colour market reports rather than any bottom-up estimate, with no price point, no cost of goods and no unit economics anywhere. Continuation is plausible rather than secured: they state plainly that as a high-school iGEM team they can never test on human hair, so KeraTINT must pursue third-party testing or operate independently of iGEM after the competition, and they sequence cytotoxicity, pH and thermal assays as the first post-Jamboree work. The precedent helps their case, since the same team's 2023 RhizeUp project went through the same incubator.

**For GEMS:** Steal the OKR table: every commercialisation objective gets a numeric key result, a business-day estimate and a fixed-cost line, including scientific gates such as cell viability above 70 percent and dye longevity of 40 wash cycles, so a business plan becomes a checklist a successor team can inherit. Also copy getting institutional IRB approval before running consumer surveys, which both protects participants and makes the resulting data citable.

### CHINAGuangdongShimen — Re-CDI Alert: an engineered EcN platform for monitoring and treating recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection
High School · China · https://2026.igem.wiki/chinaguangdongshimen/
Shimen built an Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) biosensor that detects p-cresol, the metabolite Clostridioides difficile produces to suppress competing gut microbes and secure its own niche, and couples detection to a therapeutic output targeting the TcdB toxin. Because recurrence after CDI treatment is diagnosed only once symptoms return, the aim is to shift from symptom-triggered diagnosis toward proactive risk sensing during the post-treatment window. The dry-lab contribution is the measurement protocol itself: a documented, reusable workflow for characterising a small-molecule biosensor, covering plate layout, normalisation, chassis comparison, tolerance limits, dose response and specificity against structural analogues.

**frameworks.** The measurement page is written as a contribution: seven numbered measurement strategies are stated up front, then each is given its own design, methods, results and discussion, with the standardisation framed explicitly as something future iGEM teams can reuse. Measurements are ordered so that each answers a prerequisite for the next, establishing the reporter, then the chassis, then the tolerance window, then the dose response, then specificity.

**datascience.** Three parts of this stand out for a high-school team. First, plate layout is treated as a source of error: three empty wells are left between each set of three replicate wells, because repeated experiments showed that when adjacent wells differed substantially in p-cresol concentration, the high-concentration wells affected the readings from the low-concentration wells. That is an optical and chemical cross-talk control most teams never run. Second, normalisation is written out as a formula rather than implied, with normalised fluorescence calculated as (sample fluorescence minus fluorescence background) divided by (sample OD600 minus medium OD600 blank), and the team specifies what each blank must be: the fluorescence background from a GFP-negative culture matched to the experimental conditions, and the OD600 blank from cell-free medium. The stated reason is that total fluorescence depends on cell abundance, so raw fluorescence cannot be compared across conditions and only a per-biomass value answers the question. Third, the viable measurement window is established before the dose response is interpreted: a tolerance assay incubating EcN at 0 to 20 mM p-cresol with OD600 read every two hours over 24 hours found no appreciable inhibition at 0.1 to 1 mM, inhibition emerging at 2 mM, strong inhibition at 5 to 10 mM and near-total inhibition at 20 mM, which produced the rule that induction experiments must stay at or below 1 mM so that growth inhibition cannot be mistaken for a sensor response. Only then is the full dose response run, across fifteen concentrations from 0 to 5 mM, locating a discernible rise at roughly 500 nM to 1 uM and a working range of 1 uM to 1 mM. Chassis comparison is measured rather than argued: BL21 and modified EcN (cryptic plasmids pMUT1 and pMUT2 removed and the flagellar regulators flhDC deleted to free cellular resources) are run side by side, and the team reports that OD600 stayed between about 0.77 and 0.89 in both strains with no decrease as concentration rose, which is what licenses the claim that the fluorescence rise is not a cell-number artefact. Specificity is tested against the structural analogues that would actually confound a gut measurement, with o-cresol, m-cresol and phenol all at the same 10 uM concentration, and all reading close to the uninduced control while only p-cresol rose. All fluorescence is read on a BioTek plate reader at 485 nm excitation and 528 nm emission in triplicate, with a no-p-cresol negative control throughout. The team notes a p-cresol stock preparation protocol down to the weighed mass and 0.22 um filtration, with light-protected aliquots stored at -20 C.

**dataviz.** Nine numbered measurement figures covering the chassis comparison, the tolerance assay, the concentration-response series and the specificity panel, each expandable on the wiki alongside the protocol that produced it.

**ihp.** Human Practices is reported in four stages with four named changes of direction. Conversations with a Chinese clinician reframed the opening question from whether CDI exists in China to whether patients are being identified in time, because the physician attributed low reported incidence partly to insufficient testing and clinical awareness rather than low disease occurrence. Interviews with two physicians abroad narrowed the target population from the general public to people with a confirmed CDI history who remain at high risk of recurrence. Interviews at Guangdong Hospital of Integrated Chinese and Western Medicine highlighted that antibiotic treatment itself further disturbs the gut microbiota, which moved the project from a standalone detection concept to coupling monitoring with targeted intervention. Advice from a microbiology researcher, Dr Peng, replaced a planned multivalent antibody with a single E3 monovalent nanobody against TcdB to improve experimental feasibility and reduce cost, and also informed the EcN chassis optimisation that improved protein expression.

**publicEngagement.** An education page and an inclusivity page accompany the project.

**realWorld.** The intended use is a monitoring platform for the post-treatment recurrence window in patients with a confirmed CDI history, chosen because recurrence occurs in 20 to 30% of patients after an initial episode and up to 60% after a second, and because diagnosis of recurrence usually waits for overt symptoms such as diarrhoea. Chassis selection is justified against three stated criteria: adaptation to the human intestinal environment, availability of established genetic tools, and biosafety with a history of clinical use. The project also states a biosafety framework as one of its outputs.

**For GEMS:** Run a tolerance curve before the dose-response curve. Establishing the concentration at which the chassis itself starts to suffer defines the window in which a reporter signal can honestly be attributed to sensing rather than to dying cells, and it costs one 24-hour plate.

### DKU — PeptiCraft
Undergrad · China · https://2026.igem.wiki/dku/
PeptiCraft addresses a specific physical problem: a free 10-30 residue bioactive peptide has essentially no structural stability, is degraded quickly by proteases, cannot be cast or gelled into a material, and diffuses away from where it is needed. The team's hypothesis is that such a peptide can be rescued by gene-fusing it to a structural scaffold, here a 364-residue recombinant Bombyx mori silk fibroin (FibLNT8-10xRep-FibHCT) chosen because its mechanical behaviour comes from sequence repeats rather than a folded globular core and therefore survives editing. The dry lab streamed 849,416,450 published protein sequences, kept the 19.9 million that are 3-30 standard residues, and ran them down an eight-round funnel to 496 assembled constructs across four functional directions, with a 99.9975% overall rejection rate. Three antioxidant candidates and a scaffold-only control were then expressed in E. coli and assayed: Top1 roughly doubled the scaffold's radical-scavenging capacity (TEAC 0.375 vs 0.195 mmol TE/g, p = 0.0075), no construct was cytotoxic to human keratinocytes, and no construct significantly protected cells against oxidative stress.

**frameworks.** A live, publicly accessible web application at https://pepticraft.pages.dev (Cloudflare Pages) serving 496 constructs over 19 endpoints, with a three-step workflow: define your needs (functions and product format), design the protein, review recommended expression strategies. The computational pipeline behind it is built as sixteen discrete predictive services, declared per stage and started on demand rather than run continuously, because keeping every service alive left a GPU context allocated per service until the card filled; in practice two to five live services at a time, which the team describes as removing contention rather than managing it. State lives in a columnar database rather than CSV hand-offs, with checkpoint and resume, progressive batch writes, and every result write as an upsert keyed on candidate identifier so batches can be re-run without duplicates and different rounds can write different columns of the same row. Batch size is explicitly chosen as the amount of work the team is willing to recompute, not as a performance parameter, on the stated assumption that a fourteen-hour pipeline will fail somewhere. Source: https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/dku/pepticraft-2, with a PeptiCraft-Project-Master-Reference.md in docs/.

**datascience.** The pipeline is governed by five explicitly stated principles that are the project's methodological contribution. (1) Hierarchical filtering, never cross-attribute averaging: each round either sorts and takes a percentile or applies a threshold and eliminates, on the grounds that a blend is only meaningful when components share a unit and a direction, which antioxidant activity and haemolysis risk do not. (2) Safety is a hard threshold: toxicity (ToxinPred3 at 0.38), haemolysis (HemoPI2 at 0.55) and MHC class I immunogenicity (MHCflurry at 0.50, tightened to 0.35 for wound dressing and injectable routes) are pass-or-eliminate, never scored, weighted or compensable, while MHC class II (NetMHCIIpan) is a soft signal and allergenicity (AlgPred2) and B-cell epitope (BepiPred-3.0) are reported only. (3) The functional activity score is used exactly once, in round 1, so the two channels stay independent. (4) The pipeline has exactly one weighted average and its weights come from the data, computed as each component's winsorised standard deviation (truncated at the 5th and 95th percentiles so one outlier cannot dominate) normalised to sum to one, with any manual coefficient invalid without a recorded justification, which is a rule against tuning weights after seeing which constructs won. (5) Order by cost: moving the toxicity predictor out of round 1 onto a 50,000-sequence subset took it from an estimated 22 hours to about 48 minutes with no effect on the result. The design feature that makes the whole thing falsifiable is a dual channel: a Bottom channel of candidates predicted to be poor is carried through the entire identical pipeline as a matched negative control (100 of the 250 constructs in the v1.4 run, 206 of the 496 on the platform), so if both channels behave the same at the bench the pipeline's central assumption is refuted. Round 8 re-predicted the top ten of each channel with a second, independent structure model: mean confidence 0.52 against 0.42 for the primary, same trend and same ordering at the top. The final structural score is published as a formula: 0.40 x SASA + 0.40 x (1 - Aggrescan3D) + 0.20 x normalised pLDDT, with confidence at half weight because a predicted structure is evidence about a construct, not the construct itself. Verification: 115 backend tests (113 pass, 2 skipped), 91 static-data-layer assertions, and 58 end-to-end walkthrough assertions, where the static walkthrough serves the export directory over HTTP, reads it with the frontend's own data layer, compares an interface-assembled sequence against the service's sample residue by residue, and fails if any read reaches the network. Data scale: a 367,717,240-row per-tool score table at roughly 130 GB, plus a second immunogenicity pathway of about 147.5M rows across 131 alleles.

**dataviz.** The platform's defining display is the safety panel, which resolves to four verdicts rather than three: clear, exceeded, borderline and not assessed, so that an unmeasured gate can never be read as a passed one. Of the 496 constructs, 198 carry no immunogenicity measurement from either pathway and say so. Where a value exists it is shown against its applicable range, because the MHC class I predictor accepts only 5-15 residue peptides and returns zero outside that window, so a stored zero is not evidence of low immunogenicity. Alongside the constructs the platform serves a hand-compiled reference layer: 8 scaffold protein clusters with 16 patent sequence variants carrying real amino-acid sequences and graded E1-E5 by evidence level, and 15 curated linker entries with literature provenance. Five application routes (injectable filler, wound dressing, mask patch, topical film, hair care) are ordered by barrier integrity and each binds its own immunogenicity threshold (0.35, 0.35, 0.50, 0.50, 0.60). Every number on a candidate is traceable to its source. The wiki itself publishes the funnel as a diagram with per-source pass rates and reports the round-by-round wall-clock times.

**software.** PeptiCraft is one of the very few 2026 iGEM software tools that is both live and candid about its own limits. Four things make it worth copying. First, the pipeline's own history is published as four versions with their failure modes, and the team says plainly that the version that succeeded was not a better implementation but a different arrangement of where each kind of judgement is allowed to happen. Version 1.1's hard filters removed 94% of an already-curated antioxidant peptide set on safety grounds alone. Version 1.2 ran end to end on 1,081,772 sequences in six and a half hours and its output exposed two composition errors found by inspecting the arithmetic of stored results rather than by any crash: safety attributes could be outvoted because small safety coefficients sat inside a weighted total alongside a strong activity term, and the antioxidant signal leaked past the channel split because the later ranking composite still carried an antioxidant term at the largest coefficient, which weakened the very comparison the dual channel existed to enable. A third error was found the same way: a construct-level composite assigned half the final weight turned out to have a spread of only 0.011 between its 25th and 75th percentiles across the top ninety, so at half weight it was ordering on noise, and it was removed. All three were fixed by changing the pipeline's structure rather than by adjusting coefficients. Second, every elimination is recorded with its cause, with discarded candidates written out rather than dropped along with the tool and score that removed them, which makes the funnel auditable after the fact and lets a rejection rate be stated per round. Third, the team re-evaluated the 18 predictive tools against their own library and reclassified what each can actually support: three can eliminate a candidate, two can rank, one ranks weakly. Fourth, the composition of the output is reported as a consequence rather than a choice: a 30-residue ceiling removes almost all of a full-length reference proteome (0.33% pass rate) and almost none of a metagenomic small-protein catalogue (3.07%), so 96.3% of the surviving pool is metagenomic and only 3.7% carries functional annotation, which the team notes means experimental evidence for these sequences is scarce and the output is a set of predictions. One planned reduction step was tested and abandoned and said so: clustering at 90% identity achieved only 0.2-5% reduction because short peptides are too diverse for identity clustering. The wet-lab comparison is reported with unusual statistical restraint: the developability composite's ordering of the three tested candidates matched the measured TEAC ordering exactly while the antioxidant predictor's ordering was nearly its reverse, and the team immediately points out that three candidates cannot support a rank-correlation statistic, that a chance match has probability one in six, that the composite scores span only 0.024, that adjacent TEAC differences are not individually significant, and that the agreement is therefore compatible with measurement error alone. They then state it as a hypothesis for future work rather than a finding: exposure may predict activity better than sequence score, because a peptide buried in the scaffold cannot reach what it reacts with.

**ihp.** Ten exchange activities produced six specific, named design changes, including the entire cell-based assay programme and the rule that an application's immunogenicity threshold is set by barrier integrity, which is why the five application routes each carry their own threshold. Scientific exchanges ran with XJTLU, Synbiopunk x CCiC, the VIT Gathering and the SJTU-Software AI x Synthetic Biology Roundtable; the industry exchange was a company visit to Changzhou Taimeirui Biotechnology, which brought production, cost and translation into focus. The team contributed to the JLU-NBBMS Dry Lab Summer Course and to a collaborative handbook, 'Together with iGEM: Across Villages, From Myths to Facts'. The most unusual feature is the human practices page itself, which answers four questions about PeptiCraft and refuses to overclaim on any of them: its current role is early-stage research support and commercial advantage remains unproven; early feedback exposed an unclear link between tool outputs and recommendations, which prompted clearer workflow displays, score explanations and missing-assessment labels, but independent user testing is still needed to establish whether people interpret recommendations correctly; the Top1 ABTS result does not establish ranking accuracy, cellular protection or lower research costs; and the page states outright that the effects of all this engagement on understanding and adoption remain unmeasured.

**publicEngagement.** Science publicity followed one stated principle: start with a familiar question, explain the science, connect it back to PeptiCraft, and close with a question that invites reflection. Twelve distinct topics were covered across four entry points (skincare and peptides 4, protein engineering 4, AI-assisted biology 3, safety and responsibility 1), published through Instagram and Rednote, moving from 'what are peptides in skincare' and 'why can combining beneficial ingredients still create problems' through linkers, silk fibroin and skin-barrier delivery to whether AI can design biology. Two campus events pushed past explanation into argument: 'Beyond ChatGPT', co-run with the DKU AI Club, walked from transformers to AlphaFold, ESM/ESMFold and generative protein design with PeptiCraft as the case study, deliberately using it to explain why protein design is hard and why experimental validation remains necessary; and a bioethics debate with the DKU Debate Society on the motion that AI-designed cosmetic bioengineering should not get a free pass. A 'Campus Voices' video interviewed students as prospective users about whether they would use AI-designed skincare and what would make them trust or distrust it, and the team reports the split answer (interest in discovery alongside demands for stronger evidence) while explicitly stating these individual perspectives should not be treated as conclusions about wider public attitudes.

**realWorld.** The market case is sourced: a US$450bn global beauty industry in 2025 projected to US$590bn by 2030 at about 5% annual growth (McKinsey State of Beauty), collagen raw materials at US$1.41bn growing 11.0% CAGR 2020-2023 with Chinese retail collagen products at RMB 58.42bn growing 41.9% CAGR, and peptides already appearing in 17% of 88 sensitive-skin facial cosmetics in a Portuguese pharmacy sample. The project restricts itself explicitly to topical and cosmetic-material use, functional skincare and dressing products where activity is delivered by a material that stays where it is applied, and states that nothing in the work concerns systemic delivery. Silk fibroin was chosen partly because it already has an established recombinant E. coli expression route in the literature, which the team says makes the wet lab tractable rather than speculative. The team's own list of what practical application would still require is specific: reproducible software, verified sequence-to-result links, suitable prediction models, user testing, and for product translation consistent production, storage and formulation studies, application-specific function and safety evidence, cost assessment, and a clear regulatory pathway.

**For GEMS:** Carry a deliberately unpromising control channel through the identical pipeline, so the screen's central assumption can be refuted at the bench rather than merely presented, and make safety a non-compensable veto that no activity score can outvote. Equally transferable is their reporting of a positive result: when the composite's ordering matched the measured ordering of three candidates, they computed that a chance match has probability one in six and labelled the agreement compatible with measurement error, then restated it as a hypothesis instead of a finding.

### GYHS — ReefBond: A Mussel-Inspired Bioadhesive for Coral Reef Restoration
High School · China · https://2026.igem.wiki/gyhs/
GYHS (Guangdong Guangya High School, Guangzhou) built ReefBond, a recombinant fusion protein that joins a mussel foot protein adhesion module (Mfp3-v12 / Mfp3-v15) to an acidic mineralization module (a CARP3-derived peptide, (Asp)8, (DE)6 or (DDE)4) so that surface adhesion and interfacial mineral deposition act at the same coral-substrate interface. Eight fusion designs were expressed in E. coli BL21(DE3) from pET21a; the team reports qualitative surface-retention staining, in vitro CaCO3 deposition with SEM imaging, and a purpose-built two-version underwater test tank with a motor-guided force gauge, five-level wave generator and a six-channel monitoring interface. The project is unusually honest: nearly every claim is paired with what has not yet been measured, and no live-coral test has been done. Human Practices is the spine of the project rather than a decoration - expert and practitioner advice visibly reorders the experimental programme.

**frameworks.** No computational modelling framework. The Model and Software template pages are essentially unfilled iGEM boilerplate; the dry-lab contribution is the instrumentation and data-recording software for the hardware platform, plus a literature-based mechanistic review (Venn 2011, Mass 2013, Cornwall 2021, Lange 2024, Gavriel 2018, Laipnik 2020) used in place of simulation.

**datascience.** Record discipline rather than analysis: readings and the manually selected wave level are written to CSV with timestamps, a channel is left blank after more than 6 s without a reading while a measured zero is kept as zero, and the team insists raw ADC and ppm values are not relabelled as lux/PAR or PSU without calibration. Planned work is to key sensor CSVs, photographs and mechanical test sheets to shared experiment and sample identifiers.

**dataviz.** ReefBond monitor renders live time-series charts for six channels (electrical conductivity, water temperature, total dissolved solids, salinity, pH and a raw light-sensor ADC value), a recent-image gallery and time-lapse playback; records are written about once per second and plots refresh about every two seconds.

**software.** ReefBond monitor - a browser-based acquisition and recording interface for the underwater test platform (device status, six environmental channels, scheduled photography at 5-86,400 s intervals, time-lapse, CSV export). Published at https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/gyhs/reefbondmonitor .

**ihp.** The causal chain is explicit and runs through five strands. A field visit to the Guangdong Marine Science Education Base with Professor Xie (Shenzhen Research Institute, Guangdong Ocean University) and the coral husbandry and restoration staff produced the first redirection: Xie explained that the facility's existing modified mortar already wins on cost and underwater handling but needs surface cleaning, and recommended testing underwater setting time, substrate differences, resistance to water movement and temperature stability - so the team replaced 'bond strength' with a seven-part requirement set (working and setting time, substrate compatibility, disturbance resistance, stable positioning, durability, cost, effects on coral and water quality) and adopted a staged validation pathway starting in ornamental reef aquaria rather than the sea. Yusong Shi, a Westlake University doctoral student and stony-coral hobbyist, turned handling into structure: his insistence on minimising handling disturbance produced the V2 fixed base, screw-in detachable holders and recessed model interfaces, and his suggestion of an ointment-style tube became the roughly 0.5 g single-use small-dose packaging concept. The sharpest change came from four experts converging against the team's own favourite module - Xie doubted their equipment could measure coral calcification rates, Shi recommended simpler mineralization work, Professor Baowei Chen (School of Marine Sciences, Sun Yat-sen University) told them not to interpret external deposition as stimulation of coral metabolism, and Professor Wang (South China University of Technology) prioritised adhesion because mineralization tests are more demanding; instead of dropping or defending the module, the team rewrote its research question to 'does a candidate mineralization module change in vitro deposition, and can that change measurably affect attachment performance?', reinterpreted mineralization as material-interface deposition and kept only comparative screening of the four acidic peptide classes. Professor Wang's point that microbes will use the protein and raise local oxygen demand added aeration, dissolved-oxygen and coral-microbiome questions to the assessment plan, while Professor Xu (College of Environmental and Resource Sciences, Zhejiang University) converted 'did mineral form?' into a method - indirect turbidity and TDS monitoring followed by SEM of endpoint samples - which is why TDS recording and a turbidity meter were added to V2. A peer, Student Chen of Guangdong Guangya High School with internship experience at a South China Sea coral facility, asked how long ReefBond would hold and what failure would mean, which pushed the team from a single tensile number to attachment service life, reapplication after failure and pollution burden. Professor Chen's separation of composition, dose, release, bioavailability and the distinction between functional aging and biodegradation became a six-dimension safety endpoint framework (composition and residues; exposure; degradation; water quality and microbes; deposit contact; organism selection), and the team then read Chinese Biosecurity Law Articles 35-38 and environmental-code Articles 95 and 737-738 against their own plan. They state clearly that no regulatory consultation has yet happened and no live coral has been tested - the honesty is itself part of the method.

**publicEngagement.** A school club exhibition with a Chinese-language 'SAVE CORAL REEF' poster, a knowledge quiz with small prizes and whiteboard questions introduced coral biology, reef ecology, threats and existing restoration methods before explaining ReefBond; students and teachers read the displays and talked with the team. Social media extended this, with post-level viewing records of 1,489 views for the iGEM introduction and 679 for the coral-themed post. The strongest element is a published set of six quiz questions and answers written specifically to kill misconceptions the team had encountered - corals are animals, bleaching is not death, an acidic module is a design hypothesis and not proof of increased coral calcification, engineered bacteria stay in the lab. The team states plainly that it has evidence of participation (photos, view counts) but not of learning, and sets out the paired anonymous pre/post records it will collect next.

**realWorld.** Need is framed with cited numbers rather than slogans: reefs are about 0.2% of the seafloor but support at least 25% of marine species, NOAA recorded bleaching-level heat stress over roughly 84.4% of global reef area in 2023-2025, and a review of historical restoration cases found 60-70% survival for common genera but a median restored area of only 100 m2 monitored for 12 months - which is why the team targets the early post-transplant attachment window rather than restoration as a whole. Four SDGs are claimed with named sub-targets and justification: 14.2 (attachment material for ecosystem restoration), 14.a (the open hardware, operating instructions and published software as marine research-capacity and knowledge transfer), 12.4 and 12.5 (composition, release, degradation and a proposed metric of material consumed per acceptable attachment over a defined period, including reapplication after failure), 9.5 and 9.4 (traceable development and testing capacity), and 11.4 (conservation practice and engagement); SDG 13 is explicitly held as indirect rather than counted. Deployment follows an evidence-gated pathway - laboratory production and functional testing, then functional and safety assessment in aquaria or nurseries, then carefully planned marine trials - with Xie's warning that cost could block large-scale restoration kept on the page. The regulatory path is named but unstarted: teachers and the partner institution will compile composition, residue, dose, release and site information for internal review before consulting local environmental, natural resources and fisheries authorities and the site manager about approvals, filings, organism sources, site use and monitoring. Cost is treated as full accounting - preparation and application losses, replacement, tool reuse, equipment cost, training and maintenance - and after the Jamboree the plan is calibration and repeatability testing of the platform, matched-control comparisons of fusion proteins against the adhesive component and commercial materials, staged safety assessment, aquarium user trials of dispensing and positioning, and returning the data to Professor Xie, Shi and Student Chen to ask whether their concerns were actually answered, recording the reasons for each decision including when results show no improvement.

**For GEMS:** Adopt GYHS's habit of letting stakeholders attack the module you are most attached to and then rewriting the research question instead of the conclusion: four experts doubted their mineralization story, so the team reinterpreted it as interfacial deposition and kept only a controlled comparative screen. Pair it with their discipline of printing, beside every result, the measurement that would be needed to make the claim and has not yet been made.

### HK-Joint-School — FlaminGone
High School · Hong Kong · https://2026.igem.wiki/hk-joint-school/
FlaminGone replaces halogenated chemical fire retardants with a self-assembling biological coating: E. coli's CsgA curli subunit forms an amyloid scaffold, fused to hydrophobic BslA for weatherproofing and polyethylene-binding peptides for substrate anchoring, in a two-layer system that sidesteps secretion limits and steric hindrance. Under fire testing the matrix forms a dense char shield that halts flame propagation and self-extinguishes, BslA prevents rain washout across weathering, and Arabidopsis assays indicated no ecotoxicity. To design the fusion peptides without waiting on crystal structures, the team built PyroForge, a publicly deployed web application that uses a frozen ESM-2 650M protein language model as a feature extractor under three lightweight custom-trained heads predicting melting temperature, folding free energy and per-mutation stability change, then scans every single-residue substitution and returns a ranked shortlist. For a high school team the engineering rigour is remarkable: a published S669 benchmark against 21 competing methods, Zenodo-archived weights and datasets with DOIs, 226-respondent user acceptance testing, and documented bugs that changed the model's reported accuracy.

**frameworks.** React + TypeScript + Vite + Mantine frontend over a FastAPI backend with Pydantic schema validation that rejects malformed inputs at the API boundary with HTTP 400 before they reach the queue. Celery with Redis splits work across three purpose-separated queues: 'fast' for sequence predictions and registry search using the resident ESM-2 (about 1 s), 'heavy' for GPU-bound mutation scanning and model training (minutes), and 'io' for network-bound ESMFold calls with waits up to 300 s, specifically so long network waits never occupy a GPU worker slot. Six Docker containers run on a GPU host via Docker Compose and a systemd unit, with only an Nginx reverse proxy exposed publicly and FastAPI, Redis and the workers isolated on the internal Docker network. Nginx also enforces the rate limiting, because the deployment is intentionally unauthenticated. The backend exposes five engines through a central registry (Prediction, Optimization, Visualization, Registry, Procurement) and rejects checkpoints whose normalization statistics do not match.

**datascience.** ESM-2 650M is frozen and used only to map sequences to 1,280-dimensional vectors, with three light heads on top: a PCA-100 to Ridge plus gradient boosting model for Tm trained on Meltome Atlas (4,000 training proteins, 1,106 held out, 5,106 total), an MLP [128, 1024, 128, 1024] for dG whose architecture came from a Hyperband neural architecture search, and an MLP [256, 256, 256] with dropout 0.324 for ddG trained on the Tsuboyama 2023 mega-scale dataset (494,370 rows across 449 parent proteins). The ddG head takes both the mutant embedding and the mutant-minus-wildtype difference embedding, which removes sequence-invariant features and sharpens within-protein ranking at the acknowledged cost of cross-protein absolute comparison. Internal validation is grouped cross-validation across 266 parent proteins: top-5 precision 73.6% genuinely stabilising against a 19.8% baseline, with per-protein precision reported as varying from 0% to 100% and roughly 20% of proteins scoring below 50%. External benchmarking on S669 (669 variants, 94 proteins, no prior tuning) places PyroForge 18th of 22 methods on pooled ranking but 2nd of 22 on within-protein ranking and 1st among sequence-only methods, with a +0.248 Spearman improvement over zero-shot ESM-2 (95% CI +0.051 to +0.502); the team explains that this split is exactly what their design choice predicts. Limitations are published rather than buried: Ssym shows only a non-statistically-significant trend, ranking quality drops sharply beyond 400 residues, and the Tm Pearson r of 0.810 is said to overstate performance because the distribution is bimodal between thermophiles and mesophiles, with weaker within-group ordering. Trusted regimes are tabulated (scanning and folding to 400 aa, dG and ddG trusted at 10-72 aa, Tm training window 20-400 aa) and out-of-bounds inputs return low-confidence flags rather than failing silently. Four engineering iterations are documented with their numbers: random row splits leaked protein identity and inflated correlation to 0.85, which grouped parent-protein splitting corrected to a realistic 0.46; training on forward mutations only gave inconsistent reverse predictions (r = 0.27), fixed to 0.95 by appending negated reverse mutations; expanding Tm training from 237 proteins to the Meltome Atlas cut held-out error to 5.9 degrees C; and a sign-inversion bug had the optimizer ranking the most destabilising mutations first, fixed and locked down with an end-to-end regression test. Unit tests encode thermodynamic invariants directly: ddG(wt to wt) = 0, ddG(A to B) = -ddG(B to A), batched scan consistency against single-pair prediction, complete parent-protein holdout with no split overlap, a sign floor so top-k never returns predicted-destabilising variants, and CAI normalisation within synonymous codon families.

**dataviz.** Seven workflow-ordered UI cards: sequence input (protein or DNA, with the longest ORF translated), composition descriptors, thermodynamic prediction with a plus/minus 95% confidence interval and a High/Low/Unavailable reliability flag keyed to sequence length relative to the training distribution, the ranked mutation shortlist, a browser 3D structure from ESMFold coloured by per-residue stability from the mutation scan, an iGEM Registry homology search that reports how many parts were searched and the snapshot build date so a zero-hit result stays interpretable, and codon optimisation reporting CAI and GC content with a hand-off to a DNA vendor. Long operations run asynchronously with the client polling every two seconds; fast ones return synchronously. History lives in browser local storage, managed from a sidebar, with large structure files stripped to fit quota, and an error boundary isolates individual card failures so one broken card does not take the page down. Benchmark results are published as figures: the S669 pooled-versus-within-protein comparison, the grouped cross-validation precision distribution, and the held-out scatter for all three heads.

**software.** PyroForge is live and needs no installation: https://pyroforge.26650078.xyz/, hosted on the team's own GPU server, with a QR code on the wiki and a three-step try-it path (New, paste the sample protein G B1 domain sequence, Run Prediction, Run Optimization). That makes it one of the few 2026 iGEM software tools a stranger can actually use in a browser. The problem it addresses is concrete: most established thermostability predictors need a solved 3D structure, which blocks work on newly designed or novel sequences with no PDB counterpart, so PyroForge is deliberately sequence-only and uses no structural data during prediction. The workflow is Input, Predict, Optimize, Fold, Order. Browser-only execution was explicitly ruled out with reasons given (ESM-2 650M needs about 2.5 GB of weights, a site-saturation scan is O(L x 20) sequential forward passes, and a 60-residue scan takes about a minute on a GPU using around 5.6 GB VRAM), which is why the architecture committed to a server backend with a job queue. Scope exclusions are equally explicit: no user accounts and no server-side storage, so analyses stay in the browser, and no live pricing, with synthesis quotes delegated to vendors. Four hard constraints shaped the design and are documented: ESM-2 and PyTorch are not fork-safe so the worker is single-slot and length caps, task timeouts and per-IP rate limits are enforced; Apple MPS produces near-constant ESM-2 embeddings that collapse predictions to the training mean, so serving hardware must match training hardware (and the team therefore refuses to publish its MPS-collected latency numbers as product figures); the deployment is unauthenticated on an open school GPU server so all security sits at the reverse proxy; and the folding service and iGEM Registry snapshot are separate services that report their status to the UI. Operational problems were solved rather than papered over: the public iGEM FASTA endpoint returned 403s, so the pipeline digests MySQL dumps directly and yields 22,294 clean protein parts; the archived ESM Atlas API returned 504s, so ESMFold was moved to a self-hosted instance on a second GPU with ESM Atlas kept only as an outage fallback. Reproducibility is unusually complete for iGEM: source under Apache 2.0 at https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/hk-joint-school/pyroforge, a full software document (user guide, API reference, deployment, provenance, known limits) and an engineering document as PDFs, and datasets and trained weights archived on Zenodo with DOIs (10.5281/zenodo.23455762 for the embedding archive and Meltome Tm file, 10.5281/zenodo.23456193 for the three model weights plus their evaluation reports), with ESM-2 and ESMFold weights deliberately not redistributed but loaded from their original releases at runtime, and a DATA.md documenting column definitions and what was actually verified. The tool was also used for its own project: PyroForge proposed mutations on an AI-designed fire-retardant peptide, and in a burnt-net assay the optimised Alp2 coating burned 8.5 cm (SD 0.4) against Alp1's 10.5 cm (SD 0.5), with more char formation. The team then adds the caveat themselves, noting that a different coating in the same project, CsgA-BslA-PEbp, burned less still at 7.1 cm, so the assay does not claim PyroForge beat every other design. Honest security posture: access control and TLS are listed as future work before exposure beyond the internal trusted network.

**ihp.** Stakeholders were grouped into three categories with distinct purposes: Target Users (public and industry, for safety, deployment, cost, liability and market acceptance), Science (subject experts, to validate the scientific basis), and ESG (regulators, testing bodies and environmental stakeholders, for sustainability and certification). The pivot is clearly recorded: the team started focused on improving fire retardancy and interviewed fire safety experts to build a verification plan, then consulted management at a major Hong Kong real estate developer (SHKP) who told them the critical problem with halogenated retardants is the toxic gases they release, including hydrogen chloride, hydrogen bromide and carcinogenic dioxins. The research focus shifted to making the coating non-toxic and low-smoke. An environmental analysis expert then reviewed the redesigned coating and shaped which metrics the verification plan should measure. For the software, the external benchmark exists because of one specific conversation: Prof. Joshua Ho of the School of Biomedical Sciences at the University of Hong Kong told them to run a head-to-head comparison with methods already in use, and the team ran S669 against 21 other methods and published the result including the places it ranks poorly. The 226-person UAT produced three documented fixes: ESMFold timeouts (resolved by moving folding to their own GPU), an optimization view that did not make sequence position and substitution coordinates readable (redesigned to highlight mutated positions and list the top five with residue numbers), and protein-only input (expanded to accept DNA).

**publicEngagement.** Education was built on a declared framework of one vision, four core philosophies and a set of user-specific strategies, with every initiative formatted for a particular age group and interest rather than reused, and each event documented with execution details, feedback analysis method and measured impact so other teams can reproduce it. The range extends unusually far down the age scale, including a Synthetic Biology Carnival at St. Dominic Anglo-Chinese Kindergarten built around sensory stimulation and mutual prosocial learning. The team's stated method is companionship and mutual engagement rather than monologue, and they publish a timeline and quantified impact per domain. The software itself was also engaged with the public: user acceptance testing surveyed 226 people through the complete analysis workflow.

**realWorld.** The problem framing is quantitative: 43% of all fire disasters occurred in the past decade according to a study in Science, and WHO projects extreme fire events increasing in frequency by up to 50% by the end of the century, with 2025 Los Angeles and San Diego fires causing 31 deaths, over 200,000 evacuations and more than 18,000 destroyed structures. The coating is positioned as a spray-on product for firefighters and communities whose non-negotiable requirement, set by stakeholders, is being low-smoke, non-toxic and biodegradable rather than merely effective. Arabidopsis assays were run to check ecotoxicity, BslA weatherproofing was tested across weathering for rain washout, and the team notes the platform extends to other industrial materials by swapping the binding domain. PyroForge's own industrial framing is thermostable enzymes that improve reaction efficiency and reduce cooling demand.

**For GEMS:** Run the head-to-head external benchmark and publish the ranks you lose on: PyroForge's S669 result (18th of 22 pooled, 2nd of 22 within-protein, 1st among sequence-only) is more convincing than a flattering number because the team explains why their architecture produces exactly that split. The second transferable practice is their bug ledger, where a random train/test split that inflated correlation from 0.46 to 0.85 and a sign-inversion that ranked the most destabilising mutations first are both published with the invariant unit tests now preventing them.

### ICJFLS — ORA-GUARD
High School · China · https://2026.igem.wiki/icjfls/
ICJFLS engineered Streptococcus salivarius K12, a GRAS oral probiotic, to express a Sox enzyme cluster plus an MTO enzyme that catalytically degrade the volatile sulfur compounds (H2S, methanethiol, dimethyl sulfide) responsible for bad breath, positioning it as a Live Biotherapeutic Product rather than a mouthwash. Plasmid expression was abandoned after stability tests showed near-total plasmid loss within five days without selection, so the cassettes were moved into the chromosome by CRISPR-Cas9, and a four-layer biosafety system (D-alanine auxotrophy via alr knockout, a PcspA RNA-thermometer suicide switch, no antibiotic resistance markers) was added in direct response to public fear of live GMO bacteria. The entrepreneurship case is numerically specific, with per-dose cost, retail price, gross margin and a named contract manufacturer. They were nominated for Best Entrepreneurship in the High School section.

**frameworks.** TAM-SAM-SOM with figures carried through to a revenue target, Business Model Canvas, three-tier business model (B2C subscription, B2B2C through dental clinics, technology licensing), cost structure and pricing with gross margin, a capability gap analysis, a 2026-2035 development roadmap, a risk register, and a comparative regulatory table for LBPs across the US, EU and China. Seven named appendices are listed, including a five-year financial projection model and a patent landscape and IP strategy.

**datascience.** A 745-response questionnaire analysed by age, gender and region, with roughly one third of respondents having experienced halitosis, and results segmented into pain points, safety concerns and information needs. In-vitro degradation efficiency in artificial saliva was benchmarked against purified enzymes. Plasmid-stability passaging produced the five-day loss figure that drove the architecture change.

**dataviz.** Twelve entrepreneurship figures plus six data tables: TAM/SAM/SOM breakdown, business model canvas, revenue projection chart, product-format panel, roadmap, capability-gap chart and the three-jurisdiction LBP regulatory comparison. Survey results are charted as public attitudes, concerns and information needs.

**ihp.** An explicit dialogue-reflection-iteration-redialogue loop with six documented stakeholder groups, and in each case the design consequence is named. Public fear turned a single safety mechanism into the four-layer defence system. Practising dentists and an oral microbiology researcher killed the original oral-capsule concept on the grounds that capsules have limited local effect in the mouth, which is what produced the mouthwash, lozenge, chewing gum and toothpaste format set and raised the priority on mucosal adhesion and colonisation. At CCIC, senior teams warned that gene editing in non-model organisms would be a bottleneck, so L. reuteri was adopted as a backup chassis, and they shared kill-switch leakage data that caused the team to drop a high-leakage design for the temperature-inducible one. A bioethics professor and a biosafety policy advisor are the reason plasmid expression was abandoned for CRISPR-Cas9 chromosomal integration and why genome-stability and animal toxicology studies were pre-planned.

**publicEngagement.** A 745-response online questionnaire spanning ages, genders and regions, surfacing the three questions the public actually asks about live engineered bacteria: will it get out of control in the body, will there be side effects, could it be transmitted to others. They then reported a finding most teams would bury, that patients care about what is in it for me and how it works rather than technical sophistication, and rewrote their communication from 'the technology is advanced' to 'it is safe and effective for you'. They also ran public education activities and attended CCIC, the Conference of China iGEMer Community.

**realWorld.** This is a genuine business case with real numbers, and it is the unit economics that separate it from the typical canvas exercise. They state a production cost of roughly RMB 0.5 per dose for freeze-dried bacterial powder plus RMB 0.3 for packaging and filling, totalling about RMB 0.8 per dose falling to RMB 0.3-0.5 at volume; retail pricing of RMB 199 for a 30-dose mouthwash bottle and RMB 159 for a 30-tablet box; and a resulting gross margin of 70-80 percent benchmarked against high-end probiotics. The SOM is built bottom-up rather than taken as a share of the TAM: 100,000 halitosis sufferers at an average RMB 200 per month giving roughly RMB 20 million (about USD 2.8 million) in year one or two, through Tmall, JD.com, Douyin and dental-clinic channels. Market research is partly real and partly desk work: the 745-response questionnaire and dentist interviews are theirs, while the USD 13.44 billion global halitosis market and the RMB 77.9 billion China oral-care figure come from Insight Partners, Frost and Sullivan and similar reports. The competitive analysis is specific and fair, naming BLIS Technologies' BLIS K12 and correctly observing that its deodorising mechanism is indirect because it works through salivaricin bacteriocins, whereas ORA-GUARD catalytically destroys the VSC molecules. The regulatory analysis is the strongest part and is genuinely credible: they identify that NMPA's 2020 biological-products registration classification treats LBPs as therapeutic biological products containing microorganisms, note honestly that neither NMPA nor the FDA has yet issued complete LBP-specific technical guidance, and draw the correct strategic conclusion that this is both policy risk and a chance to help set the standard, with early regulator engagement as the stated tactic. Partners are named rather than implied: Shandong Bona Technology Group for probiotic fermentation and freeze-drying, with industrialisation discussions already begun, and Shijia Doctor Dental Hospital as a clinical and channel partner. Be blunt about the gaps, though. There is no registered company, no incubator place, no grant and no investor commitment; investment partners are described only as a category ('biotechnology VCs and oral care industry funds'). The IP position is weaker than it first reads: the strain construction strategy and genetic circuits are said to form technical barriers that are 'planned to be protected through patent applications', so nothing is filed. The revenue projection figure is labelled as internal estimates, and the appendices (five-year financial model, patent landscape) are listed as titles rather than linked documents, so the deepest financial work is asserted rather than shown. Continuation is a licensing-and-partnering intent rather than a funded plan, and an LBP approval route of that length will outlast any student team unless the Bona relationship becomes a formal transfer.

**For GEMS:** Insist on three numbers before any market slide: cost per dose, price per unit and resulting gross margin, built from the actual process (freeze-drying plus fill-and-finish) rather than from a market-report percentage. And copy their SOM discipline, where the obtainable market is users times spend per user per month, not a fraction of a global TAM.

### Jilin-China — A DNA-based recorder of transient fermentation stress in Pichia pastoris
Undergrad · China · https://2026.igem.wiki/jilin-china/
Jilin-China built a two-channel genetic event recorder: pGTH1 drives Cre (recording glucose limitation) acting on a lox71/lox66 pair, and PsADH2 drives FLP (recording oxygen limitation) acting on an FRT-LE/FRT-RE pair, each inversion flipping a fluorescent reporter read after the run. Five separate models answer five design questions that experiments could not settle: which synonymous FLP sequence to synthesise, how bulk glucose maps to a promoter input, whether an alginate capsule isolates its cells from the broth, what DNA states the construct can occupy, and which published promoter evidence actually applies. The most striking feature is epistemic discipline: nearly every claim is accompanied by a statement of what the calculation does NOT establish, and when the glucose model's predicted low-glucose crossing time (7.56 h) disagreed with the measured 0.11 g/L at 8 h, the team reported the disagreement and downgraded the 0.05 g/L figure to a scenario threshold rather than a promoter activation threshold.

**frameworks.** Five models, each tied to a design action. (1) RecombiOpt — synonymous CDS design. It works in the real construct context (the 6,628 nt pET28a-FLP plasmid with a BL21(DE3) host profile), correctly identifies that translation starts at position 107 while FLP starts at 221 because of a 114 nt / 38 aa fusion tag, and computes accessibility as an opening free energy Delta_G_open = -RT ln P_unpaired for the contiguous 48 nt window [-24, +24) around the ACTUAL translation start using local RNA folding in ViennaRNA at 30 C with W = L = 210 nt. A greedy coordinate-descent local search over the first 10/15/30 FLP codons (max three rounds, methionine preserved) produced 'target5prime-30', which changed only 15 nt across 14 codons and cut opening energy from 10.6473 to 7.9007 kcal/mol while leaving CAI essentially flat (0.5184 to 0.5246), versus a constrained-maxCAI design that changed 352 nt to reach CAI 0.9948 but only reached 8.3520 kcal/mol. A complementary RNAstructure 6.6 analysis at 30 C compared MFE and mean single-base unpaired probability across the first 30, 90, 150 nt and full 1,272 nt CDS windows. (2) Glucose model — a coupled ODE of enzymatic glucose release, cellular uptake and OD growth. Sterile release was calibrated FIRST and separately in water and in YP medium (no parameter transfer between them) as a sum of first-order releasable pools dD_i/dt = -k_i D_i with r_h(t) = sum k_i D_i, giving the closed form G(t) = G_0 + sum A_i(1 - exp(-k_i t)); a one-pool model was retained unless adding a second pool cut fitting RMSE by more than 40%. Uptake and growth were then fitted jointly with shared parameters across conditions, with time and condition holdouts. (3) Capsule2Memory — a spherically symmetric reaction-diffusion PDE for an immobilisation bead, dG/dt = (D_eff/r^2) d/dr(r^2 dG/dr) - X q_max G/(K_m + G) with Monod uptake, solved under three distinct boundary regimes (prescribed surface concentration; a Robin condition D_eff dG/dr|_R = k_L[G_b - G(R,t)] for finite interfacial transfer; and a finite-bath case with instantaneous partitioning c_g(R,t) = K C_b(t) that solves bath and interior together including the sampling withdrawals). Four model variants are compared — M0 (follows input directly), M1 (diffusion only), M2 (diffusion plus uptake), M2-lumped (one uniform internal state with k_eff = 15 D_eff/R^2, where the factor 15 is derived from the steady-state mean deficit of a sphere with constant volumetric uptake) — and the page explicitly derives the exact volume-averaged balance and states why the lumped closure is an approximation, since Monod uptake is nonlinear so <G/(K_m+G)>_V is not G_bar/(K_m+G_bar). Numerics are a spherical-shell finite-volume discretisation with implicit BDF integration, solved separately across input discontinuities. (4) Recombistate — a discrete state machine over DNA sequences. The 16,098 bp final plasmid is annotated down to coordinates (lox71 at 4,767-4,800, lox66 at 6,050-6,083, FRT-LE at 6,272-6,305, FRT-RE at 7,784-7,817, with the reverse-strand FRT-RE reported in both genomic-forward and feature-oriented conventions), and the state graph is enumerated on an earlier 3,367 bp reporter fragment under specified Cre/lox and FLP/FRT rules, max two recombination steps, yielding four distinct DNA sequences, four transitions and five event histories. The key result is a negative one about observability: the two orderings of events A and B converge on the SAME final sequence, so the final DNA does not retain event order. (5) FermentPromoterBank — a promoter evidence registry (9 core constructs, 8 watchlist candidates, 252 discovery entries, 12 design entries) that keeps sequence boundaries, host and culture conditions in one record, explicitly described as not an activity predictor.

**datascience.** The machine-learning work is a model of restraint. They tested whether RNA structure features add information to expression proxy models by holding the ExtraTrees algorithm, base features and data splits fixed and only adding opening energy and local MFE, across three tasks (Boel expression levels, TIsigner detectable-expression labels, Nieuwkoop mRFP synonymous variants) with grouped five-fold validation and five random seeds — grouping by protein family for the first two and by experimental plate for the third, specifically to stop related samples appearing in both train and test. Gains were small but consistent: Boel QWK 0.1391 to 0.1677 (+0.0286 [0.0229, 0.0344]), TIsigner AP 0.8851 to 0.8997 (+0.0146), Nieuwkoop Spearman 0.7622 to 0.7906 (+0.0283), all five seeds positive — and they then note that even with RNA features the Boel QWK of ~0.168 means expression-level agreement 'remained limited', and that Boel and TIsigner share 2,363 protein-family components so positive results in both are not two independent replications. Crucially, they then DECLINED to use those models to rank their FLP candidates: an out-of-distribution protocol (MMseqs2 10-6d92c family search with predefined thresholds fident >= 0.30 and bidirectional coverage qcov, tcov >= 0.80, plus explicit feature distance, prediction disagreement and construct context) classified all 12 candidate-task combinations as OOD, so candidate selection was made on hard constraints (protein and vector invariance) plus a qualitative trade-off, with the team stating 'we did not add numerical weights after the fact' and that target5prime-30 'is not the unique optimum across every metric and window' since a five-window sensitivity analysis changed the ranking. Model selection followed predefined performance-and-complexity rules that retained simple linear models for two tasks and rejected frozen CodonBERT representations for lack of consistent gain. Wet-lab closure: FLP-Var (target5prime-30) gave a stronger anti-His Western signal than FLP-WT after 0.5 mM IPTG for 6 h and a higher OD600-normalised RFP recombination-reporter curve — reported as qualitative support only, with the team noting the two assays use different regulatory constructs, that OD600 normalisation does not equalise FLP amounts, and that no RNA-decay assay was run so the proposed hydrolysis-resistance mechanism remains a hypothesis. The glucose dataset is 138 concentration and OD600 records; six '<0.02 g/L' readings were retained as upper bounds rather than coerced to 0.02.

**dataviz.** Twenty-two numbered figures, and the captions are the most instructive part of them. Each caption states the axis meaning, the exact computational settings used, and what the figure may not be read as: 'connecting lines guide the eye and do not represent a time course'; 'the panels use different metrics and horizontal scales'; 'Error bars and asterisks are reproduced from the original figure. Replicate counts, the error measure and the statistical comparisons are unspecified, so we do not infer P values or statistical significance from these marks'; 'the graph is a structural calculation under the registered FRT rule; it is not a measurement of four fluorescence channels'. Figure 3 plots mean paired gains with 95% intervals from 5,000 group-bootstrap resamples, and the caption notes the intervals come from saved out-of-fold predictions and do not include full-retraining uncertainty. Figure 1 is a model-dependency diagram that distinguishes solid arrows (within-module workflows and documented design selections) from dashed arrows (conceptual interfaces that are NOT a validated coupled prediction) — a distinction almost no iGEM team draws. Figure 4 shows the three-way trade-off (CAI, opening energy, nucleotide edits) as separate aligned panels rather than a composite score. Figure 20 is a conditional DNA-state graph that visually separates sequence states from event histories, making the two converging paths to S_CF legible.

**software.** RecombiOpt is a released tool (v0.3.0 noted) with host profiles for E. coli BL21(DE3) and P. pastoris GS115, a conditional synonymous generator, a separate 'engineering repair' step that searches for synonymous fixes to declared rule violations and then re-runs all checks, protein and vector invariant verification, and retained tool versions and complete parameters alongside every analysis. The team is explicit that a current optimize run cannot reproduce the entire historical study, and that repair 'addresses whether a sequence meets engineering requirements; it does not predict expression'. The validation table lists, per module, exactly which checks were completed and what evidence supports them — analytical and numerical checks plus replay of a public transport subcase for Capsule2Memory, comparison against an independent solver for the bacterial parameter example, mass-balance and numerical-refinement checks for the tracer experiment, grouped internal validation and OOD checks for RecombiOpt, sterile-source calibration plus joint fitting plus time and condition holdouts for the glucose model, and DNA/junction/convergence checks for Recombistate.

**ihp.** The team built a named framework from the sociology-of-technology literature: a Social Shaping Loop of Encounter, Reflect, Respond, Rewrite, grounded in Argyris's distinction between single-loop learning (improving the existing method) and double-loop learning (questioning the assumptions behind it), layered on their own 5C Guidelines (Collect, Comprehend, Compromise, Continue) carried over from 2025, and framed by MacKenzie and Wajcman's The Social Shaping of Technology. They then applied the distinction honestly: single-loop work was adjusting recombinant expression conditions, codon optimisation, leakage-test conditions and hydrogel diffusion; the double loop was realising that a strong fluorescence signal does not establish industrial usefulness, and that the real questions are whether a recorded state accurately represents a relevant environmental event, whether the information stays interpretable after the event has passed, and whether the system works under representative fermentation conditions. Industrial engagement at BYHEALTH and vaccine and pharmaceutical production facilities surfaced stability, process compatibility, data interpretation and operational safety as criteria. Scientific exchange at the iGEM Northeast China Exchange and university visits fed directly into a modelling result: the Recombistate finding that different event sequences converge on the same final DNA state changed the design goal, pushing them toward a modular sensing-memory-readout toolkit while stating plainly that the toolkit is a direction rather than a validated set.

**publicEngagement.** A sustained programme rather than one-off events, organised under the 'Continue' step of their 5C Guidelines: the 5th Annual Community Day, the Apricot Blossom Festival, high-school and middle-school outreach, a Popular Science Series Course, a Summer Science Exploration Camp, senior-community outreach and a Sci-Tech Festival, reaching audiences across generations and educational backgrounds through lectures, hands-on activity and conversation. A promotion brochure is published as a downloadable PDF.

**realWorld.** The application target is industrial fermentation monitoring: a recorder that preserves information about transient stress events (glucose limitation, oxygen limitation) that a bulk probe reading cannot capture, read out after the run. Alginate-style encapsulation is part of the deployment concept, which is exactly why Capsule2Memory exists — the model shows that splitting one large bead into several of equal total biomass shortens the diffusion distance, but that insufficient interfacial exchange can still produce substantial error during a long low-glucose event, so size, cell loading and exchange capacity must be screened together rather than separately. The team repeatedly marks the boundary of the claim, noting that glucose trajectory, promoter response and DNA writing have not yet been measured in the same experiment.

**For GEMS:** Write every figure caption and every model claim with an explicit scope limit attached — what this calculation does not establish, which constructs and conditions it covers, which arrows in your diagram are validated and which are aspirational — and when a prediction disagrees with a measurement, publish the disagreement and demote the prediction rather than quietly dropping it. Jilin also shows the right way to use an off-the-shelf ML model: run a prespecified out-of-distribution check first, and if your target fails it, do not use the score.

### McMaster-Canada — Chariot: A Platform Technology for OMV-based Therapeutics
Undergrad · Canada · https://2026.igem.wiki/mcmaster-canada/
McMaster built Chariot, a platform that loads cargo into bacterial outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) using the VNp tagging system, so that accumulation of a VNp-fused protein forces membrane curvature and vesiculation under an inducible promoter. Having identified that OMV work is held back less by biology than by the absence of standard methods, the team made measurement the project: they characterised VNp-driven OMV generation, benchmarked four isolation methods against a shared filtrate reference, and wrote everything into an openly published Protocol Handbook. Alongside this sits Apollo and Artemis, an in-silico platform combining GFlowNet-based active learning for peptide design with molecular dynamics for VNp-cargo compatibility. The project was shaped by 40 stakeholder interviews run through a purpose-built OMVS framework.

**frameworks.** A declared 'dual measurement' policy: every conclusion must be supported by at least two independent measurement techniques, and every comparison must run against a control. Integrated Human Practices uses a bespoke OMVS framework (Observe, Modify, Vision, Synthesis) built on the UKRI AREA principles, with each letter mapped to a specific iGEM Human Practices judging question. Machine learning is framed as an explicit design-test-learn loop in which measurements become training data.

**datascience.** The measurement work is built around the idea that a single endpoint cannot be trusted. OMV preparations are characterised by dynamic light scattering (Z-average diameter and polydispersity index on a Zetasizer Nano ZS) and by nanoparticle tracking analysis (particle concentration), with the team noting explicitly that DLS readings and NTA runs are independent and not paired by row, and flagging a date discrepancy between the workbook label and the raw file timestamps rather than quietly fixing it. Total protein is quantified with a Pierce BCA assay against a BSA standard curve (R2 = 0.97), with blank-subtracted technical triplicates and the individual absorbance readings published; the resulting 709.2 ug/mL is reported alongside the caveat that BCA measures total protein and cannot distinguish lumenal cargo from membrane-associated or co-isolated protein. Comparisons between isolation methods are tested statistically rather than by eye: one-way ANOVA on log10-transformed values with Tukey post-hoc at alpha 0.05 for size and polydispersity across ultracentrifugation, centrifugal concentration, the Norgen kit, a novel 'Push-Pull' adaptation and 0.22 um filtration, all referenced to a single shared 0.45 um PES filtrate so no method gets a head start; lysis conditions are tested by one-way ANOVA with Dunnett's test against untreated OMVs; and the 4-hour versus 18-hour vesiculation comparison uses Welch's t-test on log10 values (p = 0.0005). SDS-PAGE is quantified by ImageJ densitometry, giving 41% recovery of total extracellular mNeonGreen through OMV isolation. Crucially the team kept and measured every fraction each method produced, including supernatants, flow-throughs and intermediate washes they were meant to discard, so losses can be attributed to a step. Limitations are stated as findings: the proteinase K protection assay that would distinguish genuine vesicle lysis from detergent micelle formation was not completed, so DLS size shifts remain the only lysis evidence; the 0.45 um filtrate was never run on NTA; and BCA reports preparation-level protein, not cargo. On the modelling side, Apollo is a generative flow network trained with trajectory balance and coupled to Bayesian optimisation: an ensemble of five independently initialised MLP regressors on padded one-hot peptide sequences acts as a proxy for a fixed D2-AlBERT oracle, with a UCB acquisition score converted into the GFN reward, and the released CLAMP/DBAASP dataset deduplicated and split by target identifier. The team is careful about what this does not establish, writing that negative labels do not represent experimentally demonstrated inactivity, that grouping by target does not separate closely related sequences, and that a falling training loss does not verify exact reward-proportional sampling.

**dataviz.** Interactive wiki charts with toggles for 'individual measurements', 'mean +/- SD', 'logarithmic scale' and 'show data', so a reader can switch between the summary and the underlying points; an interactive stakeholder network of 40 stakeholders across 37 nodes, colour-coded by category, where clicking a node jumps to its position on an engagement timeline; a conceptual platform-workflow animation for the Apollo/Artemis pipeline.

**software.** Apollo (GFlowNet + Bayesian optimisation peptide design, built on the published GFlowNet biological-sequence-design framework and the CLAMP/DBAASP dataset) and Artemis (molecular dynamics comparison of VNp-cargo pairings). A Protocol Handbook covering molecular cloning through OMV generation, isolation, lysis and analysis is published for reuse. Wiki source at gitlab.igem.org/2026/mcmaster-canada; site content licensed CC BY 4.0.

**ihp.** Forty stakeholders were consulted across five groups (patients, healthcare providers, regulatory experts, industry experts and biosafety experts), with sub-expertise in clinical infection, biofilms and pathogen biology, OMV and EV engineering, and drug delivery and nanomedicine. Each conversation is written up through the OMVS framework and tied to a project change; the stakeholder map records three kinds of link (referrals, sequences where a question raised in one meeting was answered in a later one, and convergences where two stakeholders who had never met reached the same conclusion), so a reader can trace a design decision back to the conversation that caused it. The first major pivot came from Dr Coombes, who raised uncontrolled inflammation and septic-like responses as unavoidable risks of systemic bacterial-derived therapeutics and cautioned that peanut-allergy mechanisms are not well enough understood for rational design; the team dropped its oncology and allergy concepts and moved to localised gut-associated systems, judging every subsequent concept on biological feasibility and patient safety before therapeutic potential.

**publicEngagement.** Education outputs include a SynBio Handbook and a zine series, classroom and community sessions with named educators, and outreach materials documented on the education page.

**realWorld.** The entrepreneurship case positions Chariot as a modular OMV loading platform for biotechnology and pharmaceutical partners developing protein-based therapeutics, with antimicrobial resistance as the first application because OMVs fuse with bacterial and mammalian membranes and can deliver non-membrane-disrupting antimicrobial peptides past the permeability barrier. The stated value proposition is improved cargo loading plus more consistent and scalable production. The team also frames its protocol standardisation as the deliverable most likely to outlive the competition, benchmarking itself against earlier OMV teams (Freiburg 2024, NYU Abu Dhabi 2025).

**For GEMS:** Keep and measure the fractions you were told to throw away. Benchmarking every isolation or purification method against one shared starting material, then analysing the supernatants, flow-throughs and washes as well as the eluates, turns a yield number into a map of where material is lost and at which step.

### Mingdao — Waste-to-Watt — bioethanol from plastic-coated paper containers
High School · Taiwan · https://2026.igem.wiki/mingdao/
Mingdao take used paper containers — coffee cups, lunch boxes, ramen bowls — and break their cellulose to glucose with an enzyme cocktail for fermentation to bioethanol. The obstacle is end-product inhibition: cellulase is inhibited by cellobiose and beta-glucosidase by glucose. Their answer is Simultaneous Saccharification and Fermentation, putting Zymomonas mobilis in the same vessel as a glucose sink so neither enzyme ever sees inhibitory product. Three models carry it: a Michaelis-Menten competitive-inhibition fit to their own pNPG assay data giving Km, Vmax and Ki for BglA at fermentation-compatible conditions; a Monod fit to their own Z. mobilis growth curves giving mu_max, Ks and biomass yield; and a coupled ODE in SciPy that feeds every one of those measured parameters into a closed-versus-open simulation of the real one-pot reactor. Every parameter in model three came from their own bench.

**frameworks.** Three models in strict dependency order, and the thing that makes this exemplary for a school team is that the third model contains no borrowed numbers — every parameter was measured by the students in models one and two. MODEL 1 is classical enzyme kinetics on BglA beta-glucosidase from Thermotoga maritima, cloned into pET-24a(+) and auto-induced in E. coli BL21(DE3) in Studier's ZYM-5052 medium. They deliberately characterised it at fermentation-compatible conditions (34 C, Bis-Tris pH ~6.4) rather than the enzyme's thermophilic optimum of 80-100 C, because those are the conditions Z. mobilis can survive. The pNPG assay was run as a two-dimensional matrix: three substrate concentrations (1, 2.5, 5 mM) crossed with a 1000-to-0 mM two-fold glucose dilution series, read kinetically at 405 nm over 30 min. Absorbance was converted to product with their own pNP standard curve (Abs405 = 4.0005 x [pNP, mM] + 0.0477, R2 = 0.9989, n = 3).
